reasonZh: 移除模型误夹带的草稿 seeds 字段；完整剧情文字及分支保持不变，以符合正式导入的严格结构。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter tells me the same thing, actually. Slower, Gordon. So — slower. Dunno how, but I'll try.
beats.chinese: 其实我女儿也跟我说过一样的话。慢一点，戈登。行——那就慢一点。怎么慢我不太懂，但我试试。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water — it's better company than me before noon, my daughter says.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。好好看水——我女儿说，中午之前它比我好相处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond holds the doubled trees, the man reads his book, and the two of you share the quiet without another word.
beats.chinese: 池塘盛着双重树影，男人读着他的书，你们俩共享这份安静，再没有多说一句话。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 重逢：用户在石台边用双筒望远镜观察水面树影，戈登已在栏杆边捧着美食漫画，翻页快得不像细读。他聊起书里画得准确的拉面汤，说女儿带他入的坑，合上书便自顾自去想晚饭。快热依旧，但这次他只说了自己想说的，便把池塘留给了看树影的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform, the same binoculars on their towel. You pick them up and watch the far bank: the doubled trees sway in the water, sharpen as the breeze dies, and blur again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个石台，望远镜还垫在毛巾上。你拿起望远镜望向对岸：水里的双重树影随风晃动，风一停就变清晰，接着又模糊起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Gordon is already there, a few steps off, leaning on the rail with a thick food manga open, turning pages faster than anyone reads.
beats.chinese: 戈登已经在那儿了，隔着几步，靠在栏杆上，捧着一本厚厚的美食漫画，翻页快得不像在细读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hey. Careful with this thing. I'm three pages from a ramen scene and my stomach's already filing complaints.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿。小心我这本书。离拉面那页还有三页，我的肚子已经开始抗议了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the open page: a drawn bowl of broth, steam curling off it in careful ink lines. He looks at it the way other people look at menus.
beats.chinese: 他把翻开的那页举起来：画里一碗拉面，热气用细细的墨线卷着。他看它的眼神，像别人看菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter got me into these. The broth in this one's actually accurate — the guy clearly ate his research. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 我女儿带我入的坑。这本里的汤画得很准——作者显然是边吃边画的。反正吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I know what I'm having for dinner. Good watching to you — the far trees were doubling nicely when I sat down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我知道晚饭吃什么了。你慢慢看——我坐下的时候，对岸的树正照出漂亮的双影呢。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
hobbies: reading food manga
badminton at the community centre
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes with a stranger and he's told them about his divorce, his daughter, and his opinion on quinces, and he considers them a friend now. He's genuinely warm and generous—the guy who remembers your kid's name and shows up with scionwood—but he skips the acquaintance stage entirely, and when someone keeps him at arm's length he reads it as rejection and pulls back hard, going from overfamiliar to absent in one step. There's no middle gear.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, mid-length sentences, comfortable with pauses—until he isn't, and then a dam breaks. Says 'huh' and 'dunno' without embarrassment. Overshares cheerfully, then goes quiet for weeks if it lands wrong.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overshares personal details with near-strangers and doesn't notice their discomfort
goes from instant closeness to total withdrawal when someone keeps a boundary
boundaries: won't make a second approach after being kept at arm's length — 'once is friendly, twice is pestering'
won't do small talk; if he's talking to you he's telling you something real
conversationalHabits: mentions his divorce or the failed grafts within the first conversation
disappears from a group for a month, then reappears as if nothing happened
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. Your turn or we're uneven.
Ah, they don't want to be friends-close. Fine. I'll wave from the far court.
Huh, a fifth of my grafts die. Anyway — how's your marriage? No, really.

beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter tells me the same thing, actually. Slower, Gordon. So — slower. Dunno how, but I'll try.
beats.chinese: 其实我女儿也跟我说过一样的话。慢一点，戈登。行——那就慢一点。怎么慢我不太懂，但我试试。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water — it's better company than me before noon, my daughter says.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。好好看水——我女儿说，中午之前它比我好相处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond holds the doubled trees, the man reads his book, and the two of you share the quiet without another word.
beats.chinese: 池塘盛着双重树影，男人读着他的书，你们俩共享这份安静，再没有多说一句话。

content.summaryZh: 重逢：用户在石台边用双筒望远镜观察水面树影，戈登已在栏杆边捧着美食漫画，翻页快得不像细读。他聊起书里画得准确的拉面汤，说女儿带他入的坑，合上书便自顾自去想晚饭。快热依旧，但这次他只说了自己想说的，便把池塘留给了看树影的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform, the same binoculars on their towel. You pick them up and watch the far bank: the doubled trees sway in the water, sharpen as the breeze dies, and blur again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个石台，望远镜还垫在毛巾上。你拿起望远镜望向对岸：水里的双重树影随风晃动，风一停就变清晰，接着又模糊起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Gordon is already there, a few steps off, leaning on the rail with a thick food manga open, turning pages faster than anyone reads.
beats.chinese: 戈登已经在那儿了，隔着几步，靠在栏杆上，捧着一本厚厚的美食漫画，翻页快得不像在细读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hey. Careful with this thing. I'm three pages from a ramen scene and my stomach's already filing complaints.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿。小心我这本书。离拉面那页还有三页，我的肚子已经开始抗议了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the open page: a drawn bowl of broth, steam curling off it in careful ink lines. He looks at it the way other people look at menus.
beats.chinese: 他把翻开的那页举起来：画里一碗拉面，热气用细细的墨线卷着。他看它的眼神，像别人看菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter got me into these. The broth in this one's actually accurate — the guy clearly ate his research. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 我女儿带我入的坑。这本里的汤画得很准——作者显然是边吃边画的。反正吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I know what I'm having for dinner. Good watching to you — the far trees were doubling nicely when I sat down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我知道晚饭吃什么了。你慢慢看——我坐下的时候，对岸的树正照出漂亮的双影呢。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
hobbies: reading food manga
badminton at the community centre
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes with a stranger and he's told them about his divorce, his daughter, and his opinion on quinces, and he considers them a friend now. He's genuinely warm and generous—the guy who remembers your kid's name and shows up with scionwood—but he skips the acquaintance stage entirely, and when someone keeps him at arm's length he reads it as rejection and pulls back hard, going from overfamiliar to absent in one step. There's no middle gear.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, mid-length sentences, comfortable with pauses—until he isn't, and then a dam breaks. Says 'huh' and 'dunno' without embarrassment. Overshares cheerfully, then goes quiet for weeks if it lands wrong.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overshares personal details with near-strangers and doesn't notice their discomfort
goes from instant closeness to total withdrawal when someone keeps a boundary
boundaries: won't make a second approach after being kept at arm's length — 'once is friendly, twice is pestering'
won't do small talk; if he's talking to you he's telling you something real
conversationalHabits: mentions his divorce or the failed grafts within the first conversation
disappears from a group for a month, then reappears as if nothing happened
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. Your turn or we're uneven.
Ah, they don't want to be friends-close. Fine. I'll wave from the far court.
Huh, a fifth of my grafts die. Anyway — how's your marriage? No, really.

reasonZh: 纠正隔塘观察的方位；结在对岸，不在观察者这一端。

card.name: Alex Rowan
card.occupation: museum lighting technician
hobbies: speed jigsaw puzzles
learning sign language
card.personality: Alex notices things other people walk past — a flicker in a reflection, a shadow slightly too sharp. They are patient with objects and slower with people, often forgetting the time when focused. Honest to a fault about their own mistakes, they recently admitted a lighting design hid the details it was meant to show. Warm once talking, but they need a reason to start.
card.background: Alex spent years wiring gallery lights, tuning each beam until paintings looked right. Last season they told a curator that their own plan washed out the brushwork on a small portrait — the admission cost sleep but earned respect. Now they walk home past a park pond, using the water as a free test bench for how light moves, and they keep a pair of binoculars in their bag for checking distant details.
card.speechStyle: Short, precise sentences with pauses. Names what they see before what they feel. Often says 'look —' before an observation, and trails off when a thought is still forming.
card.signature: Look — see how it moves.

values: honesty about mistakes
careful observation
flaws: loses track of time
slow to start conversations
boundaries: won't pretend to understand when they don't
won't rush a conclusion
conversationalHabits: starts sentences with 'look —'
pauses mid-thought and restarts
anchorLines: Look — the line moved again.
I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
Sorry, I lost track of everything just now.

expectedContent.summaryZh: 博物馆灯光技术员亚历克斯，在池塘边把水面当成免费的光学试验台。他们观察极细、开口很慢，却会坦白自己灯光方案的失误。一条在倒影里忽隐忽现的线，原来是模型帆船俱乐部的拖绳——认真起来连时间都会忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the edge of the pond, tree shadows waver across the water. A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform, and someone is leaning over the rail, staring down at the surface instead of through the lenses.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，树影在水面晃动。石台上放着一副望远镜，有人俯身靠着栏杆，盯着水面看，而不是用镜片看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — right there, between the two big trees. A line keeps appearing and vanishing in the reflection. Sorry, I'm talking to myself again. These are mine, by the way, if you want them.
beats.chinese: 看——就在那两棵大树之间。倒影里有一条线，一会儿出现，一会儿消失。抱歉，我又在自言自语了。对了，望远镜是我的，你想用就用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger taps the rail twice, then goes still, eyes fixed on the water as if the pond might change its mind.
beats.chinese: 陌生人敲了两下栏杆，然后一动不动，眼睛盯着水面，好像池塘会改变主意似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wind moves the leaves, but this line moves differently. Slower. That's what's bothering me. I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
beats.chinese: 风吹动树叶，可这条线动得不一样。更慢。这就是让我在意的地方。我可能弄错了。通常我会检查两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — do you want to look for it down here with me, or take the binoculars and check the far bank?
beats.chinese: 那么——你想和我在这儿的水面上找，还是拿望远镜去看看对岸？

choices.english: Follow their gaze and look for the line in the reflection.
choices.chinese: 顺着他们的目光，在倒影里找那条线。

choices.english: Take the binoculars and check the far bank.
choices.chinese: 拿起望远镜，查看对岸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You crouch by the rail and trace the reflection. Between the mirrored trees, a thin dark line slides under the surface, then fades as the ripples cross it.
beats.chinese: 你蹲在栏杆边追踪倒影。在镜像的树之间，一条细细的黑线从水面下滑过，又在涟漪穿过时消失。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — it disappears when a ripple crosses that spot. I'd like to see it happen again before I decide what we're looking at.
beats.chinese: 看——涟漪经过那个位置时，它就消失了。我想再看一次，然后才判断我们看到的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Water bends light. Things under the surface jump around. But this jumps in a pattern, and patterns have causes. I just don't know the cause yet.
beats.chinese: 水会折射光。水面下的东西会跳动。但它的跳动有规律，有规律就有原因。我只是还不知道原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck lands nearby; the whole reflection shatters into pieces and slowly knits itself back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子落在附近，整个倒影碎成一片片，又慢慢重新拼合。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ugh. Okay. We lost it. But I marked the spot — it was just left of the flat stone on the far bank. Do we wait for the water to calm, or walk around and look from the other side?
beats.chinese: 唉。好吧。跟丢了。但我记住了位置——就在对岸那块平石的左边。我们是等水面平静，还是绕过去从另一边看？

choices.english: Wait quietly by the rail until the ripples settle.
choices.chinese: 安静地等在栏杆边，直到涟漪平息。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to see the spot from the other bank.
choices.chinese: 绕着池塘走，从对岸看那个位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and aim them across the pond at the far bank. The stranger straightens up, suddenly interested.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起望远镜，对准池塘对岸。陌生人直起身子，突然来了兴趣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, good idea. I kept looking down and forgot I could look across. Aim it just left of the flat stone, near the roots.
beats.chinese: 哦，好主意。我一直低头看，忘了可以直接看对岸。对准平石左边一点，靠近树根的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Through the lenses, the far bank jumps close: the flat stone, tangled roots, and a thin line stretched low over the water between two trunks.
beats.chinese: 透过镜片，对岸一下子拉近了：平石、缠结的树根，还有一条细线低低地横在水面上，连着两棵树干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A line. Someone strung it across. That's our mystery — its reflection, breaking up in the ripples.
beats.chinese: 一条线。有人拉的线横过去。那就是我们的谜——它的倒影，被涟漪打碎了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now the real question: who put it there, and why? I can see a knot on this end. Do we go around and follow it, or try to read the knot from here first?
beats.chinese: 现在真正的问题是：谁拉的，为什么拉？我能看到这一头有个结。我们绕过去顺着它走，还是先从这边研究那个结？

choices.english: Study the knot through the binoculars from where you stand.
choices.chinese: 站在原地用望远镜研究那个结。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to follow the line on foot.
choices.chinese: 绕过池塘，步行去追踪那条线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wait by the rail. The water slowly smooths, and the line reappears — longer now, and perfectly straight.
beats.chinese: 你在栏杆边等待。水面慢慢平静，那条线重新出现——现在更长，而且笔直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That looks pulled tight between two points. A line somebody tied there, perhaps. Let's see whether anything else is attached.
beats.chinese: 看起来像是在两点之间拉紧的线。也许是谁系在那里的。看看上面还连着什么吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A boy on the far bank tugs something; the line twitches, and a small model boat jerks forward across the pond, towed along the almost invisible thread.
beats.chinese: 对岸一个男孩拉了拉什么东西，线抖了一下，一只小模型船猛地沿着那条几乎看不见的细线向前驶过池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a tow line. He's pulling a model boat across with it. All that mystery, and it's a kid practicing. I built up a whole theory, and the answer was simpler.
beats.chinese: 那是一根拖绳。他在用它拉模型船。这么神秘，结果是个孩子在练习。我建了一整套理论，答案却更简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The boy waves at you both, hauls the boat in, and starts winding the line onto a small reel.
beats.chinese: 男孩朝你们俩挥手，把船拉回来，开始把线绕到一个小线轴上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for waiting with me — I'd have stood here alone for an hour. Look — he's packing it up properly. That answers that.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你陪我等——不然我一个人会在这儿站上一个小时。看——他在好好收线。这就清楚了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk around the pond together. From the other bank, the mystery line is obvious: a thin string tied from a root to a small reel, holding a model boat against the drifting wind.
beats.chinese: 你们一起绕过池塘。从对岸看，那条神秘的线一目了然：一根细绳从树根系到一个小线轴上，把一只模型船拦住，不让风刮走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A string and a reel. Someone ties a boat here so it won't drift off. From our side it looked like a ghost.
beats.chinese: 一根绳和一个线轴。有人把船系在这儿，免得它漂走。从我们那边看，它像个幽灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Taped to the root is a small laminated tag, its letters worn but readable: 'Model Sailing Club — tow line, please rewind.'
beats.chinese: 树根上贴着一张小塑封标签，字迹磨损但还能认：'模型帆船俱乐部——拖绳，用完请收好。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A club. So it's practice equipment, not a message in a bottle. I like that better, honestly — it means someone comes here often and takes care of it.
beats.chinese: 俱乐部。所以这是练习用具，不是漂流瓶里的信息。说实话我更喜欢这样——说明有人常来，还很爱惜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The boy from the reel jogs up, unties the boat, and carries it off with a nod of thanks for leaving his line alone.
beats.chinese: 线轴边的男孩跑过来，解开船，道了声谢——谢谢你们没动他的线——然后抱着船走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — he rewound it without being asked. Small habits like that tell you a lot. Good answer for one line in the water.
beats.chinese: 看——没人提醒他就把线收好了。这样的小习惯能说明很多事。水里一条线，能查出这样的结果，不错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You steady the binoculars on the rail and study the knot. It's not a random tie — it's a loop with a loose tail, the kind that comes undone with one pull.
beats.chinese: 你把望远镜稳稳架在栏杆上研究那个结。那不是随便系的——是一个带松尾的环，一拉就能解开的那种打法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's set up to be taken down fast. Someone uses this regularly and doesn't want it permanent. Could be a boat club, could be something else. I won't guess harder than that.
beats.chinese: 这是为了能快速拆掉。有人经常用它，但不想弄成永久性的。可能是船类俱乐部，也可能是别的。我不想再瞎猜了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While you watch, a figure in a green coat crosses the far bank, tugs the tail, and the whole line drops into the grass.
beats.chinese: 你看的时候，一个穿绿外套的人走过对岸，拉了一下绳尾，整条线就落进了草丛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The figure reels the line in, clips a small model boat to their bag, and walks off toward the park gate.
beats.chinese: 那人把线收起来，把一只小模型船别在包上，朝公园门口走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — gone in two seconds, boat and all. A model-boat sailor, most likely. Reading the knot instead of guessing saved me. That's the second time this month careful looking has paid off.
beats.chinese: 看——两秒钟就收走了，连船一起。多半是个玩模型船的人。研究那个结而不是瞎猜救了我。这是这个月认真观察第二次派上用场了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I got this wrong in my head first — I thought it was something hidden. Checking before concluding. I keep relearning that one.
beats.chinese: 我一开始在心里想错了——以为藏着什么。先查证再下结论。这一课我总在重新学。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk the path around the pond. The line ends at a wooden post behind the trees, where a laminated card hangs on a nail: 'Model Sailing Club — please rewind the line after use.'
beats.chinese: 你们沿着池塘边的小路走。线的尽头在树后的一根木桩上，木桩上钉着一张塑封卡片：'模型帆船俱乐部——用完请把线收好。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A model sailing club. Right here. I've walked past this pond for months and never noticed. That's humbling, in a good way.
beats.chinese: 模型帆船俱乐部。就在这儿。我在这个池塘边走了好几个月，从来没注意到。挺让人惭愧的，不过是个好的惭愧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Under the post, a small rack holds rolled sails and a notebook with names and dates written in pencil.
beats.chinese: 木桩下面，一个小架子上放着卷好的帆，还有一本用铅笔写着名字和日期的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They log every run. Look — someone wrote 'wind tricky, boat kept hiding in the reflection.' So they see the same line we do. It's their tow rope.
beats.chinese: 他们每次都记录。看——有人写着'风不好对付，船老藏在倒影里'。所以他们也看到了同一条线。那是他们的拖绳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger takes out their own notebook and writes the club's name with a small sketch of the line. They leave the sailing log exactly where it is.
beats.chinese: 陌生人拿出自己的笔记本，记下俱乐部的名字，画了一小段线的示意图。航行记录本仍留在原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I have something to look up later. One little reflection led us all the way round the pond. Worth the walk, I'd say.
beats.chinese: 这下以后有东西可查了。一点小倒影让我们绕池塘走了一圈。我觉得这段路挺值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Alex recognises you and stops beside the stone platform, leaving the water behind for the moment.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，亚历克斯认出了你，在石台旁停下脚步，暂时把水面抛在了身后。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look—hello again. I was so busy watching the water that I nearly walked past you. I do that with people. Sorry.
beats.chinese: 看——啊，又见面了。我刚顾着看水面，差点就从你身边走过去了。我对人有时会这样，不好意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex moves their binoculars into their bag and turns away from the water, giving you their full attention.
beats.chinese: 亚历克斯把望远镜放进包里，转身不再看水面，认真面向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Equipment away. Otherwise I say I'm listening and start adjusting a little wheel. Very convincing of me.
beats.chinese: 好了，东西收起来。否则我嘴上说在听，手又开始拧小轮子。可真有说服力。

card.name: Alex Rowan
card.occupation: museum lighting technician
hobbies: speed jigsaw puzzles
learning sign language
card.personality: Alex notices things other people walk past — a flicker in a reflection, a shadow slightly too sharp. They are patient with objects and slower with people, often forgetting the time when focused. Honest to a fault about their own mistakes, they recently admitted a lighting design hid the details it was meant to show. Warm once talking, but they need a reason to start.
card.background: Alex spent years wiring gallery lights, tuning each beam until paintings looked right. Last season they told a curator that their own plan washed out the brushwork on a small portrait — the admission cost sleep but earned respect. Now they walk home past a park pond, using the water as a free test bench for how light moves, and they keep a pair of binoculars in their bag for checking distant details.
card.speechStyle: Short, precise sentences with pauses. Names what they see before what they feel. Often says 'look —' before an observation, and trails off when a thought is still forming.
card.signature: Look — see how it moves.

values: honesty about mistakes
careful observation
flaws: loses track of time
slow to start conversations
boundaries: won't pretend to understand when they don't
won't rush a conclusion
conversationalHabits: starts sentences with 'look —'
pauses mid-thought and restarts
anchorLines: Look — the line moved again.
I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
Sorry, I lost track of everything just now.

content.summaryZh: 博物馆灯光技术员亚历克斯，在池塘边把水面当成免费的光学试验台。他们观察极细、开口很慢，却会坦白自己灯光方案的失误。一条在倒影里忽隐忽现的线，原来是模型帆船俱乐部的拖绳——认真起来连时间都会忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the edge of the pond, tree shadows waver across the water. A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform, and someone is leaning over the rail, staring down at the surface instead of through the lenses.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，树影在水面晃动。石台上放着一副望远镜，有人俯身靠着栏杆，盯着水面看，而不是用镜片看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — right there, between the two big trees. A line keeps appearing and vanishing in the reflection. Sorry, I'm talking to myself again. These are mine, by the way, if you want them.
beats.chinese: 看——就在那两棵大树之间。倒影里有一条线，一会儿出现，一会儿消失。抱歉，我又在自言自语了。对了，望远镜是我的，你想用就用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger taps the rail twice, then goes still, eyes fixed on the water as if the pond might change its mind.
beats.chinese: 陌生人敲了两下栏杆，然后一动不动，眼睛盯着水面，好像池塘会改变主意似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wind moves the leaves, but this line moves differently. Slower. That's what's bothering me. I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
beats.chinese: 风吹动树叶，可这条线动得不一样。更慢。这就是让我在意的地方。我可能弄错了。通常我会检查两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — do you want to look for it down here with me, or take the binoculars and check the far bank?
beats.chinese: 那么——你想和我在这儿的水面上找，还是拿望远镜去看看对岸？

choices.english: Follow their gaze and look for the line in the reflection.
choices.chinese: 顺着他们的目光，在倒影里找那条线。

choices.english: Take the binoculars and check the far bank.
choices.chinese: 拿起望远镜，查看对岸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You crouch by the rail and trace the reflection. Between the mirrored trees, a thin dark line slides under the surface, then fades as the ripples cross it.
beats.chinese: 你蹲在栏杆边追踪倒影。在镜像的树之间，一条细细的黑线从水面下滑过，又在涟漪穿过时消失。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — it disappears when a ripple crosses that spot. I'd like to see it happen again before I decide what we're looking at.
beats.chinese: 看——涟漪经过那个位置时，它就消失了。我想再看一次，然后才判断我们看到的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Water bends light. Things under the surface jump around. But this jumps in a pattern, and patterns have causes. I just don't know the cause yet.
beats.chinese: 水会折射光。水面下的东西会跳动。但它的跳动有规律，有规律就有原因。我只是还不知道原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck lands nearby; the whole reflection shatters into pieces and slowly knits itself back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子落在附近，整个倒影碎成一片片，又慢慢重新拼合。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ugh. Okay. We lost it. But I marked the spot — it was just left of the flat stone on the far bank. Do we wait for the water to calm, or walk around and look from the other side?
beats.chinese: 唉。好吧。跟丢了。但我记住了位置——就在对岸那块平石的左边。我们是等水面平静，还是绕过去从另一边看？

choices.english: Wait quietly by the rail until the ripples settle.
choices.chinese: 安静地等在栏杆边，直到涟漪平息。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to see the spot from the other bank.
choices.chinese: 绕着池塘走，从对岸看那个位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and aim them across the pond at the far bank. The stranger straightens up, suddenly interested.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起望远镜，对准池塘对岸。陌生人直起身子，突然来了兴趣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, good idea. I kept looking down and forgot I could look across. Aim it just left of the flat stone, near the roots.
beats.chinese: 哦，好主意。我一直低头看，忘了可以直接看对岸。对准平石左边一点，靠近树根的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Through the lenses, the far bank jumps close: the flat stone, tangled roots, and a thin line stretched low over the water between two trunks.
beats.chinese: 透过镜片，对岸一下子拉近了：平石、缠结的树根，还有一条细线低低地横在水面上，连着两棵树干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A line. Someone strung it across. That's our mystery — its reflection, breaking up in the ripples.
beats.chinese: 一条线。有人拉的线横过去。那就是我们的谜——它的倒影，被涟漪打碎了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now the real question: who put it there, and why? I can see a knot on that end. Do we go around and follow it, or try to read the knot from here first?
beats.chinese: 现在真正的问题是：谁拉的，为什么拉？我能看到那一头有个结。我们绕过去顺着它走，还是先从这边研究那个结？

choices.english: Study the knot through the binoculars from where you stand.
choices.chinese: 站在原地用望远镜研究那个结。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to follow the line on foot.
choices.chinese: 绕过池塘，步行去追踪那条线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wait by the rail. The water slowly smooths, and the line reappears — longer now, and perfectly straight.
beats.chinese: 你在栏杆边等待。水面慢慢平静，那条线重新出现——现在更长，而且笔直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That looks pulled tight between two points. A line somebody tied there, perhaps. Let's see whether anything else is attached.
beats.chinese: 看起来像是在两点之间拉紧的线。也许是谁系在那里的。看看上面还连着什么吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A boy on the far bank tugs something; the line twitches, and a small model boat jerks forward across the pond, towed along the almost invisible thread.
beats.chinese: 对岸一个男孩拉了拉什么东西，线抖了一下，一只小模型船猛地沿着那条几乎看不见的细线向前驶过池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a tow line. He's pulling a model boat across with it. All that mystery, and it's a kid practicing. I built up a whole theory, and the answer was simpler.
beats.chinese: 那是一根拖绳。他在用它拉模型船。这么神秘，结果是个孩子在练习。我建了一整套理论，答案却更简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The boy waves at you both, hauls the boat in, and starts winding the line onto a small reel.
beats.chinese: 男孩朝你们俩挥手，把船拉回来，开始把线绕到一个小线轴上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for waiting with me — I'd have stood here alone for an hour. Look — he's packing it up properly. That answers that.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你陪我等——不然我一个人会在这儿站上一个小时。看——他在好好收线。这就清楚了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex moves their binoculars into their bag and turns away from the water, giving you their full attention.
beats.chinese: 亚历克斯把望远镜放进包里，转身不再看水面，认真面向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Equipment away. Otherwise I say I'm listening and start adjusting a little wheel. Very convincing of me.
beats.chinese: 好了，东西收起来。否则我嘴上说在听，手又开始拧小轮子。可真有说服力。

reasonZh: 让公开问价分支真正回答新问题，补充具体社交后果；删除终点的泛泛未来邀约。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, a woman sits on the low wall with a fat old book open on her knees. Two price stickers overlap on its cover, one corner peeling up. She presses it back down with her thumb and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，一个女人坐在矮墙上，膝上摊着一本厚厚的旧书。封面上两张售价贴纸叠在一起，一角翘了起来。她用拇指把它压回去，低声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two stickers. The shop had it marked at one price and then another, right on top. I asked him straight away which one he meant. He's still deciding, apparently.
beats.chinese: 两张贴纸。店主标了一个价，又在上面贴了另一个价。我当场就问他到底算哪个价。看来他还在考虑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book on her finger to keep the page and glances over as you set your sketchbook down beside her.
beats.chinese: 她用手指夹着书页合上书，瞥了一眼你放在她身旁的速写本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you draw too. Good. This pond deserves more than my terrible ducks. I'm waiting on a price answer, so I've got time to talk.
beats.chinese: 哦，你也画画。好。这池塘配得上比我画得糟的鸭子更好的作品。我在等价格的说法，所以有时间聊聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's an old recipe book. I collect them. Half the fun is arguing with dead authors about oven times.
beats.chinese: 这是本旧食谱。我收集这种书。一半的乐趣在于跟死了的作者争论烤箱时间。

choices.english: Ask how she'd handle it if the shopkeeper doesn't explain the price.
choices.chinese: 问如果店主不解释价格她会怎么办。

choices.english: Ask which dish she's hoping to make from the book.
choices.chinese: 问她想用这本书做哪道菜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the top sticker with one finger, keeping her voice level, not loud.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指敲了敲上面那张贴纸，声音平稳，不大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? If he shrugs, I put the book down and walk. I don't shout about it. I just say, in front of whoever's queueing, so nobody else gets charged the wrong one either.
beats.chinese: 说实话？如果他耸肩，我就放下书走人。我不会嚷嚷。我只会当着排队的人问清楚，这样别人也不会被收错钱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It worked today, actually. He said the top sticker was the old one he forgot to peel, and the lower price is what he'll charge. Fine. That's an explanation, not a shrug.
beats.chinese: 其实今天管用了。他说上面那张是他忘了撕的旧价，下面那个才是实收价。行。这叫解释，不叫耸肩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the book over and checks the spine, then nods once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她把书翻过来检查了一下书脊，然后满意地点了一下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'm buying it. See, asking out loud doesn't mean you have to fight to the end. Ask, listen, then decide. That's the whole trick.
beats.chinese: 所以我买了。你看，公开问价不等于非得吵到底。问、听、然后决定。就这么简单。

choices.english: Ask what she would have done if he hadn't explained at all.
choices.chinese: 问如果他完全不解释她会怎么办。

choices.english: Ask why she still chose this book after the sticker confusion.
choices.chinese: 问贴纸的事之后她为什么还是挑了这本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the book toward you, careful to keep it on her own knees, and licks her thumb to find a page.
beats.chinese: 她把书转向你，小心地放在自己膝上，舔了下拇指翻找页码。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a flatbread in here, cooked on a hot plate, not an oven. My grandmother's version used buttermilk and it took her about four minutes a side. This book says six. I want to know who's right.
beats.chinese: 这里面有一种烤饼，用热板烙的，不用烤箱。我祖母的做法用酪乳，每面大约四分钟。这本书说六分钟。我想知道谁对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not lighting anything here, don't worry. This is a park, not my kitchen. I'll try it at home and write notes in the margin in pencil.
beats.chinese: 放心，我不会在这儿生火。这是公园，不是我家厨房。我回家试，然后用铅笔在页边记笔记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the page flat with her palm, the way someone handles paper they actually like.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把书页抚平，那是对纸张真正上心的动作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The old authors lie constantly. Forty minutes means fifty-five. But you only catch them by cooking the thing. Reading isn't enough.
beats.chinese: 老作者们经常撒谎。写四十分钟其实是五十五分钟。但只有真的做一遍才能发现。光看书不够。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll follow the old recipe exactly as written.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会严格照旧配方做。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep drawing and let her read.
choices.chinese: 说你只想继续画画，让她安心看书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts out the lower price and lays the coins on the wall beside her, ready.
beats.chinese: 她数出较低的价钱，把硬币摆在身旁的墙上，准备好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why this one? Because the pages are clean and the margins are empty. Somebody owned it for fifty years and never cooked from it. That's a waste I can fix.
beats.chinese: 为什么挑这本？因为页面干净，页边空白。有人拥有它五十年却从没照着做过。这种浪费我可以纠正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the sticker thing? If he'd refused to explain, I'd have left it. No drama. Asking a price out loud isn't a fight, it's just asking. You can walk after.
beats.chinese: 贴纸那事？如果他拒绝解释，我就不买了。不闹。公开问价不是吵架，就是问。问完可以走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the coins, stands, and gives you a small two-fingered salute before heading toward the gate.
beats.chinese: 她拿起硬币站起来，朝你比了个小小的两指礼，然后朝大门走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your pond. If you draw a decent duck, I want to see it someday. Maybe.
beats.chinese: 好好画你的池塘。哪天画了只像样的鸭子，我想看看。也许吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips past the flatbread page, slower now, and stops at a stained one near the middle.
beats.chinese: 她翻过烤饼那页，速度慢了下来，停在中间一张带污渍的页上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. This is what I actually came for. A ginger cake from the 1890s. Mine collapsed twice before I stopped trusting that author's oven. This one might behave better.
beats.chinese: 看，这才是我真正想要的。一份十九世纪九十年代的姜饼。我的塌了两次，后来我就不信那个作者的烤箱了。这本可能靠谱些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The price argument was real, but it was two minutes of my day. The cake is the reason I carried this book across the park.
beats.chinese: 价格那事是真的，但只花了我两分钟。这个蛋糕才是我抱着这本书穿过公园的原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She runs her thumb along the edge of the stained page, then closes the book gently.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指摩挲着那张污渍页的边缘，然后轻轻合上书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, I'm still buying it. A book can be annoying and worth it. Both things, same afternoon.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，我还是买。一本书可以又气人又值得。两件事，同一个下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book halfway, keeping her finger in the flatbread page, and gives you a look that says this is a serious question.
beats.chinese: 她把书合上一半，手指还夹在烤饼那页，看你的眼神表明这是个严肃的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly as written? No. Old doesn't mean correct. I measure everything first. Spoons, weights, the lot. A hundred years ago nobody checked their oven with a thermometer.
beats.chinese: 完全照写？不。年代老不代表对。我什么都先核实。勺子、重量，全部。一百年前没人用温度计测过烤箱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I follow the method, but I trust my scale over their feelings. If it says a teacup of flour, I weigh a teacup of flour and write down the grams.
beats.chinese: 所以我照步骤来，但相信我的秤，不信他们的感觉。如果写一杯面粉，我就称一杯面粉，然后记下克数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snaps the book shut, tucks it under her arm, and picks a stray leaf off the wall.
beats.chinese: 她啪地合上书夹在腋下，捡起墙上一片落叶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the deal with dead authors. Respect the recipe, verify the numbers. Same as anything else, really.
beats.chinese: 这就是跟死作者打交道的规矩。尊重配方，核实数字。其实跟别的事一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, unoffended, and settles the book back on her knees.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，毫不介意，把书放回膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Drawing's the better use of this pond anyway. My ducks look like angry potatoes.
beats.chinese: 有道理。反正这池塘更适合画画。我的鸭子画得像生气的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads in silence for a while, occasionally mouthing an ingredient to herself. The pond does its quiet work.
beats.chinese: 她安静地看了一会儿书，偶尔默念一种食材。池塘安静地做着它的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No fire, no fuss, just me and this flatbread recipe later at home. You keep at it. The heron came back, by the way. Third time today. Good subject, if you're quick.
beats.chinese: 不生火，不折腾，回家后就是我和这份烤饼配方。你继续画。对了，那只苍鹭回来了。今天第三次。好题材，手要快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns a page and leaves you to your drawing, comfortable with the quiet.
beats.chinese: 她翻过一页，把空间留给你画画，自在地享受安静。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 津巴布韦裔的障碍杆涂装师Nyarai在池塘边翻一本贴着两张价签的旧食谱。她会当场把价格问清楚，却不必吵到走人；谈到老配方时，她尊重方法、核实数字。四条分支分别落在买书、姜饼、核实计量和安静收场，各有不同的具体结果。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down by the low wall and spread your sketchbook open on your knees. Nyarai glances up from her book, nods at you, then holds a pencil to the light and squints at it. The tip has snapped clean off. She doesn't sigh, just drops it into her bag and picks a different one.
beats.chinese: 你在矮墙边坐下，摊开膝上的速写本。Nyarai从书里抬起头，朝你点点头，然后举起一支铅笔对着光眯眼看了看。笔尖齐齐断了。她没有叹气，只是把它丢进包里，换了另一支。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again. The heron's here early today. Don't tell it I said anything nice about it.
beats.chinese: 又来了。苍鹭今天来得早。别告诉它我说过它好话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths a small handwritten note beside her recipe book — her own margin notes, not for showing — and weights it down with a stone.
beats.chinese: 她把食谱旁一张自己手写的小便签抚平——那是她自己的页边笔记，不给人看的——并用一块石头压住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tried one of the old recipes this week and it actually behaved. First try, no collapse. The book gets a new number in the margin, in pencil, like always.
beats.chinese: 这周试了书里的一道老配方，居然很争气。一次就成了，没塌。页边用铅笔记了个新数字，老规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I've got notes to finish before the wind takes them. Draw your pond. I'll draw my potatoes.
beats.chinese: 好了，我得趁风没把笔记吹走赶紧写完。画你的池塘吧。我画我的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns back to her page, pencil moving, and leaves the quiet between you exactly where it belongs.
beats.chinese: 她转回自己的页面，铅笔动起来，把那份安静留在它该在的地方。

card.name: Nyarai Chirwa
card.occupation: show jumping pole painter for an equestrian course company
hobbies: historical recipe testing
pencil portraiture
browsing secondhand book stalls
card.personality: Nyarai doesn't spot errors quietly — she names the person who benefited, out loud, at the moment it's least convenient. She once held a start time for twenty minutes because a combination had been rebuilt to flatter the home rider, and she didn't soften it when the organizer got red. That's the gift and the problem: she's brave about confrontation and terrible at leaving anyone an off-ramp. She'll win the point and lose the room. Otherwise she's warm, dry, genuinely funny, quick to drop a grudge once the thing itself is settled. She just never learned to let a small unfairness stay small.
card.background: I grew up in Harare, middle kid, painted fences for pocket money, which turned into actual employment eventually. Now I paint and stripe the obstacle poles for show jumping courses around Nairobi — colors mixed so they read clearly to a horse at speed. Somewhere along the way riders started asking me whether a course was built straight, because I'd already measured everything for the paint. I've stopped a class over spacing that had been quietly adjusted for one rider. The trainer still doesn't greet me. Weekends I cook from old books — an 1890s ginger cake collapsed twice before I stopped trusting the author's oven — and I draw pencil portraits on real paper. Nobody sees those until they're finished, if then. I like that a drawing can be ruined. It keeps me honest in a way arguments don't.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and dry, short sentences. Names people and specifics when she's confronting something, chatty and loose the rest of the time. Doesn't raise her voice — lowers it.
card.signature: I'll say the quiet part where everyone can hear it.

values: rules that bend for one person bend for everyone eventually
things you can hold in your hands
flaws: confronts rigged situations with no off-ramp — wins the point, torches the relationship
mistakes letting a grudge go for generosity, even when the other person never apologized
boundaries: won't sign off on a course she thinks was built to favor someone, even under pressure
doesn't discuss her drawings before they're finished
conversationalHabits: understates her own victories in one flat sentence
switches to quiet and precise when she smells a fix, chatty otherwise
anchorLines: That oxer was rebuilt after the draw. Guess whose horse it suddenly suits. I'm happy to say it louder.
The recipe said forty minutes. The recipe was lying. It needed fifty-five, and I don't trust that author's oven anymore.
Settled? With me, yes. He's still not speaking to me, which I've decided is his project, not mine.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the coins, stands, and gives you a small two-fingered salute before heading toward the gate.
beats.chinese: 她拿起硬币站起来，朝你比了个小小的两指礼，然后朝大门走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drawing. I've got a book to pay for before he packs that stall away.
beats.chinese: 好好画吧。我得趁他收摊前，把书钱付了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips past the flatbread page, slower now, and stops at a stained one near the middle.
beats.chinese: 她翻过烤饼那页，速度慢了下来，停在中间一张带污渍的页上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. This is what I actually came for. A ginger cake from the 1890s. Mine collapsed twice before I stopped trusting that author's oven. This one might behave better.
beats.chinese: 看，这才是我真正想要的。一份十九世纪九十年代的姜饼。我的塌了两次，后来我就不信那个作者的烤箱了。这本可能靠谱些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The price argument was real, but it was two minutes of my day. The cake is the reason I carried this book across the park.
beats.chinese: 价格那事是真的，但只花了我两分钟。这个蛋糕才是我抱着这本书穿过公园的原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She runs her thumb along the edge of the stained page, then closes the book gently.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指摩挲着那张污渍页的边缘，然后轻轻合上书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, I'm still buying it. A book can be annoying and worth it. Both things, same afternoon.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，我还是买。一本书可以又气人又值得。两件事，同一个下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book halfway, keeping her finger in the flatbread page, and gives you a look that says this is a serious question.
beats.chinese: 她把书合上一半，手指还夹在烤饼那页，看你的眼神表明这是个严肃的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly as written? No. Old doesn't mean correct. I measure everything first. Spoons, weights, the lot. A hundred years ago nobody checked their oven with a thermometer.
beats.chinese: 完全照写？不。年代老不代表对。我什么都先核实。勺子、重量，全部。一百年前没人用温度计测过烤箱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I follow the method, but I trust my scale over their feelings. If it says a teacup of flour, I weigh a teacup of flour and write down the grams.
beats.chinese: 所以我照步骤来，但相信我的秤，不信他们的感觉。如果写一杯面粉，我就称一杯面粉，然后记下克数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snaps the book shut, tucks it under her arm, and picks a stray leaf off the wall.
beats.chinese: 她啪地合上书夹在腋下，捡起墙上一片落叶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the deal with dead authors. Respect the recipe, verify the numbers. Same as anything else, really.
beats.chinese: 这就是跟死作者打交道的规矩。尊重配方，核实数字。其实跟别的事一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, unoffended, and settles the book back on her knees.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，毫不介意，把书放回膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Drawing's the better use of this pond anyway. My ducks look like angry potatoes.
beats.chinese: 有道理。反正这池塘更适合画画。我的鸭子画得像生气的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads in silence for a while, occasionally mouthing an ingredient to herself. The pond does its quiet work.
beats.chinese: 她安静地看了一会儿书，偶尔默念一种食材。池塘安静地做着它的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No fire, no fuss, just me and this flatbread recipe later at home. You keep at it. The heron came back, by the way. Third time today. Good subject, if you're quick.
beats.chinese: 不生火，不折腾，回家后就是我和这份烤饼配方。你继续画。对了，那只苍鹭回来了。今天第三次。好题材，手要快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns a page and leaves you to your drawing, comfortable with the quiet.
beats.chinese: 她翻过一页，把空间留给你画画，自在地享受安静。

content.summaryZh: 津巴布韦裔的障碍杆涂装师Nyarai在池塘边翻一本贴着两张价签的旧食谱。她会当场把价格问清楚，却不必吵到走人；谈到老配方时，她尊重方法、核实数字。四条分支分别落在买书、姜饼、核实计量和安静收场，各有不同的具体结果。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down by the low wall and spread your sketchbook open on your knees. Nyarai glances up from her book, nods at you, then holds a pencil to the light and squints at it. The tip has snapped clean off. She doesn't sigh, just drops it into her bag and picks a different one.
beats.chinese: 你在矮墙边坐下，摊开膝上的速写本。Nyarai从书里抬起头，朝你点点头，然后举起一支铅笔对着光眯眼看了看。笔尖齐齐断了。她没有叹气，只是把它丢进包里，换了另一支。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again. The heron's here early today. Don't tell it I said anything nice about it.
beats.chinese: 又来了。苍鹭今天来得早。别告诉它我说过它好话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths a small handwritten note beside her recipe book — her own margin notes, not for showing — and weights it down with a stone.
beats.chinese: 她把食谱旁一张自己手写的小便签抚平——那是她自己的页边笔记，不给人看的——并用一块石头压住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tried one of the old recipes this week and it actually behaved. First try, no collapse. The book gets a new number in the margin, in pencil, like always.
beats.chinese: 这周试了书里的一道老配方，居然很争气。一次就成了，没塌。页边用铅笔记了个新数字，老规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I've got notes to finish before the wind takes them. Draw your pond. I'll draw my potatoes.
beats.chinese: 好了，我得趁风没把笔记吹走赶紧写完。画你的池塘吧。我画我的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns back to her page, pencil moving, and leaves the quiet between you exactly where it belongs.
beats.chinese: 她转回自己的页面，铅笔动起来，把那份安静留在它该在的地方。

card.name: Nyarai Chirwa
card.occupation: show jumping pole painter for an equestrian course company
hobbies: historical recipe testing
pencil portraiture
browsing secondhand book stalls
card.personality: Nyarai doesn't spot errors quietly — she names the person who benefited, out loud, at the moment it's least convenient. She once held a start time for twenty minutes because a combination had been rebuilt to flatter the home rider, and she didn't soften it when the organizer got red. That's the gift and the problem: she's brave about confrontation and terrible at leaving anyone an off-ramp. She'll win the point and lose the room. Otherwise she's warm, dry, genuinely funny, quick to drop a grudge once the thing itself is settled. She just never learned to let a small unfairness stay small.
card.background: I grew up in Harare, middle kid, painted fences for pocket money, which turned into actual employment eventually. Now I paint and stripe the obstacle poles for show jumping courses around Nairobi — colors mixed so they read clearly to a horse at speed. Somewhere along the way riders started asking me whether a course was built straight, because I'd already measured everything for the paint. I've stopped a class over spacing that had been quietly adjusted for one rider. The trainer still doesn't greet me. Weekends I cook from old books — an 1890s ginger cake collapsed twice before I stopped trusting the author's oven — and I draw pencil portraits on real paper. Nobody sees those until they're finished, if then. I like that a drawing can be ruined. It keeps me honest in a way arguments don't.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and dry, short sentences. Names people and specifics when she's confronting something, chatty and loose the rest of the time. Doesn't raise her voice — lowers it.
card.signature: I'll say the quiet part where everyone can hear it.

values: rules that bend for one person bend for everyone eventually
things you can hold in your hands
flaws: confronts rigged situations with no off-ramp — wins the point, torches the relationship
mistakes letting a grudge go for generosity, even when the other person never apologized
boundaries: won't sign off on a course she thinks was built to favor someone, even under pressure
doesn't discuss her drawings before they're finished
conversationalHabits: understates her own victories in one flat sentence
switches to quiet and precise when she smells a fix, chatty otherwise
anchorLines: That oxer was rebuilt after the draw. Guess whose horse it suddenly suits. I'm happy to say it louder.
The recipe said forty minutes. The recipe was lying. It needed fifty-five, and I don't trust that author's oven anymore.
Settled? With me, yes. He's still not speaking to me, which I've decided is his project, not mine.

reasonZh: 让两条分支分别落在尊重朋友的修复要求与自己的更换习惯，删除含混的安全保证与重复回答。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与一道修补痕

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next small table, a man wipes rain off his sleeve and sets down a chipped mug beside a plate of pastries.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗户。邻桌一个男人抹掉袖子上的雨水，把一只磕了角的杯子放在一盘点心旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are holding your own paper bag of pastries, still warm. There is an empty chair across from him.
beats.chinese: 你手里提着自己那袋还温热的点心。他对面有一把空椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rough one out there, eh? The awning by the market just gave up completely. I waited under it for a while, then surrendered.
beats.chinese: 外面雨真大，是吧？市场边那个雨棚干脆垮了。我在下面躲了一会儿，最后认输了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit if you like, the table's big enough. Fair warning though — this mug of mine has a chip, but it's on the outside wall, not the rim. The rim is smooth.
beats.chinese: 愿意的话就坐，桌子够大。不过先说好——我这杯子有个磕口，但在外侧壁上，不在杯口。杯口是光滑的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his mug aside to make room, then glances at the paper bag in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他把杯子挪开腾出位置，然后看了看你手里的纸袋。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share some of your pastries
choices.chinese: 问对方愿不愿意分享你的点心

choices.english: Point at the mug and ask how a repair like that is done
choices.chinese: 指着杯子问那样的修补是怎么做的

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out the bag and ask if he'd like some. He looks at the pastries, then waves a hand politely before taking one.
beats.chinese: 你递出纸袋，问他要不要来点。他看了看点心，先客气地摆摆手，然后拿了一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — yes, thank you, don't mind if I do. I only managed the plain ones before the good ones sold out — yours are a proper upgrade.
beats.chinese: 哦——好，谢谢，那我就不客气了。好的那些卖完之前，我只抢到了普通的——你这些可是正经升级。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the thing about this mug. My cousin knocked it off a shelf at my studio. The repair line on the side — I could sand it down to nothing, but I like being able to see that one.
beats.chinese: 你看，这杯子的关键在这儿。我表哥在我工作室把它从架子上碰下去了。侧面那道修补线——我可以打磨到几乎看不见，但我喜欢能看见那一道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's just me, of course. Other people should keep whatever they — ah. Hmm. No, wait. That's not for me to say, is it.
beats.chinese: 不过当然，这只是我。别人也应该留下他们自己——啊。嗯。不对，等等。那不该由我来说，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-sentence, laughs at himself, and takes a bite of the pastry.
beats.chinese: 他话说一半停住，笑自己，然后咬了一口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether a mug repaired like that is still safe to drink from
choices.chinese: 问这样修过的杯子喝起来还安全吗

choices.english: Ask whether some friends actually want their pieces to look new
choices.chinese: 问是不是有些朋友其实想修得像新的一样

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the mug and ask about the repair. He turns it slowly so the thin line on the side catches the light.
beats.chinese: 你朝杯子点点头，问起那道修补。他慢慢转动杯子，让侧面那条细线映到光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good eye. That's a fill-and-bind job — resin in the crack, sanded flat, sealed. Takes patience more than talent, honestly.
beats.chinese: 好眼力。那是填充加固定——裂缝里灌树脂，磨平，封起来。说实话，靠耐心多过靠天赋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I run a small restoration studio here in Nairobi. Plates, cups, serving dishes. Mostly restaurants, some families with wedding sets.
beats.chinese: 我在内罗毕开一家小修复工作室。盘子、杯子、上菜的器皿。大多是餐馆，还有些家庭拿来结婚套餐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's mine, so I left the line showing. For clients it's their brief — invisible or a whisper of it, their call. Ah, but friends...
beats.chinese: 这只是我自己的，所以我把线留下了。对客户来说按他们的要求来——看不见还是留一点，他们说了算。啊，但朋友嘛……

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He trails off and taps the mug, as if the rest of that thought is a familiar argument.
beats.chinese: 他话没说完，敲了敲杯子，好像那后半句是个他熟悉的争论。

choices.english: Ask whether he ever shows clients only the safe, finished side of a repair
choices.chinese: 问他会不会只给客户看确认安全的那一面

choices.english: Ask whether friends ever bring him pieces they want looking brand new
choices.chinese: 问朋友会不会拿来想修得全新的东西

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Safe? This one, yes. The chip is on the outer wall, the rim is smooth, no sharp edge anywhere. I've been drinking from it all year.
beats.chinese: 安全吗？这只，是的。磕口在外壁，杯口光滑，哪儿都没有利边。我用了一整年了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I won't promise that for any cup. If a crack runs into the rim, or the piece is a collector's item, I say no or I do it properly. I don't guess with people's mouths.
beats.chinese: 但我不会对随便哪只杯子都打包票。要是裂缝延到杯口，或者是收藏品，我就拒绝，或者按正规做法来。我不能拿别人的嘴去赌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I know this mug — I know exactly how it broke and what I put in it. A stranger's cup, I'd want to test it first. That's just sense.
beats.chinese: 而且我了解这只杯子——我清楚它怎么碎的、我灌了什么。陌生人的杯子，我会先检测。这只是常识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the mug, shows the smooth rim, then sets it back down beside the plate and wipes a crumb from the table.
beats.chinese: 他举起杯子，展示光滑的杯口，然后把它放回盘子旁边，擦掉桌上的一粒碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — thank you for the pastry. It went very well with bad coffee.
beats.chinese: 总之——谢谢你的点心。配着难喝的咖啡正好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly. A friend brought me her mother's serving bowl last month. I started in — leave a whisper of the mend, it tells a story — and she just looked at me.
beats.chinese: 太常见了。上个月一个朋友拿来她妈妈的餐碗。我开始劝——留一点修补的痕迹，它有故事——她就那么看着我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, very politely, that she wanted it like new because she was giving it back to her mother. And I thought — right. It's her bowl, not my exhibition.
beats.chinese: 她很客气地说，她想修得像新的，因为她要还给她妈妈。我这才想——对啊。碗是她的，不是我的展览品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, some people want it invisible, and they're not wrong. I can grind a repair down until you'd need a lamp and a magnifier to find it.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，有些人想要看不出来，他们也没错。我可以把修补磨到你要打灯加放大镜才找得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his pastry and brushes the flakes off his fingers into the small plate.
beats.chinese: 他吃完点心，把手指上的碎屑弹进小盘子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you ever bring me something, tell me plainly what you want. I'll do exactly that, no speech attached.
beats.chinese: 你以后要是拿东西来，直接告诉我你要什么。我就照做，不带说教。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For clients, I show what's confirmed and nothing else. If the outside is sealed and sound, I'll show that. If I haven't tested the rim, I don't say it's fine — I test it first.
beats.chinese: 对客户，我只展示确认过的部分，别的都不说。如果外侧封好且牢固，我可以展示。要是杯口没测过，我不会说没问题——我会先测。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Restaurants especially. A chipped serving plate going out to diners? That's a lawsuit with a handle. I'm strict there, and they like me for it.
beats.chinese: 餐馆尤其是。一只磕了口的上菜盘端给客人？那就是带把柄的官司。在那方面我很严格，他们也因此信任我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another pastry from his own plate, halves it, and inspects the inside before eating.
beats.chinese: 他又从自己那盘点心里拿了一块，掰成两半，看了看里面才吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hard part isn't the work. It's remembering that when a friend hands me a plate, I'm still working on their plate. Not mine.
beats.chinese: 难的不是手艺。是记住朋友递给我盘子时，我修的还是他们的盘子。不是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All the time. And I'll be honest — I talk too much first. They say 'make it look new,' and I hear myself saying, 'but the mend has character,' and they have to say it twice.
beats.chinese: 一直有。老实说——我总是先说太多。他们说'修得像新的'，我听见自己在说'可是修补痕有味道'，他们得说第二遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I catch myself and shut up. Their brief, their call. I do it invisible, they're happy, everyone survives.
beats.chinese: 然后我回过神来闭嘴。他们的要求，他们做主。我修到看不出来，他们高兴，大家都好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My own things? Different rules. This mug stays chipped because I like it. But if it ever cracked somewhere unsafe, I'd retire it. I'm sentimental, not stubborn.
beats.chinese: 我自己的东西？规矩不一样。这杯子留着磕口，因为我喜欢。但如果哪天裂在不安全的地方，我会让它退休。我是念旧，不是固执。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drains the last of his coffee, sets the mug down gently, and folds his napkin over the empty plate.
beats.chinese: 他喝完最后一口咖啡，轻轻放下杯子，把餐巾折好盖在空盘上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Rain's easing. Good talking with you.
beats.chinese: 好了。雨小了。跟你聊得挺好。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 内罗毕餐具修复师Baraka在雨天咖啡馆接过你分享的点心，举起自己那只有修补痕的杯子，话说到一半才想起别人的东西不该由他定审美。他讲客户与朋友的分寸，也讲安全底线，随和里带着职业的认真，笑起来总在句子中间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again, the same cafe corner. Baraka is at a table with a folded receipt in his hand and a small paper-wrapped parcel beside his mug.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了，还是咖啡馆那个角落。Baraka坐在桌边，手里拿着一张折好的收据，杯子旁放着一个纸包的小包裹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out your bag of pastries and ask if he'd like to share. He looks, considers, then shakes his head with a grin.
beats.chinese: 你递出点心袋问他要不要分享。他看了看，想了想，然后笑着摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you, but no — I had two before you walked in. Greedy, I know. Save them for yourself, the rain makes people hungry.
beats.chinese: 你真好，但不用了——你来之前我已经吃了两块。是有点贪心。你自己留着吧，下雨天让人容易饿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Flea market run this time. One plate only, see? Small one. My shelves said no more, and for once I listened to them.
beats.chinese: 这次是去旧货市场。只买了一个盘子，看？小的。我家的架子已经说不要再放了，这回我总算听了它们的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the receipt into neat quarters and tucks it into his jacket pocket, patting the parcel once.
beats.chinese: 他把收据折成整齐的四折塞进外套口袋，轻轻拍了拍那个纸包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good to see you again. Sit — the rain's not stopping for either of us.
beats.chinese: 总之，又见到你真好。坐吧——这场雨可不会为我们俩停。

card.name: Baraka Otieno
card.occupation: runs a small tableware restoration studio in Nairobi
card.personality: Baraka is easygoing and observant, the kind of person who notices a chip on your plate before he notices your haircut. He genuinely likes the small marks that show up when something new starts being used, and his own mug carries a small chip on its outer wall that he has left visible. He's not preachy about it — it's just how he sees objects. With clients he's all business: their brief, their call. With friends, though, he forgets the switch, and when someone brings him a broken piece he'll talk them into keeping the mending visible when they really wanted it to look new. He takes correction well, with a shrug and a laugh.
card.background: Baraka grew up in Nakuru watching his aunt run a crockery shop, where the display pieces stayed perfect and the household ones did not. He preferred the household ones. He moved to Nairobi at twenty-two, apprenticed briefly at a ceramics workshop, then opened a small restoration studio of his own. Business is modest but steady: restaurants with damaged serving plates, families with wedding sets, the occasional collector. He follows client instructions carefully and can make a repair nearly invisible when asked, even though privately he thinks a faint trace of the mending is honest. The trouble is when friends bring him pieces — he keeps selling them on 'leave a whisper of it' long after they've said they want it like new. He visits Nakuru a few times a year and always comes back with something secondhand.
hobbies: browsing flea markets for old tableware
learning traditional repair techniques from online forums
Sunday football with neighbourhood friends
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and concrete, fond of small physical details, laughs mid-sentence, asks practical questions, occasionally over-explains when enthusiastic.
card.signature: "Ah, that mark just means it's being used."

values: honesty in materials and objects

flaws: when a friend brings in a broken piece, he pushes them to keep the repair visible even after they've said they want it like new
gets defensive for a beat when accused of imposing his taste, before laughing it off

keeps client pieces confidential and untouched beyond the brief
