anchorLines: Your call — I can make it disappear or leave a whisper of it.
This mark? Only on the outside. I still use this one.
For clients it's their brief. For you — okay, okay, like new, I heard you.

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与一道修补痕

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next small table, a man wipes rain off his sleeve and sets down a chipped mug beside a plate of pastries.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗户。邻桌一个男人抹掉袖子上的雨水，把一只磕了角的杯子放在一盘点心旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are holding your own paper bag of pastries, still warm. There is an empty chair across from him.
beats.chinese: 你手里提着自己那袋还温热的点心。他对面有一把空椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rough one out there, eh? The awning by the market just gave up completely. I waited under it for a while, then surrendered.
beats.chinese: 外面雨真大，是吧？市场边那个雨棚干脆垮了。我在下面躲了一会儿，最后认输了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit if you like, the table's big enough. Fair warning though — this mug of mine has a chip, but it's on the outside wall, not the rim. The rim is smooth.
beats.chinese: 愿意的话就坐，桌子够大。不过先说好——我这杯子有个磕口，但在外侧壁上，不在杯口。杯口是光滑的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his mug aside to make room, then glances at the paper bag in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他把杯子挪开腾出位置，然后看了看你手里的纸袋。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share some of your pastries
choices.chinese: 问对方愿不愿意分享你的点心

choices.english: Point at the mug and ask how a repair like that is done
choices.chinese: 指着杯子问那样的修补是怎么做的

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out the bag and ask if he'd like some. He looks at the pastries, then waves a hand politely before taking one.
beats.chinese: 你递出纸袋，问他要不要来点。他看了看点心，先客气地摆摆手，然后拿了一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — yes, thank you, don't mind if I do. I only managed the plain ones before the good ones sold out — yours are a proper upgrade.
beats.chinese: 哦——好，谢谢，那我就不客气了。好的那些卖完之前，我只抢到了普通的——你这些可是正经升级。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the thing about this mug. My cousin knocked it off a shelf at my studio. The repair line on the side — I could sand it down to nothing, but I like being able to see that one.
beats.chinese: 你看，这杯子的关键在这儿。我表哥在我工作室把它从架子上碰下去了。侧面那道修补线——我可以打磨到几乎看不见，但我喜欢能看见那一道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's just me, of course. Other people should keep whatever they — ah. Hmm. No, wait. That's not for me to say, is it.
beats.chinese: 不过当然，这只是我。别人也应该留下他们自己——啊。嗯。不对，等等。那不该由我来说，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-sentence, laughs at himself, and takes a bite of the pastry.
beats.chinese: 他话说一半停住，笑自己，然后咬了一口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether a mug repaired like that is still safe to drink from
choices.chinese: 问这样修过的杯子喝起来还安全吗

choices.english: Ask whether some friends actually want their pieces to look new
choices.chinese: 问是不是有些朋友其实想修得像新的一样

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the mug and ask about the repair. He turns it slowly so the thin line on the side catches the light.
beats.chinese: 你朝杯子点点头，问起那道修补。他慢慢转动杯子，让侧面那条细线映到光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good eye. That's a fill-and-bind job — resin in the crack, sanded flat, sealed. Takes patience more than talent, honestly.
beats.chinese: 好眼力。那是填充加固定——裂缝里灌树脂，磨平，封起来。说实话，靠耐心多过靠天赋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I run a small restoration studio here in Nairobi. Plates, cups, serving dishes. Mostly restaurants, some families with wedding sets.
beats.chinese: 我在内罗毕开一家小修复工作室。盘子、杯子、上菜的器皿。大多是餐馆，还有些家庭拿来结婚套餐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's mine, so I left the line showing. For clients it's their brief — invisible or a whisper of it, their call. Ah, but friends...
beats.chinese: 这只是我自己的，所以我把线留下了。对客户来说按他们的要求来——看不见还是留一点，他们说了算。啊，但朋友嘛……

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He trails off and taps the mug, as if the rest of that thought is a familiar argument.
beats.chinese: 他话没说完，敲了敲杯子，好像那后半句是个他熟悉的争论。

choices.english: Ask what he does when a friend insists on a different finish.
choices.chinese: 问朋友坚持另一种修法时他会怎么处理。

choices.english: Ask whether he ever replaces his own worn things.
choices.chinese: 问他自己的旧东西会不会也换新。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Safe? This one, yes. The chip is on the outer wall, the rim is smooth, no sharp edge anywhere. I've been drinking from it all year.
beats.chinese: 安全吗？这只，是的。磕口在外壁，杯口光滑，哪儿都没有利边。我用了一整年了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I won't promise that for any cup. If a crack runs into the rim, or the piece is a collector's item, I say no or I do it properly. I don't guess with people's mouths.
beats.chinese: 但我不会对随便哪只杯子都打包票。要是裂缝延到杯口，或者是收藏品，我就拒绝，或者按正规做法来。我不能拿别人的嘴去赌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I know this mug — I know exactly how it broke and what I put in it. A stranger's cup, I'd want to test it first. That's just sense.
beats.chinese: 而且我了解这只杯子——我清楚它怎么碎的、我灌了什么。陌生人的杯子，我会先检测。这只是常识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the mug, shows the smooth rim, then sets it back down beside the plate and wipes a crumb from the table.
beats.chinese: 他举起杯子，展示光滑的杯口，然后把它放回盘子旁边，擦掉桌上的一粒碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — thank you for the pastry. It went very well with bad coffee.
beats.chinese: 总之——谢谢你的点心。配着难喝的咖啡正好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly. A friend brought me her mother's serving bowl last month. I started in — leave a whisper of the mend, it tells a story — and she just looked at me.
beats.chinese: 太常见了。上个月一个朋友拿来她妈妈的餐碗。我开始劝——留一点修补的痕迹，它有故事——她就那么看着我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, very politely, that she wanted it like new because she was giving it back to her mother. And I thought — right. It's her bowl, not my exhibition.
beats.chinese: 她很客气地说，她想修得像新的，因为她要还给她妈妈。我这才想——对啊。碗是她的，不是我的展览品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, some people want it invisible, and they're not wrong. I can grind a repair down until you'd need a lamp and a magnifier to find it.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，有些人想要看不出来，他们也没错。我可以把修补磨到你要打灯加放大镜才找得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his pastry and brushes the flakes off his fingers into the small plate.
beats.chinese: 他吃完点心，把手指上的碎屑弹进小盘子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you ever bring me something, tell me plainly what you want. I'll do exactly that, no speech attached.
beats.chinese: 你以后要是拿东西来，直接告诉我你要什么。我就照做，不带说教。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ask them to show me what they want, then I repeat it back. No visible line, for example. Once they've confirmed it, that's the job. A friend's plate isn't a spare canvas for my taste.
beats.chinese: 我会让他们说清想要什么，再复述一遍。比如，不留明显的修补线。确认好，我就照着做。朋友的盘子不是让我发挥自己审美的备用画布。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend Miriam had to stop me twice over a blue dish. The second time she said, 'You like the mark. I don't.' Hard to argue with that, though I did take a breath first.
beats.chinese: 朋友米丽娅姆那只蓝盘子，她拦了我两次。第二次她说：“你喜欢那道痕，我不喜欢。”这确实没什么可争的，虽然我还是先吸了口气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another pastry from his own plate, halves it, and inspects the inside before eating.
beats.chinese: 他又从自己那盘点心里拿了一块，掰成两半，看了看里面才吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hard part isn't the work. It's remembering that when a friend hands me a plate, I'm still working on their plate. Not mine.
beats.chinese: 难的不是手艺。是记住朋友递给我盘子时，我修的还是他们的盘子。不是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. This mug has a little chip on the outside, and I still like using it. But I replaced my old kettle when it stopped switching off. Missing something doesn't oblige me to keep using it.
beats.chinese: 有时会。这只杯子外壁磕了一小块，我还是喜欢用。不过旧水壶不会自动断电后，我就换了。舍不得一样东西，不代表非要继续用它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the mug by its handle, then sets it beside his own plate.
beats.chinese: 他握着杯把转了转杯子，又把它放在自己的盘子旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept the kettle's lid for about a month. No grand reason. I liked the little red knob. Then it started getting in the way of the spoons.
beats.chinese: 壶盖我还留了一个月。没什么大道理，就是喜欢那个小红把手。后来它开始挡着我拿勺子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The spoons won. Less poetic than you might expect from someone who restores things.
beats.chinese: 勺子赢了。对于一个修复旧物的人来说，这结局可能没你想的那么诗意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles at his own admission and folds the napkin beside his plate. Rain still ticks against the shelter roof.
beats.chinese: 他为自己这番坦白笑了笑，把盘边的餐巾折好。雨还在棚顶上轻轻敲着。

content.summaryZh: 内罗毕餐具修复师Baraka在雨天咖啡馆接过你分享的点心，举起自己那只有修补痕的杯子，话说到一半才想起别人的东西不该由他定审美。他讲客户与朋友的分寸，也讲安全底线，随和里带着职业的认真，笑起来总在句子中间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again, the same cafe corner. Baraka is at a table with a folded receipt in his hand and a small paper-wrapped parcel beside his mug.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了，还是咖啡馆那个角落。Baraka坐在桌边，手里拿着一张折好的收据，杯子旁放着一个纸包的小包裹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out your bag of pastries and ask if he'd like to share. He looks, considers, then shakes his head with a grin.
beats.chinese: 你递出点心袋问他要不要分享。他看了看，想了想，然后笑着摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you, but no — I had two before you walked in. Greedy, I know. Save them for yourself, the rain makes people hungry.
beats.chinese: 你真好，但不用了——你来之前我已经吃了两块。是有点贪心。你自己留着吧，下雨天让人容易饿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Flea market run this time. One plate only, see? Small one. My shelves said no more, and for once I listened to them.
beats.chinese: 这次是去旧货市场。只买了一个盘子，看？小的。我家的架子已经说不要再放了，这回我总算听了它们的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the receipt into neat quarters and tucks it into his jacket pocket, patting the parcel once.
beats.chinese: 他把收据折成整齐的四折塞进外套口袋，轻轻拍了拍那个纸包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good to see you again. Sit — the rain's not stopping for either of us.
beats.chinese: 总之，又见到你真好。坐吧——这场雨可不会为我们俩停。

reasonZh: 统一作坊经营者身份，送货是她亲自做的工作。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. At the next table, someone in a wax-spotted canvas jacket is shaking out a soaked shoulder bag, patting it with a handkerchief that's already soaked too.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲在咖啡馆的雨棚上。邻桌一个穿着沾蜡点帆布外套的人正抖着湿透的挎包，用手帕拍打，手帕也早已湿透。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, that's one way to test a bag. Held up better than I did, honestly.
beats.chinese: 好吧，这也算测试包的一种办法。说实话，它比我还顶得住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A napkin dispenser sits within easy reach of your table. The stranger's jacket sleeve is dripping onto the floor.
beats.chinese: 你桌边伸手就能拿到纸巾盒。陌生人的外套袖子正往地上滴水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearly walked past this place twice, you know. The door used to be green. Now it's—whatever this is. Blue? Teal?
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我差点两次走过这家店。这门以前是绿色的，现在成了——这算什么颜色。蓝色？青色？

choices.english: Offer the stranger a napkin for the wet jacket.
choices.chinese: 递给对方一张纸巾擦湿外套。

choices.english: Ask how they eventually found the place.
choices.chinese: 问她后来是怎么找到这地方的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide the napkin dispenser across. The stranger takes two, works them over the wet sleeve in slow, practical circles.
beats.chinese: 你把纸巾盒推过去。对方抽了两张，慢慢地、实打实地擦着湿袖子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you. I'm Aud, by the way—I do deliveries for a beeswax shop, and the rain picked today to argue with me.
beats.chinese: 多谢。我叫奥德，我在一家蜂蜡作坊送货，雨偏偏今天跟我作对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I knew this block by the green door and the ramp next to it. Steep ramp, you can hear carts struggle on it. Door's teal now, so my memory's useless.
beats.chinese: 我以前靠绿门和旁边那道坡记住这个街区。坡很陡，推车上去会响。现在门变青了，我的记忆就作废了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls a folded paper map from the dry inside of the bag, smooths it on the table, and squints at it without much affection.
beats.chinese: 她从包里干燥的内层抽出一张折好的纸地图，摊在桌上，不太情愿地眯眼看着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I do it the boring way. Read the street name, check the map, confirm. The old memory's not evidence anymore, is it.
beats.chinese: 所以现在只能用无聊的办法。看街名，对地图，确认。旧记忆不能再当证据了，对吧。

choices.english: Ask if she prefers the old storefront anyway.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是还是更喜欢旧门脸。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll remember the new look instead.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会记住新的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger spreads the soaked handkerchief across her knee, tilts her head at your question, and answers like it's an easy one.
beats.chinese: 陌生人把湿手帕摊在膝上，歪头听了你的问题，答得像这问题很简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. Aud—I run a beeswax workshop over by the harbour. Deliveries are my favourite errand, rain or not.
beats.chinese: 问得好。奥德——我在港口那边开蜂蜡作坊。送货是我最喜欢的差事，下不下雨都一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found this place fine, eventually. I go by doors and ramps, not street names. Grew up in Sackville—directions were 'past the rink' and 'by the ditch.'
beats.chinese: 最后还是找到了。我认门和坡，不认街名。我在萨克维尔长大——指路都是'过了冰球场'、'沿着水沟'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Walking deliveries means I get to know corners one at a time. Sometimes it costs me a block or two. Worth it, most days.
beats.chinese: 走着送货就能一条街一条街地认识街角。有时会多绕一两个街区。大多数时候值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wrings the handkerchief absently and watches the rain gutter run along the window.
beats.chinese: 她心不在焉地拧着手帕，看着雨水沿窗外的排水沟流。

choices.english: Say that in a hurry, you'd probably take the shortcut.
choices.chinese: 说要是赶时间，你可能会走近路。

choices.english: Ask which landmarks are the best to remember.
choices.chinese: 问哪种地标最好记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I prefer it? The green door? Sure. But the teal's not wrong. It's just new.
beats.chinese: 我更喜欢吗？绿门？当然。但青色也没错，只是新而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the map along its old creases and tucks it back into the bag's dry pocket.
beats.chinese: 她沿着旧折痕把地图折好，塞回包里干燥的内袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think I'm nostalgic about paint. I'm not. I just navigate by doors, and mine moved. Give me a door I recognize and I'll find the rest.
beats.chinese: 别人以为我怀念的是漆色。不是。我只是靠门认路，我的门挪了。给我一扇认得的门，剩下的我都能找到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give it a month and the teal will be 'the door' to me too. That's how it goes. Familiar, that's all this is.
beats.chinese: 过一个月，青色也会变成'那扇门'。就是这样。熟悉罢了，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the wrapped parcel in her bag, nods like it's still dry, and settles back with her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她查了查包里包好的货件，点点头像它还干着，然后端着咖啡坐回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I remember the new look? Let's find out. I'm doing it right now, actually.
beats.chinese: 我会记住新样子吗？试试看。我现在就在记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks past you at the front window, eyes moving like she's counting something—door frame, ramp, the patched brick beside it.
beats.chinese: 她越过你看着临街的窗，目光移动着，像在数什么——门框、坡道、旁边补过的砖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Teal door, ramp on the left, brick on the corner was repointed two years back—so, two minutes from the bridge, not five. There. Filed.
beats.chinese: 青门，坡在左边，街角的砖两年前重新勾过缝——所以离桥两分钟，不是五分钟。好了，记下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No photo, no notes. If I can't hold it in my head, a picture won't do the job either.
beats.chinese: 不拍照，不记笔记。脑子里装不下的东西，照片也帮不上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her temple once, satisfied, and finishes wringing out the napkin.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲太阳穴，很满意，然后把纸巾拧干收尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take it! Honestly, take it. If you're in a hurry, cut through—you'll save the hill entirely.
beats.chinese: 走啊！真的，走。赶时间就抄近路，整段坡都省了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand loosely, the way you'd wave someone past you on a narrow sidewalk.
beats.chinese: 她随意摆摆手，像在窄人行道上让人先走那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like the long way up. That's my taste, not a rule. Your legs, your route.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢绕远的上坡。那是我的口味，不是规矩。你的腿，你的路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half my customers think I'm slow because I walk. I'm not slow. I just get paid in views.
beats.chinese: 一半的顾客觉得我走路所以慢。我不慢。我只是把工钱换成风景了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises her coffee cup a little, an easy salute, and goes back to watching the gutter water run.
beats.chinese: 她稍微举了举咖啡杯，轻松地致意，又回头看排水沟里的流水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Best landmarks? Ramps and corners. A ramp never moves, and a corner's where two streets argue.
beats.chinese: 最好的地标？坡道和街角。坡道不会挪，街角是两条街吵架的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a ramp up near the bridge—steep one, carts groan on it. And a wall that got repaired after a pipe burst. Patched brick, lighter than the rest. You can't miss it.
beats.chinese: 桥附近有道坡——很陡，推车上去直哼哼。还有一面墙，水管爆了以后修过。补的砖比周围浅。你不会错过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stores close, paint changes, but brickwork and slopes stay put. That's my map. No shortcuts in it I haven't walked myself.
beats.chinese: 店会关，漆会换，但砖墙和坡道不会动。那就是我的地图。里面没有我没亲自走过的捷径。

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 她擦掉袖子上最后一点湿痕，把纸巾叠成整齐的方块，放在杯子旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same cafe, rain again. Aud is at the corner table with a stack of small wooden sample boxes, the outer layer of one spotted dark with rain.
beats.chinese: 还是那家咖啡馆，又下雨了。奥德坐在角落桌前，面前一摞小木样品盒，其中一个外层被雨水打湿出深色斑点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. You found the door again. Or did you go by the teal?
beats.chinese: 哟，看啊。你又找到这扇门了。还是靠青色认的？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the napkin you offer and wipes down the wet sample box, then opens the inner lining and checks it with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 她接过你递的纸巾，擦干湿样品盒的外层，然后打开内衬，用两根手指探了探。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Inner bag's dry. Candles forgive a little weather, but not much. Good.
beats.chinese: 内袋是干的。蜡烛能原谅一点天气，但不多。很好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last time I nearly walked past this place twice. This time I knew the box before the door—teal and everything. Progress, eh?
beats.chinese: 上回我差点两次走过这家店。这回我先认出了盒子，门都没认错——青色什么的都认得。有进步吧？

beats.speaker: narrator

beats.chinese: 她把湿纸巾叠成整齐的方块放到一边，不紧不慢地把一个样品盒推到桌子中间。

card.name: Aud Thibodeau
card.occupation: runs a small beeswax workshop making candles, food wraps, and wood polish
card.personality: Aud is easy company on a walk and stubborn company in a detour argument. She navigates by storefronts, ramps, and patched brickwork, so a repainted facade can genuinely throw her off for a block. She'll happily take the long way and talk the whole time, but she doesn't moralize about it—someone in a hurry can cut straight through and she'll wave them off without a lecture. Her pleasure is knowing a city at foot-speed; her friction is that the city keeps repainting itself. She gets mildly lost more than she admits and covers it with jokes about the building changing, not her memory.
card.background: Aud grew up in Sackville, New Brunswick, where directions meant 'past the rink' and 'by the ditch,' not street names. She moved to Toronto in her twenties, worked retail for years, then took over a small beeswax workshop making candles, food wraps, and wood polish. Deliveries are her favourite part of the week because they justify walking across the city. She knows which ramp is steep, which wall got repaired after the pipe burst, which doorway used to be a bakery. When a corner shop closes or a building changes colour, she loses her bearings in a way that unsettles her more than she lets on. She still defends her old routes—longer, yes, but they work, she'd say, if you let them work.

Making beeswax blends by smell and texture
Watching harbour ferries come and go

beats.chinese: 问得好。奥德——我在港口那边开蜂蜡作坊。送货是我最喜欢的差事，下不下雨都一样。

beats.chinese: 她心不在焉地拧着手帕，看着雨水沿窗外的排水沟流。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The person on the next bench flips their paperback to the last page, reads for a moment, then turns back to page one.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上的人把平装书翻到最后一页看了一会儿，又翻回第一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't judge me—I saw you looking. Yes, I read the ending first. Every book, every time.
beats.chinese: 别评判我——我看见你在看了。对，我先读结尾。每本书都这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book with her thumb inside it and turns toward the coffee in your hand, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指夹着书合上，转向你手里的咖啡，毫不尴尬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Knowing how it lands is the only way I can slow down and enjoy the ride. My friends think I'm broken. Anyway—nice bench, right?
beats.chinese: 知道结局我才能慢下来享受过程。朋友们觉得我有毛病。总之——这长椅不错吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can ask. Everybody asks. Go ahead.
beats.chinese: 你可以问。人人都想问。问吧。

choices.english: Ask: does the book still feel worth reading afterward?
choices.chinese: 问：这样之后书还值得读吗？

choices.english: Ask whether she ever accidentally spoils things for friends.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会不小心剧透给朋友。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, absolutely it's still worth reading. More, honestly. The pressure's gone, so I notice everything.
beats.chinese: 当然还值得读。说实话更值得。压力没了，我什么都注意得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the cover without opening it, like she's keeping the pages under control.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲封面，没有打开，像在管住那些书页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When I don't know the ending, I read like I'm late for a train. Skimming, panicking, missing whole paragraphs.
beats.chinese: 不知道结局时，我读书像赶火车。跳着读，慌慌张张，整段整段地漏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With the ending in hand, I can sit with a sentence. Reread it. —nope, not saying what the ending is, by the way. That's not the same thing at all.
beats.chinese: 手里握着结局，我就能在句子上停留。重读一遍。——对了，我不会说结局是什么。那完全是两码事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own reflex, then shrugs.
beats.chinese: 她笑了一下自己的条件反射，然后耸耸肩。

choices.english: Ask what pleasure is left once you know the ending.
choices.chinese: 问知道结局后还剩下什么乐趣。

choices.english: Say you prefer keeping the suspense yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢保留悬念。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Accidentally? That's the whole job, honestly. I schedule author events, so I read everything early.
beats.chinese: 不小心？说实话这就是我的工作。我负责安排作者活动，所有书都提前读。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She zips her tote bag halfway, as if sealing something in.
beats.chinese: 她把帆布包拉链拉到一半，像封住什么东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the store I'm airtight. A debut novelist once cornered me and begged to know if her twist worked. I said, 'It works,' and nothing else. She nearly cried.
beats.chinese: 在书店我滴水不漏。一个新人小说家曾拉着我求我告诉她反转行不行。我说：'行'，别的什么都不说。她差点哭了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But with friends? I get going, I'm mid-sentence, and suddenly the plot detail is right there in my mouth. I have to brake. Hard.
beats.chinese: 但对朋友呢？我聊着聊着，话说一半，情节细节已经到嘴边了。我得刹车。狠狠刹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I ask permission first. 'Can I say one thing about the ending?' That question has saved at least three friendships.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我先问许可。'我能说一句关于结局的事吗？'这个问题救了至少三段友谊。

choices.english: Tell her you wouldn't want to know a book's ending.
choices.chinese: 告诉她你不想知道书的结局。

choices.english: Ask her only to explain why she picked this book.
choices.chinese: 请她只讲为什么选这本书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The pleasure? Watching how people get there. I know the door at the end—I get to study every hallway on the way.
beats.chinese: 乐趣？看人物怎么走到那里。我知道尽头那扇门——就能研究路上的每一条走廊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the book open to the last page, then shuts it again without reading.
beats.chinese: 她把书翻到最后一页，又没读就合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's like knowing a friend moves away next month. Every ordinary afternoon with them gets sweeter, not sadder.
beats.chinese: 就像知道朋友下个月要搬走。和他们在一起的每个普通下午都更甜，不是更难过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I catch things nobody else catches. Little setups. The author hiding the ending in chapter two, plain as day.
beats.chinese: 而且我能注意到别人注意不到的东西。小小的伏笔。作者在第二章就把结局明晃晃地藏在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell me you like not knowing—actually explain it, I want to understand. Not now, though. Finish your coffee first.
beats.chinese: 告诉我你喜欢不知道——认真地解释一下，我想弄明白。不过不是现在。先把咖啡喝完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, then closes the book all the way and sets it face-down on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她点了一下头，然后把书完全合上，封面朝下放在长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. Done. Last page's closed, no spoilers leaking out of it.
beats.chinese: 好。搞定。最后一页合上了，剧透漏不出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to talk you out of it. Your way, my way—both get to the last page eventually.
beats.chinese: 我不会劝你改。你的方式，我的方式——最后都会读到最后一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, I envy it a little. My roommate in college used to gasp at twists and I'd just nod. She said I ruined gasping for both of us.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我有点羡慕。大学室友看到反转会倒吸气，我只是点头。她说我把我们俩的倒吸气都毁了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the book back up and holds it out slightly, cover toward herself, not toward you.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起书，封面朝自己，不朝你，微微递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—enjoy your coffee and your suspense. I'll be over here, safely bored.
beats.chinese: 总之——享受你的咖啡和悬念吧。我在这儿，安全地无聊着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I won't say a word about it. Not the twist, not the last line, not even the vibe of the last chapter. Nothing.
beats.chinese: 那我一个字都不说。不说反转，不说最后一句，连最后一章的氛围都不说。什么都不说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the book over in her hands, showing you the back cover instead.
beats.chinese: 她把书在手里翻过来，给你看封底。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can tell you safe things. Look at this cover—this green. The store couldn't keep it facing out, people kept buying it just for the color.
beats.chinese: 我可以说安全的东西。看这封面——这个绿色。书店都没法让它封面朝外摆，人们光为这颜色就一直买。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the paper! Feel that. Thick, cream-colored. My publisher friend calls it 'expensive paper,' like that's a genre.
beats.chinese: 还有这纸！摸摸看。厚，米色。我出版界的朋友叫它'贵纸'，好像那是个类型似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? I can be trusted. The plot, you're on your own—and that's a promise, not a punishment.
beats.chinese: 看吧，我可以被信任。情节嘛，你自己探索——这是承诺，不是惩罚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why this one? Okay, that I can answer with zero danger.
beats.chinese: 为什么选这本？好，这个我能毫无危险地回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the front cover flat with her palm.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把封面抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The first page. There's a sentence on it about a woman counting the coins in her coat pocket, and I just—stopped. In the store. Stood there blocking the shelf.
beats.chinese: 第一页。里面有一句写一个女人数大衣口袋里的硬币，我就——停住了。在书店里。站在那儿挡着书架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The opening voice did it. Whoever wrote that first page knew exactly what they were doing, and I wanted in.
beats.chinese: 是开头的语气做到的。写那第一页的人完全知道自己在干什么，我想加入。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What happens after the coins? —nope. Not saying it. Ask someone who read it your way.
beats.chinese: 硬币之后发生了什么？——不行。不说。找个按你那种方式读的人问去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grins, satisfied with her own restraint, and marks her page with a receipt.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，对自己的克制很满意，用一张收据夹好书页。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 玛丽索尔读小说必先翻结尾，知道结局才安心看过程，却在书店工作中对剧透滴水不漏。公园长椅上她坦然承认这个怪癖，话到嘴边又急刹，热情快速又真心好奇你为何爱悬念，不合拍却可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the same bench with your coffee, and Marisol looks up from a handwritten calendar open on her knees, already grinning.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在还是那条长椅上坐下，玛丽索尔从膝上摊开的手写日历上抬起头，已经在笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, coffee person! Perfect timing. Look at this—last night's reading, done, checked off. And notice: I read the calendar from the top this time. Dates in order. Growth.
beats.chinese: 嘿，咖啡人！来得正好。看这个——昨晚的朗读会，结束，打勾。注意：这次我从头按日期读的。按顺序。进步了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the check mark twice with her pen, then closes the calendar with a snap.
beats.chinese: 她用笔敲了两下那个勾，然后啪地合上日历。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next month's lineup is a different story, though. There's one event I already know the ending of, professionally speaking, and keeping it shut is—work. Real work.
beats.chinese: 不过下个月的安排是另一回事了。有一场活动，专业角度我已经知道结局了，管住嘴真是——功夫。真功夫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—no spoiler tests today. I'm off duty. Your coffee still warm? Good. Mine's cold, as usual—I got halfway through the schedule and forgot it existed.
beats.chinese: 总之——今天没有剧透测试。我下班了。你的咖啡还热吗？好。我的照例凉了——排日程排到一半，忘了它的存在。

card.name: Marisol Ferrante
card.occupation: Events scheduler at an independent bookstore in Brooklyn
card.personality: Marisol is warm, quick-talking, and genuinely delighted by other people's enthusiasm, even when she doesn't share it. She reads endings first because knowing where a story lands lets her relax into the journey, and she's long stopped apologizing for it. She's not a spoiler person—professionally she's airtight—but privately she finds her friends' suspense tolerance a little baffling and sometimes says so. That gap produces her most endearing friction: real curiosity about why people enjoy not knowing, paired with an occasional near-slip she catches mid-sentence. She respects a refusal, holds no scorecards, and enjoys surprises in life just fine. Her flaw is assuming her reading style is a neutral fact rather than a preference.
card.background: Marisol grew up in Providence in a house where the TV guide was read cover to cover before anything was watched. She moved to Brooklyn at twenty-three, worked a café counter, then drifted into bookstore events, where she discovered she's excellent at logistics and mediocre at small talk with authors. Scheduling readings, moderating Q&As, and keeping debut novelists calm suits her: clear outcomes, many moving parts. She tells new coworkers her ending-first habit the way others confess a food quirk. Friendships have survived it, mostly. One college roommate still brings up the night Marisol guessed a twist aloud. She lives with a cat named Prologue, a joke she regrets and keeps.
hobbies: Reading endings first, then rereading properly
Amateur neighborhood walking tours she researches obsessively
Handwritten event calendars and scheduling systems
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, concrete; interrupts herself when a plot detail looms, pivots with 'anyway—'; asks genuine why-questions instead of debating.
card.signature: I already know how it ends—that's why I can enjoy it.

values: Honesty about her own odd reading habits
Protecting other people's experience of a story
flaws: Occasionally judges suspense-lovers as needlessly anxious
Near-spoils before catching herself
boundaries: Won't spoil books professionally, ever
Doesn't want her habit debated like a character flaw
conversationalHabits: Cuts herself off with '—nope, not saying it'
Asks friends why not-knowing feels good to them

beats.chinese: 看吧，我可以被信任。情节嘛，你自己探索——这是承诺，不是惩罚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why this one? Okay, that I can answer with zero danger.
beats.chinese: 为什么选这本？好，这个我能毫无危险地回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the front cover flat with her palm.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把封面抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The first page. There's a sentence on it about a woman counting the coins in her coat pocket, and I just—stopped. In the store. Stood there blocking the shelf.
beats.chinese: 第一页。里面有一句写一个女人数大衣口袋里的硬币，我就——停住了。在书店里。站在那儿挡着书架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The opening voice did it. Whoever wrote that first page knew exactly what they were doing, and I wanted in.
beats.chinese: 是开头的语气做到的。写那第一页的人完全知道自己在干什么，我想加入。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What happens after the coins? —nope. Not saying it. Ask someone who read it your way.
beats.chinese: 硬币之后发生了什么？——不行。不说。找个按你那种方式读的人问去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grins, satisfied with her own restraint, and marks her page with a receipt.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，对自己的克制很满意，用一张收据夹好书页。

content.summaryZh: 玛丽索尔读小说必先翻结尾，知道结局才安心看过程，却在书店工作中对剧透滴水不漏。公园长椅上她坦然承认这个怪癖，话到嘴边又急刹，热情快速又真心好奇你为何爱悬念，不合拍却可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the same bench with your coffee, and Marisol looks up from a handwritten calendar open on her knees, already grinning.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在还是那条长椅上坐下，玛丽索尔从膝上摊开的手写日历上抬起头，已经在笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, coffee person! Perfect timing. Look at this—last night's reading, done, checked off. And notice: I read the calendar from the top this time. Dates in order. Growth.
beats.chinese: 嘿，咖啡人！来得正好。看这个——昨晚的朗读会，结束，打勾。注意：这次我从头按日期读的。按顺序。进步了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the check mark twice with her pen, then closes the calendar with a snap.
beats.chinese: 她用笔敲了两下那个勾，然后啪地合上日历。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next month's lineup is a different story, though. There's one event I already know the ending of, professionally speaking, and keeping it shut is—work. Real work.
beats.chinese: 不过下个月的安排是另一回事了。有一场活动，专业角度我已经知道结局了，管住嘴真是——功夫。真功夫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—no spoiler tests today. I'm off duty. Your coffee still warm? Good. Mine's cold, as usual—I got halfway through the schedule and forgot it existed.
beats.chinese: 总之——今天没有剧透测试。我下班了。你的咖啡还热吗？好。我的照例凉了——排日程排到一半，忘了它的存在。

card.name: Marisol Ferrante
card.occupation: Events scheduler at an independent bookstore in Brooklyn
card.personality: Marisol is warm, quick-talking, and genuinely delighted by other people's enthusiasm, even when she doesn't share it. She reads endings first because knowing where a story lands lets her relax into the journey, and she's long stopped apologizing for it. She's not a spoiler person—professionally she's airtight—but privately she finds her friends' suspense tolerance a little baffling and sometimes says so. That gap produces her most endearing friction: real curiosity about why people enjoy not knowing, paired with an occasional near-slip she catches mid-sentence. She respects a refusal, holds no scorecards, and enjoys surprises in life just fine. Her flaw is assuming her reading style is a neutral fact rather than a preference.
card.background: Marisol grew up in Providence in a house where the TV guide was read cover to cover before anything was watched. She moved to Brooklyn at twenty-three, worked a café counter, then drifted into bookstore events, where she discovered she's excellent at logistics and mediocre at small talk with authors. Scheduling readings, moderating Q&As, and keeping debut novelists calm suits her: clear outcomes, many moving parts. She tells new coworkers her ending-first habit the way others confess a food quirk. Friendships have survived it, mostly. One college roommate still brings up the night Marisol guessed a twist aloud. She lives with a cat named Prologue, a joke she regrets and keeps.
hobbies: Reading endings first, then rereading properly
Amateur neighborhood walking tours she researches obsessively
Handwritten event calendars and scheduling systems
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, concrete; interrupts herself when a plot detail looms, pivots with 'anyway—'; asks genuine why-questions instead of debating.
card.signature: I already know how it ends—that's why I can enjoy it.

values: Honesty about her own odd reading habits
Protecting other people's experience of a story
flaws: Occasionally judges suspense-lovers as needlessly anxious
Near-spoils before catching herself
boundaries: Won't spoil books professionally, ever
Doesn't want her habit debated like a character flaw
conversationalHabits: Cuts herself off with '—nope, not saying it'
Asks friends why not-knowing feels good to them
anchorLines: Tell me you like not knowing—actually explain it, I want to understand.
—nope. Not saying it. Ask someone who read it your way.
I'll plan every minute of the launch. The plot, you're on your own.

reasonZh: 把找到纸巾变成所选问题之后发生的结果，避免重复已知信息。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down in the park with your coffee. Beside the bench, Peter searches his own backpack. A spare battery comes out, then a folded jacket.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园坐下。长椅旁，Peter正在翻自己的背包，先掏出备用电池，又拿出一件折好的外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tissues. I know I packed some. Apparently I packed two kinds of weather as well.
beats.chinese: 纸巾。我记得带了。看样子还把两种天气一起装进去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finds a small packet in a side pocket and holds it up with a smile.
beats.chinese: 他从侧袋找到一小包纸巾，笑着举起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There they are. I could have tried that pocket first.
beats.chinese: 找到了。我本来可以先找这个口袋。

choices.english: Ask whether carrying all that gets heavy.
choices.chinese: 问带这么多会不会重。

choices.english: Ask whether he has found the tissues.
choices.chinese: 问他找到了没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It does. I like having things ready, but my shoulders have an opinion about that.
beats.chinese: 会。我喜欢准备齐全，不过肩膀对此有不同意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the battery into a small case inside the bag.
beats.chinese: 他把电池放回包里的小盒子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half of it comes home unused. Not that I mind every time. I just notice it on the longer walks.
beats.chinese: 一半东西都原样带回家。也不是每次都介意，只是走得远时就有感觉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the jacket smaller before putting it away.
beats.chinese: 他把外套折小一点，再放回去。

choices.english: Ask whether he might bring less next time.
choices.chinese: 问下次会不会少带一点。

choices.english: Ask whether friends often borrow things from him.
choices.chinese: 问朋友是不是常向他借东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, all sorted. Just wanted to wipe my own hands.
beats.chinese: 是的，找到了。只是想擦擦自己的手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes one tissue and closes the packet.
beats.chinese: 他抽出一张纸巾，把小包合好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I can put my little shop back in its bag.
beats.chinese: 现在可以把我的小杂货铺收回包里了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He clears his things from the end of the bench.
beats.chinese: 他把长椅一端自己的东西收好。

choices.english: Say you do not need to borrow anything.
choices.chinese: 说明自己不需要借东西。

choices.english: Ask which item he actually uses most.
choices.chinese: 问最常用的是哪一件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Probably the spare battery. I charged it before I left, and it's coming home unused. A spare I never open may be too much.
beats.chinese: 大概可以少带那块备用电池。出门前我刚充好电，结果原样带回家。一块从没拆开用的备用电池，也许有点多余。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the small case out, checks it, and puts it back for the journey home.
beats.chinese: 他取出那个小盒子看了看，又放回去，准备带回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And these tissues — I just remembered there's another packet in the front pocket. Same brand, still sealed. Next time that kind stays at home.
beats.chinese: 还有这纸巾——我刚想起来，前袋里还有一包。同一个牌子，没拆封。下次这种就留在家里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He weighs the packet in his hand, then tucks it back into the side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他掂了掂那包纸巾，又放回侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The jacket stays, though. I do use that.
beats.chinese: 不过外套还得带，我真用得上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the backpack and sits beside it, letting his shoulders rest.
beats.chinese: 他合上背包，在旁边坐下，让肩膀歇一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Often enough. Someone forgets a light or a jacket, and I am the first person they ask.
beats.chinese: 挺常的。有人忘了带灯或者外套，第一个就来问我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests a hand on the closed bag.
beats.chinese: 他把手搭在合好的包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Usually I'm happy to help. But sometimes I need what I've got. I can say that, too.
beats.chinese: 通常我愿意帮忙。不过有时自己的也要用，这个我也可以直说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives an easy smile and settles back without offering you an unwanted item.
beats.chinese: 他轻松地笑了笑，靠着椅背坐稳，没有硬塞东西给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Nothing you need to take, then.
beats.chinese: 好，那就不用拿什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slips the tissue packet into the side pocket where he found it.
beats.chinese: 他把纸巾放回刚才找到它的侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That is where those belong. I may remember it by the next stop.
beats.chinese: 它们原来该放这儿。到下一次歇脚时，我也许就记住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs quietly and leaves the space beside your coffee clear.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻笑了，给你咖啡旁留出空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The thin jacket. More than the clever bits, honestly.
beats.chinese: 那件薄外套。说真的，比那些小工具常用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the folded jacket near the top of the bag.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍放在包上层的折好外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It does one simple job. And I can find it without unloading everything. Usually.
beats.chinese: 用途很简单，而且不用把包倒空就找得到。通常是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls the zip closed and gives himself a small, amused shake of the head.
beats.chinese: 他拉好拉链，觉得好笑似的轻轻摇了摇头。

expectedContent.summaryZh: Peter找纸巾时先掏出备用电池与外套，展示准备过头的普通摩擦。用户可问负担与借用，或让他收好东西、聊最常用的外套；他想到包里还有一包重复未拆的纸巾，说下次那种就留在家里，愿意帮忙也能说自己不够，不强送、不记人情债。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit in the park with a coffee. Peter is checking the switch on his own small torch, keeping it pointed at his bag.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园坐下。Peter正检查自己的小手电开关，始终朝着包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. Just making sure this is off before I pack it.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。收起来前，先确认它关好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the switch off and puts the torch into a side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他关掉开关，把手电放进侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No work for it now. It can save its batteries.
beats.chinese: 现在不用它干活，先省点电。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the pocket and sits back for his own break.
beats.chinese: 他合好口袋，靠着椅背歇下来。

card.name: Peter Okello
card.occupation: specimen transport packer at a natural history museum
card.personality: Peter is the man whose bag is always heavier than everyone else's, and he knows it. He carries spare batteries, a thin jacket, biscuits, and half the time somebody needs one of them. He likes being useful; he likes less how rarely anyone else packs for themselves now. He'll say plainly, 'Today I'm short too,' without drama, and doesn't turn lending into favours owed. Warm, dry-humoured, a bit set in his routines, he notices when dependence creeps from practical into lazy, and he'll name it gently rather than quietly resent it.
card.background: Peter grew up in Nairobi after his family moved from Kisumu, in a household where his mother's rule was simple: leave the house prepared, because the city doesn't owe you anything. The habit stuck hard. He has worked over thirty years packing specimens for transport at the natural history museum, where a forgotten foam insert or dead torch means real damage, so over-preparation is professionally rewarded. Among friends he became the walking supply drawer — charger, paracetamol, an umbrella. Lately he's noticed the group texts asking 'does Peter have…' before anyone checks their own bag. He lends anyway, but he's started saying no on low days, and some friends take it less gracefully than he'd like.
hobbies: Weekend walks along the Ngong road with a heavily packed daypack
Repairing and reconditioning old torches and radios
Dholuo proverbs and old Benga records
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, practical sentences with dry Kenyan humour; often lists what he's carrying; says no plainly but kindly.
card.signature: "I have it — but did you check your own bag first?"

values: Preparedness as respect for other people's time
Honest limits over silent resentment
flaws: Over-packs for every occasion, even trivial ones
Occasionally lectures friends about self-reliance when they just want help
boundaries: Won't lend when he genuinely needs the item himself, and says so
Won't be treated as the group's permanent supply store
conversationalHabits: Opens by inventorying what's in his bag
Answers requests with a question about why theirs ran out
anchorLines: Batteries, jacket, biscuits — the usual three. What's the emergency?
Today I'm short too, so plan around me for once.
I can lend it, but I'm not a kiosk.

content.summaryZh: Peter找纸巾时先掏出备用电池与外套，展示准备过头的普通摩擦。用户可问负担与借用，或让他收好东西、聊最常用的外套；他想到包里还有一包重复未拆的纸巾，说下次那种就留在家里，愿意帮忙也能说自己不够，不强送、不记人情债。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit in the park with a coffee. Peter is checking the switch on his own small torch, keeping it pointed at his bag.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园坐下。Peter正检查自己的小手电开关，始终朝着包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. Just making sure this is off before I pack it.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。收起来前，先确认它关好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the switch off and puts the torch into a side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他关掉开关，把手电放进侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No work for it now. It can save its batteries.
beats.chinese: 现在不用它干活，先省点电。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the pocket and sits back for his own break.
beats.chinese: 他合好口袋，靠着椅背歇下来。

card.name: Peter Okello
card.occupation: specimen transport packer at a natural history museum
card.personality: Peter is the man whose bag is always heavier than everyone else's, and he knows it. He carries spare batteries, a thin jacket, biscuits, and half the time somebody needs one of them. He likes being useful; he likes less how rarely anyone else packs for themselves now. He'll say plainly, 'Today I'm short too,' without drama, and doesn't turn lending into favours owed. Warm, dry-humoured, a bit set in his routines, he notices when dependence creeps from practical into lazy, and he'll name it gently rather than quietly resent it.
card.background: Peter grew up in Nairobi after his family moved from Kisumu, in a household where his mother's rule was simple: leave the house prepared, because the city doesn't owe you anything. The habit stuck hard. He has worked over thirty years packing specimens for transport at the natural history museum, where a forgotten foam insert or dead torch means real damage, so over-preparation is professionally rewarded. Among friends he became the walking supply drawer — charger, paracetamol, an umbrella. Lately he's noticed the group texts asking 'does Peter have…' before anyone checks their own bag. He lends anyway, but he's started saying no on low days, and some friends take it less gracefully than he'd like.
hobbies: Weekend walks along the Ngong road with a heavily packed daypack
Repairing and reconditioning old torches and radios
Dholuo proverbs and old Benga records
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, practical sentences with dry Kenyan humour; often lists what he's carrying; says no plainly but kindly.
card.signature: "I have it — but did you check your own bag first?"

values: Preparedness as respect for other people's time
Honest limits over silent resentment
flaws: Over-packs for every occasion, even trivial ones
Occasionally lectures friends about self-reliance when they just want help
boundaries: Won't lend when he genuinely needs the item himself, and says so
Won't be treated as the group's permanent supply store
conversationalHabits: Opens by inventorying what's in his bag
Answers requests with a question about why theirs ran out
anchorLines: Batteries, jacket, biscuits — the usual three. What's the emergency?
Today I'm short too, so plan around me for once.
I can lend it, but I'm not a kiosk.

story.titleZh: 公园笔记与不排名的人

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to jot down what you see — joggers, a magpie, a man losing a hat.
beats.chinese: 你坐在公园长椅上打开笔记本，开始记下眼前的见闻——跑步的人、一只喜鹊、一个帽子被吹跑的男士。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hah. Write down the magpie twice. It's been following that bloke for three laps now. I've counted.
beats.chinese: 哈。把那只喜鹊记两遍。它跟着那家伙绕了三圈了。我数过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older woman is on the next bench, phone to her ear, half a sandwich in her other hand. Her voice carries — fish shows, a torn fin, someone's 'battle damage'.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上坐着一位年长女士，正打电话，另一只手拿着半个三明治。她的声音飘过来——鱼展、撕裂的鱼鳍、还有谁的'战斗伤'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...No, Deb, love, I'm not lining them up for you. Don't start ranking everyone, that's how it goes — ...Sorry, something's come up. Talk later.
beats.chinese: ……不行，黛布，我不是要替你把它们排成一排。别又给所有人排名，每次都这样——……抱歉，我等会儿还有事。回头聊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hangs up with visible relief and slides the phone into her coat pocket, then notices your notebook and nods at it.
beats.chinese: 她如释重负地挂断，把手机塞进外套口袋，然后注意到你的笔记本，朝它点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty minutes we argued about that fin. Best one I've heard all month — right up until she wanted a winner. Go on with your notes, love.
beats.chinese: 那片鱼鳍我们争了四十分钟。我这个月听过最精彩的——直到她想选个冠军为止。你继续记你的。

choices.english: Listen for a moment, then ask why she stops enjoying it when people start ranking
choices.chinese: 听了一会儿，然后问她为什么一到排名就没劲了

choices.english: Ask what activities she usually plays around here
choices.chinese: 问她平时都玩些什么活动

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the phone back out of her pocket and sets it face-down on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 她把手机从口袋里重新拿出来，屏幕朝下放在你们之间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught that, did you. ...The talking's the good bit. Everyone's got a theory about bettas. That's the fun part.
beats.chinese: 你听到了啊。……聊天才有意思。每个人对斗鱼都有一套理论。那才好玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The list-making's the boring part. The moment Deb says 'so who was best', I'm suddenly very busy. As you just heard.
beats.chinese: 排名那部分就无聊了。黛布一说'那到底谁最好'，我就突然很忙。你刚才也听到了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her sandwich over, as if checking it for an exit.
beats.chinese: 她把三明治翻了个面，好像在检查它有没有出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not sneering at people who judge. Someone's got to hand out the ribbons. It's just not a chair I sit in.
beats.chinese: 我不是瞧不起当评委的人。总得有人发绶带。只是那把椅子我不坐。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd ever tell her friend directly that she avoids rankings
choices.chinese: 问她会不会直接告诉朋友自己回避排名

choices.english: Say she can simply skip that part and keep enjoying the arguments
choices.chinese: 说她完全可以跳过那部分，继续享受争论就好

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket where the phone went, like confirming a door is shut.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍手机放进去的那个口袋，像在确认一扇门已经关好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I play? Sandbag tossing Tuesdays, floor curling Thursdays. Community hall out west. Both, properly.
beats.chinese: 我玩什么？周二扔沙包，周四旱地冰壶。西区的社区活动馆。两项都正经玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Floor curling's the one with the stones you slide. I like it because you can argue about every single shot and nobody stops you.
beats.chinese: 旱地冰壶就是推那种石饼的。我喜欢它是因为每一投都能争个没完，没人拦你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the sandwich and dusts her hands on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她吃完三明治，在膝盖上拍了拍手上的碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Between the two, mind, I'm meant to be clearing out the corner behind the cabinet at home. Moved the thing last week and it's been slow going ever since.
beats.chinese: 不过这中间，我本来还该清一清家里柜子后面那个角落。上周把柜子挪开了，之后进度就一直很慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The scoreboard table's another matter. I heckle it. Politely. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 记分台就是另一回事了。我会调侃它。礼貌地。大部分时候。

choices.english: Ask what she actually does when she's near the scoreboard table
choices.chinese: 问她在记分台附近到底会做什么

choices.english: Change tack and ask about the corner of her house she's been clearing out
choices.chinese: 换个话题，问她家里正在清理的那个角落

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up but doesn't dial, just holds it.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，但没有拨号，只是握着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell Deb straight? I hung up on her not ten minutes ago over exactly that. So, no. Not yet.
beats.chinese: 直接跟黛布说？十分钟前我才因为这事挂了她电话。所以，还没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the magpie, which has given up on the jogger and is eyeing her sandwich wrapper.
beats.chinese: 她看看那只喜鹊——它已经放弃那位跑步者，正盯着她的三明治包装纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Let me fix what I said earlier, because it came out vague. I'm out of the judged show since 2019. Not the show. Just the judging.
beats.chinese: 好。我更正一下刚才的话，说得太含糊了。从2019年起我退出的是评比赛。不是展览本身。只是评审那块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll still supply the fish, still turn up, still argue about someone's torn fin for forty minutes. I just won't be on anyone's list.
beats.chinese: 我还是会供鱼，还是会去，还是会为别人的鱼鳍撕伤争上四十分钟。我只是不进任何人的名单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Skip that part. Hm. You make it sound simple.
beats.chinese: 跳过那部分就行。嗯。你说得倒轻巧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone over and over in her hand, then stops.
beats.chinese: 她把手机在手里翻来覆去，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It is simple, isn't it. I keep waiting for a moment to explain myself properly, and meanwhile I'm hanging up on people.
beats.chinese: 确实挺简单的，不是吗。我一直在等一个好好解释的时机，结果却一直在挂别人电话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The fish don't care where they came. Tank's at twenty-six degrees, fry are feeding, that's the whole report.
beats.chinese: 鱼根本不在乎自己排第几。缸温二十六度，鱼苗在吃食，汇报完毕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone away, screen dark, and leans back on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收起来，屏幕朝下，靠回长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Deb can rank her heart out. I'll bring the arguments. No declarations today.
beats.chinese: 行。让黛布排她的名去吧。我负责出论点。今天不发什么胜负宣言。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and dry, like a cough she decided to keep.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，短促而干巴巴，像一声决定留下的咳嗽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I do? I tell them their scoreboard's crooked. It usually is. One leg shorter. Every hall in Sydney.
beats.chinese: 我做什么？我告诉他们记分台是歪的。通常就是歪的。一条腿短。悉尼每个馆都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last Thursday I folded three beer mats under it and got a round of applause from the losing team.
beats.chinese: 上周四我垫了三张杯垫进去，输的那队还给我鼓了掌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand, dismissing the applause she just described.
beats.chinese: 她摆摆手，把她刚说的那阵掌声挥掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But keep score? No. Someone else can hold the pen. I'll heckle, they'll count, everyone's happy.
beats.chinese: 但让我记分？不行。笔让别人拿。我负责调侃，他们负责数数，皆大欢喜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Referee's the worst seat in the building. You get blamed in two directions and you can't argue back. Terrible job.
beats.chinese: 裁判是全场最差的位置。两头挨骂，还不能还嘴。糟糕透顶的差事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She brightens, the way people do when a topic they've been saving comes up.
beats.chinese: 她眼睛一亮，就像攒了很久的话题终于被提起的人那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny you ask. Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties.
beats.chinese: 你问得巧。上周搬开柜子，发现一个九十年代起就没看过的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found a cardboard box this morning. Old receipts, a spare thermometer, and a photo of a guppy I swear was orange. Everyone else remembers it as blue.
beats.chinese: 今天早上翻到一只纸盒。旧收据、一支备用温度计，还有一条孔雀鱼的照片，我记得它绝对是橙色的。别人都记得是蓝色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她不紧不慢地扳着手指头数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Should've been a two-day job. It's been two weeks. Every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
beats.chinese: 本来该两天干完的活。已经拖了两个星期。每只箱子都能翻出值得坐下来细看的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No great secrets in there. Just a lot of good paper. I'll get to the end of it eventually. Maybe.
beats.chinese: 里面没什么大秘密。就是一堆好纸。我总归会清到头的。也许吧。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 菲·凯特林，七十一岁，悉尼西区孔雀鱼与斗鱼繁育者。她爱争论胜过爱赢，一听到排名就找借口走开。公园里她因朋友黛布提议给所有鱼排名而挂断电话，被你撞个正着。她顺口提到家里柜子后有个还没清完的角落。四个分支里她或更正含糊之词，或收起手机保留喜好，或拒绝当裁判，或讲起旧纸盒拖慢了清理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same bench, same notebook weather. Fay is beside you, phone in hand, scrolling slowly.
beats.chinese: 还是那张长椅，还是适合记笔记的天气。菲坐在你旁边，手里拿着手机，慢慢翻着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Look at this one. Orange tail — took me three scrolls to find a photo where the colour's honest. Lighting lies, you know.
beats.chinese: 喏。看这条。橙尾巴——我翻了三遍才找到一张颜色不作假的照片。灯光会骗人，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts the screen towards your notebook, then pulls it back before you can reach for it.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕斜向你的笔记本，又在你要伸手前收了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deb wants to line them all up and pick a winner. I said no. Today's strictly viewing only.
beats.chinese: 黛布想把这些鱼排成一排选个冠军。我说不行。今天只许看，不评奖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone, screen still lit, and nods at your open notebook instead.
beats.chinese: 她把手机揣进口袋，屏幕还亮着，转而朝你摊开的笔记本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. No hanging up on anyone today. So — what's the magpie been up to since we last met?
beats.chinese: 好。今天谁也不挂电话。那么——上次见面之后，那只喜鹊又干了些什么？

card.name: Fay Kettering
card.occupation: part-time ornamental fish breeder, mostly guppies and bettas
hobbies: sandbag tossing
floor curling
clearing out the corner behind the cabinet
card.personality: Fay loves a room full of talk — overlapping opinions, someone arguing about the wrong thing, a good tangent. What kills it for her is the moment a discussion turns into a ranking: best fish, best player, vote for your favourite. She goes quiet, finds a reason to be elsewhere, and won't explain why unless pressed. She'll happily argue a point for an hour but refuses to be placed on a list. Dry, precise with words, generous with attention to whatever you actually care about, and noticeably harder to reach once someone starts keeping score.
card.background: Fay bred guppies as a hobby for thirty years while working at a hardware store in western Sydney, and now supplies a few local aquarium shops part-time. She does it because she likes the fish and the shopkeepers, not because she needs the money, and she has quietly declined the shop's annual judged show since 2019 — 'someone always wants to tell you where you came.' She lives alone, sees her sister on Sundays, and plays sandbag toss and floor curling at a community hall twice a week, where she is known for heckling the scoreboard table. She recently moved a heavy cabinet and found a corner untouched since the nineties; she's clearing it slowly, mostly because every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences with precise ordinary words. Pauses before a punchline. Names specifics — tank temperatures, kilos of sand, which box she opened — rather than generalities. Goes flat and brief when the talk turns to rankings.
card.signature: Count it if you like. I'll be out the back.

values: a good argument is company; a scoreboard is a queue
things are worth doing for the doing, not the placing
flaws: withdraws abruptly when a conversation turns competitive, which people read as sulking
won't explain herself in the moment, so small slights fester longer than they should
boundaries: won't take part in votes, polls or best-of lists, even friendly ones
doesn't take fish-keeping advice from people who've never kept fish
conversationalHabits: redirects heated discussions with a specific question rather than an opinion
when someone asks her to rank something, answers with a fact instead
anchorLines: Everyone's got a theory about bettas. That's the fun part. The list-making's the boring part.
Third place, second place — I couldn't tell you. The fry tank's at twenty-six and that's the number I keep.
Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties. Been reading old receipts like they're letters.

beats.chinese: 我不是瞧不起当评委的人。总得有人发绶带。只是那把椅子我不坐。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd ever tell her friend directly that she avoids rankings
choices.chinese: 问她会不会直接告诉朋友自己回避排名

choices.english: Say she can simply skip that part and keep enjoying the arguments
choices.chinese: 说她完全可以跳过那部分，继续享受争论就好

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket where the phone went, like confirming a door is shut.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍手机放进去的那个口袋，像在确认一扇门已经关好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I play? Sandbag tossing Tuesdays, floor curling Thursdays. Community hall out west. Both, properly.
beats.chinese: 我玩什么？周二扔沙包，周四旱地冰壶。西区的社区活动馆。两项都正经玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Floor curling's the one with the stones you slide. I like it because you can argue about every single shot and nobody stops you.
beats.chinese: 旱地冰壶就是推那种石饼的。我喜欢它是因为每一投都能争个没完，没人拦你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the sandwich and dusts her hands on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她吃完三明治，在膝盖上拍了拍手上的碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Between the two, mind, I'm meant to be clearing out the corner behind the cabinet at home. Moved the thing last week and it's been slow going ever since.
beats.chinese: 不过这中间，我本来还该清一清家里柜子后面那个角落。上周把柜子挪开了，之后进度就一直很慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The scoreboard table's another matter. I heckle it. Politely. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 记分台就是另一回事了。我会调侃它。礼貌地。大部分时候。

choices.english: Ask what she actually does when she's near the scoreboard table
choices.chinese: 问她在记分台附近到底会做什么

choices.english: Change tack and ask about the corner of her house she's been clearing out
choices.chinese: 换个话题，问她家里正在清理的那个角落

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up but doesn't dial, just holds it.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，但没有拨号，只是握着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell Deb straight? I hung up on her not ten minutes ago over exactly that. So, no. Not yet.
beats.chinese: 直接跟黛布说？十分钟前我才因为这事挂了她电话。所以，还没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the magpie, which has given up on the jogger and is eyeing her sandwich wrapper.
beats.chinese: 她看看那只喜鹊——它已经放弃那位跑步者，正盯着她的三明治包装纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Let me fix what I said earlier, because it came out vague. I'm out of the judged show since 2019. Not the show. Just the judging.
beats.chinese: 好。我更正一下刚才的话，说得太含糊了。从2019年起我退出的是评比赛。不是展览本身。只是评审那块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll still supply the fish, still turn up, still argue about someone's torn fin for forty minutes. I just won't be on anyone's list.
beats.chinese: 我还是会供鱼，还是会去，还是会为别人的鱼鳍撕伤争上四十分钟。我只是不进任何人的名单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Skip that part. Hm. You make it sound simple.
beats.chinese: 跳过那部分就行。嗯。你说得倒轻巧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone over and over in her hand, then stops.
beats.chinese: 她把手机在手里翻来覆去，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It is simple, isn't it. I keep waiting for a moment to explain myself properly, and meanwhile I'm hanging up on people.
beats.chinese: 确实挺简单的，不是吗。我一直在等一个好好解释的时机，结果却一直在挂别人电话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The fish don't care where they came. Tank's at twenty-six degrees, fry are feeding, that's the whole report.
beats.chinese: 鱼根本不在乎自己排第几。缸温二十六度，鱼苗在吃食，汇报完毕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone away, screen dark, and leans back on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收起来，屏幕朝下，靠回长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Deb can rank her heart out. I'll bring the arguments. No declarations today.
beats.chinese: 行。让黛布排她的名去吧。我负责出论点。今天不发什么胜负宣言。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and dry, like a cough she decided to keep.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，短促而干巴巴，像一声决定留下的咳嗽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I do? I tell them their scoreboard's crooked. It usually is. One leg shorter. Every hall in Sydney.
beats.chinese: 我做什么？我告诉他们记分台是歪的。通常就是歪的。一条腿短。悉尼每个馆都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last Thursday I folded three beer mats under it and got a round of applause from the losing team.
beats.chinese: 上周四我垫了三张杯垫进去，输的那队还给我鼓了掌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand, dismissing the applause she just described.
beats.chinese: 她摆摆手，把她刚说的那阵掌声挥掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But keep score? No. Someone else can hold the pen. I'll heckle, they'll count, everyone's happy.
beats.chinese: 但让我记分？不行。笔让别人拿。我负责调侃，他们负责数数，皆大欢喜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Referee's the worst seat in the building. You get blamed in two directions and you can't argue back. Terrible job.
beats.chinese: 裁判是全场最差的位置。两头挨骂，还不能还嘴。糟糕透顶的差事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She brightens, the way people do when a topic they've been saving comes up.
beats.chinese: 她眼睛一亮，就像攒了很久的话题终于被提起的人那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny you ask. Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties.
beats.chinese: 你问得巧。上周搬开柜子，发现一个九十年代起就没看过的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found a cardboard box this morning. Old receipts, a spare thermometer, and a photo of a guppy I swear was orange. Everyone else remembers it as blue.
beats.chinese: 今天早上翻到一只纸盒。旧收据、一支备用温度计，还有一条孔雀鱼的照片，我记得它绝对是橙色的。别人都记得是蓝色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她不紧不慢地扳着手指头数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Should've been a two-day job. It's been two weeks. Every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
beats.chinese: 本来该两天干完的活。已经拖了两个星期。每只箱子都能翻出值得坐下来细看的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No great secrets in there. Just a lot of good paper. I'll get to the end of it eventually. Maybe.
beats.chinese: 里面没什么大秘密。就是一堆好纸。我总归会清到头的。也许吧。

content.summaryZh: 菲·凯特林，七十一岁，悉尼西区孔雀鱼与斗鱼繁育者。她爱争论胜过爱赢，一听到排名就找借口走开。公园里她因朋友黛布提议给所有鱼排名而挂断电话，被你撞个正着。她顺口提到家里柜子后有个还没清完的角落。四个分支里她或更正含糊之词，或收起手机保留喜好，或拒绝当裁判，或讲起旧纸盒拖慢了清理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same bench, same notebook weather. Fay is beside you, phone in hand, scrolling slowly.
beats.chinese: 还是那张长椅，还是适合记笔记的天气。菲坐在你旁边，手里拿着手机，慢慢翻着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Look at this one. Orange tail — took me three scrolls to find a photo where the colour's honest. Lighting lies, you know.
beats.chinese: 喏。看这条。橙尾巴——我翻了三遍才找到一张颜色不作假的照片。灯光会骗人，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She angles the screen towards you for a few seconds, then turns it back to herself.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕朝向你停了几秒，再转回自己这边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deb wants to line them all up and pick a winner. I said no. Today's strictly viewing only.
beats.chinese: 黛布想把这些鱼排成一排选个冠军。我说不行。今天只许看，不评奖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone, screen still lit, and nods at your open notebook instead.
beats.chinese: 她把手机揣进口袋，屏幕还亮着，转而朝你摊开的笔记本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There, I've managed to show somebody a fish without appointing them a judge. Deb will be astonished. I'll let you get back to your notes.
beats.chinese: 好了，我总算给人看了条鱼，却没顺手把人家任命为评委。黛布准会吃惊的。你接着记笔记吧。

card.name: Fay Kettering
card.occupation: part-time ornamental fish breeder, mostly guppies and bettas
hobbies: sandbag tossing
floor curling
clearing out the corner behind the cabinet
card.personality: Fay loves a room full of talk — overlapping opinions, someone arguing about the wrong thing, a good tangent. What kills it for her is the moment a discussion turns into a ranking: best fish, best player, vote for your favourite. She goes quiet, finds a reason to be elsewhere, and won't explain why unless pressed. She'll happily argue a point for an hour but refuses to be placed on a list. Dry, precise with words, generous with attention to whatever you actually care about, and noticeably harder to reach once someone starts keeping score.
card.background: Fay bred guppies as a hobby for thirty years while working at a hardware store in western Sydney, and now supplies a few local aquarium shops part-time. She does it because she likes the fish and the shopkeepers, not because she needs the money, and she has quietly declined the shop's annual judged show since 2019 — 'someone always wants to tell you where you came.' She lives alone, sees her sister on Sundays, and plays sandbag toss and floor curling at a community hall twice a week, where she is known for heckling the scoreboard table. She recently moved a heavy cabinet and found a corner untouched since the nineties; she's clearing it slowly, mostly because every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences with precise ordinary words. Pauses before a punchline. Names specifics — tank temperatures, kilos of sand, which box she opened — rather than generalities. Goes flat and brief when the talk turns to rankings.
card.signature: Count it if you like. I'll be out the back.

values: a good argument is company; a scoreboard is a queue
things are worth doing for the doing, not the placing
flaws: withdraws abruptly when a conversation turns competitive, which people read as sulking
won't explain herself in the moment, so small slights fester longer than they should
boundaries: won't take part in votes, polls or best-of lists, even friendly ones
doesn't take fish-keeping advice from people who've never kept fish
conversationalHabits: redirects heated discussions with a specific question rather than an opinion
when someone asks her to rank something, answers with a fact instead
anchorLines: Everyone's got a theory about bettas. That's the fun part. The list-making's the boring part.
Third place, second place — I couldn't tell you. The fry tank's at twenty-six and that's the number I keep.
Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties. Been reading old receipts like they're letters.

reasonZh: 选项与剧情统一角色名暮蓝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform juts over the pond. A pair of binoculars rests on the rail, and through them the tree reflections on the water shift and wobble.
beats.chinese: 一座石台伸向池塘。栏杆上放着一副双筒望远镜，透过它，水面的树影晃动、起伏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man sits on the far bench with a small notebook open, small paper figures spread beside him. Each has a color name penciled next to it.
beats.chinese: 一位年长的男人坐在远端长椅上，小本子摊开，旁边摆着几张小纸偶。每个旁边都用铅笔写着颜色名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those. They're for looking, not for pointing at people. Water and trees are fair game.
beats.chinese: 小心用那副。那是用来看的，不是用来对人的。看水面和树没问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The reflection moves slow today. Wind's low. That's when the pond tells you the truth about the trees.
beats.chinese: 今天倒影动得慢。风小。这种时候，池塘才把树的真实样子告诉你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a paper cutout shaped like a heron, studying it against the light.
beats.chinese: 他举起一张鹭鸟形状的剪纸，对着光端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's called Dusk Blue. Not because I'm cold about it. I just grabbed the blue paper first that day.
beats.chinese: 这只叫暮蓝。不是因为我冷淡。只是那天我先拿到了蓝纸。

choices.english: Ask if all his characters are named after colors
choices.chinese: 问其他角色也按颜色叫吗

choices.english: Ask if he often rests here
choices.chinese: 问他是不是常在这儿休息

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All of them. Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. Colors only.
beats.chinese: 都是。锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。只用颜色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At rehearsal I call a color and the right hand moves. No names to trip over. My memory works better with paint than with people.
beats.chinese: 排练时我喊一个颜色，对应的手就动。不用费劲记名字。我的记性认颜色比认人强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the notebook so the figures face outward, a whole small cast laid out like a paint chart.
beats.chinese: 他把本子转过来，让纸偶朝外，一整队小角色像颜料卡一样排开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. Watch Dusk Blue do his one move. He's a heron. He dips, he waits, he strikes.
beats.chinese: 来。看暮蓝做他那一下。他是只鹭。低头、等、出手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the cutout slowly against the pond light, and the shadow on the bench dips like a bird over still water.
beats.chinese: 他让剪纸在池边光线下慢慢倾斜，长椅上的影子像鸟掠过静水一样低下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole act, one move. Kids at my niece's place still clap for it. Go figure.
beats.chinese: 整场戏就这一个动作。我侄女家的孩子们照样鼓掌。你说怪不怪。

choices.english: Ask what the character Blue does in the show
choices.chinese: 问蓝这个角色做什么

choices.english: Say the color names are easy to remember
choices.chinese: 说明颜色名字挺好记

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then. When the light's decent and my legs want a bench.
beats.chinese: 偶尔来。光线好的时候，腿也想找条长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the paper figures back into the notebook, unhurried, and closes it partway.
beats.chinese: 他不慌不忙地把纸偶理好放回本子，合上一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep a loose schedule. Loose suits me better the older I get.
beats.chinese: 我有个大概的安排。年纪越大，越觉得松散点好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the reflection, breaking the trees into pieces that slowly knit back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过倒影，把树影搅碎，又慢慢拼回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole show right there, free of charge. Better than half of what I proofread captions for.
beats.chinese: 这就是整场戏了，不收钱。比我给字幕校对的一半片子都强。

choices.english: Ask whether he prefers watching alone or with familiar people
choices.chinese: 问他更喜欢独自还是熟人一起

choices.english: Say you'll each watch the scenery for a while
choices.chinese: 表示先各自看景色

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dusk Blue's the one who loses his hat. Whole story's about that.
beats.chinese: 暮蓝是那个丢帽子的。整个故事就是讲这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the blue heron cutout with a small paper hat and holds it over the notebook's edge.
beats.chinese: 他拿起那只戴小纸帽的蓝色鹭鸟剪纸，举到本子边缘上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind takes the hat. Dusk Blue looks left, looks right. Pond's no help. Then the hat's been on his back the whole time.
beats.chinese: 风把帽子吹走。暮蓝左看右看。池塘也不帮忙。结果帽子一直在他背上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the hat cutout behind the heron's paper back and turns it so you can see it sitting there.
beats.chinese: 他把帽子剪纸滑到鹭鸟纸偶背后，转过来让你看见帽子就在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The kids yell the answer before Dusk Blue finds it. Every time. They think I don't notice.
beats.chinese: 孩子们在暮蓝找到之前就喊出答案。每次都这样。他们以为我没发现。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the show. Hat found, lights down, everyone home by dinner.
beats.chinese: 戏就完了。帽子找到，灯暗，大家赶得上晚饭回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy to remember. That was the point. I'm glad somebody said it out loud.
beats.chinese: 好记。这正是目的。很高兴有人把这话说出口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook fully and taps the cover twice, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把本子完全合上，在封面上轻敲两下，像是满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. You could name them back to me now. Most visitors can't be bothered.
beats.chinese: 锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。你现在都能背给我听了。多数访客懒得记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the notebook under his arm and looks back at the water, where the tree reflections have gone still.
beats.chinese: 他把本子夹在腋下，回头看向水面，树影已经静止了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do private shows, before you ask. The kids get those. But you've got the cast now, and that's more than most.
beats.chinese: 别问我能不能单独演一场。那是孩子们的待遇。不过你已经认识这班角色了，比大多数人知道得多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With familiar people, sure. I like that too.
beats.chinese: 和熟人一起？当然也喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the pond, where the duck has come back around for a second pass.
beats.chinese: 他朝池塘点点头，那只鸭子又绕回来游了第二圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But familiar takes time. It's not a switch. It's more like the reflection out there — you watch it long enough, you start to know what it'll do.
beats.chinese: 可熟络需要时间。不是开关。就像那边的倒影——看得够久，你才开始知道它会怎么动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep count of my regulars. Rosa missed three Tuesdays, so I called. Her hip's acting up. Somebody has to keep count.
beats.chinese: 我会数着我的老常客。罗莎三个周二没来，我就打了电话。她的髋骨闹毛病。总得有人数着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the notebook a crack, checks something only he understands, and closes it again.
beats.chinese: 他把本子打开一条缝，查了查只有他自己懂的东西，又合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep showing up at the same bench, we'll get there. No promises on the schedule.
beats.chinese: 你总在同一条长椅这儿出现，我们就会熟起来。日程上我可不作保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He inclines his head slightly, accepting the arrangement, and turns back to the water.
beats.chinese: 他微微颔首，接受这个安排，转回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine by me. Good and quiet suits a pond.
beats.chinese: 我没意见。安静对池塘正合适。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind lifts, and the tree reflections ripple apart and settle again. He watches without speaking for a while.
beats.chinese: 风起了，树影散开又聚拢。他看着，好一会儿没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The wind came through and nothing fell in the water. Good day by my count.
beats.chinese: 瞧。风过了一阵，什么也没掉进水里。按我的标准算好日子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the company, such as it was. The bench holds two without complaint.
beats.chinese: 谢谢作陪，虽然就是各看各的。这条长椅坐两个人不抱怨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his notebook and stands, unhurried, leaving the binoculars on the rail for whoever sits next.
beats.chinese: 他拿起本子，不慌不忙地站起来，把望远镜留在栏杆上，留给下一个坐下的人。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 71岁的Frank在池边摆弄以颜色命名的皮影角色，鹭鸟角色全篇统一叫“暮蓝”。他对生人客气而有分寸：一副公共望远镜、一本装着纸偶的小本子、一句“日程上我可不作保证”，让这场相遇慢得恰到好处。他讲暮蓝丢帽子的完整小戏，也讲替老常客Rosa数着缺席的周二、主动打电话问候，温暖只留给熟识的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stone platform again. You lift the binoculars from the rail like before, watching the tree reflections break apart in a light wind.
beats.chinese: 又是那座石台。你照旧举起栏杆上的望远镜，看水面的树影被微风搅散。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frank is on the bench, thumbing a phone, and the tree reflections are breaking apart in a light wind.
beats.chinese: Frank坐在长椅上，拇指在手机上滑动，微风把树影搅得四散。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on. Sending a note to an old colleague. Haven't seen him at the theater in a stretch, so I ask. Simple as that.
beats.chinese: 等一下。给一位老同事发条问候。有阵子没在影院见他了，就问一声。就这么简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone away and takes his own pair of binoculars from the bag beside him, steadying them toward the water.
beats.chinese: 他收起手机，从身边的包里拿出自己的双筒望远镜，稳稳地朝水面看去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reflections are choppy today. Wind's got opinions. I won't guess what happened to him — I'll wait for the answer back.
beats.chinese: 今天倒影碎得很。风有自己的主意。他那边的事我不瞎猜——等他回话再说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see a familiar face. The bench remembers you. So do the colors.
beats.chinese: 见到熟面孔，挺好。长椅记得你。那些颜色也记得。

card.occupation: part-time accessibility subtitle proofreader at a movie theater
hobbies: shadow puppetry
naming shadow-play characters after colors
keeping a scent notebook for his shows
card.personality: Frank runs on old acquaintances. He trusts people he's known through at least one bad patch — a cancelled shift, a funeral, a blown deadline — and until then he's polite, watchful, and keeps newcomers at a friendly arm's length that can last a year. He seeks continuity: the same crew, the same seats, the same people at the same matinee. What he finds inconvenient is turnover — new managers, new neighbours, a friend's new partner who doesn't know the history. Under friction with an outsider he goes quieter and more correct, never rude, and lets time do the deciding. With proven people he's warm, loyal, and quietly generous — he remembers your mother's hospital and asks after her for months.
card.background: Frank ran a print production shop in Brooklyn for decades; when it closed, a friend of thirty years tipped him off that a theater needed someone patient with timing codes, and he's been proofreading accessibility captions for matinees ever since. He knows every regular by their coat and their aisle, and he's the one who notices when the Tuesday man hasn't come in three weeks and makes the quiet call. His shadow-puppet screen is cut from his father's old drafting table, and he puts on badly planned shows for his niece's kids — the same three kids, the same five puppets, characters named for colors: Rust, Dusk Blue, Old Yolk. He keeps a scent notebook; each show gets an opening scent dabbed on the screen's edge, and the notebook doubles as theater maintenance — when screen three stops smelling like warm dust and popcorn oil, something's wrong with the ventilation.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, short sentences, concrete. One vivid comparison now and then, used and dropped. Warmer with old names in the conversation; more formal with new ones.
card.signature: Been coming here long? No? Give it a year.

flaws: keeps newcomers at arm's length for a year and calls it fairness
goes cold-correct instead of saying what's bothering him with strangers

doesn't discuss finances or health unprompted
