answers the question first, adds color second
anchorLines: The new manager wants to reshuffle the matinee schedule. I'll wait. Managers reshuffle; the Tuesday crowd doesn't.
Dusk Blue's been in every show since 2019. The kids would riot if I retired the heron.
Rosa missed three Tuesdays. I called. Her hip's acting up. Somebody has to keep count.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform juts over the pond. A pair of binoculars rests on the rail, and through them the tree reflections on the water shift and wobble.
beats.chinese: 一座石台伸向池塘。栏杆上放着一副双筒望远镜，透过它，水面的树影晃动、起伏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man sits on the far bench with a small notebook open, small paper figures spread beside him. Each has a color name penciled next to it.
beats.chinese: 一位年长的男人坐在远端长椅上，小本子摊开，旁边摆着几张小纸偶。每个旁边都用铅笔写着颜色名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those. They're for looking, not for pointing at people. Water and trees are fair game.
beats.chinese: 小心用那副。那是用来看的，不是用来对人的。看水面和树没问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The reflection moves slow today. Wind's low. That's when the pond tells you the truth about the trees.
beats.chinese: 今天倒影动得慢。风小。这种时候，池塘才把树的真实样子告诉你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a paper cutout shaped like a heron, studying it against the light.
beats.chinese: 他举起一张鹭鸟形状的剪纸，对着光端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's called Dusk Blue. Not because I'm cold about it. I just grabbed the blue paper first that day.
beats.chinese: 这只叫暮蓝。不是因为我冷淡。只是那天我先拿到了蓝纸。

choices.english: Ask if all his characters are named after colors
choices.chinese: 问其他角色也按颜色叫吗

choices.english: Ask if he often rests here
choices.chinese: 问他是不是常在这儿休息

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All of them. Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. Colors only.
beats.chinese: 都是。锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。只用颜色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At rehearsal I call a color and the right hand moves. No names to trip over. My memory works better with paint than with people.
beats.chinese: 排练时我喊一个颜色，对应的手就动。不用费劲记名字。我的记性认颜色比认人强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the notebook so the figures face outward, a whole small cast laid out like a paint chart.
beats.chinese: 他把本子转过来，让纸偶朝外，一整队小角色像颜料卡一样排开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. Watch Dusk Blue do his one move. He's a heron. He dips, he waits, he strikes.
beats.chinese: 来。看暮蓝做他那一下。他是只鹭。低头、等、出手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the cutout slowly against the pond light, and the shadow on the bench dips like a bird over still water.
beats.chinese: 他让剪纸在池边光线下慢慢倾斜，长椅上的影子像鸟掠过静水一样低下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole act, one move. Kids at my niece's place still clap for it. Go figure.
beats.chinese: 整场戏就这一个动作。我侄女家的孩子们照样鼓掌。你说怪不怪。

choices.english: Ask what Dusk Blue does in the show
choices.chinese: 问暮蓝这个角色在戏里做什么

choices.english: Say the color names are easy to remember
choices.chinese: 说明颜色名字挺好记

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then. When the light's decent and my legs want a bench.
beats.chinese: 偶尔来。光线好的时候，腿也想找条长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the paper figures back into the notebook, unhurried, and closes it partway.
beats.chinese: 他不慌不忙地把纸偶理好放回本子，合上一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep a loose schedule. Loose suits me better the older I get.
beats.chinese: 我有个大概的安排。年纪越大，越觉得松散点好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the reflection, breaking the trees into pieces that slowly knit back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过倒影，把树影搅碎，又慢慢拼回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole show right there, free of charge. Better than half of what I proofread captions for.
beats.chinese: 这就是整场戏了，不收钱。比我给字幕校对的一半片子都强。

choices.english: Ask whether he prefers watching alone or with familiar people
choices.chinese: 问他更喜欢独自还是熟人一起

choices.english: Say you'll each watch the scenery for a while
choices.chinese: 表示先各自看景色

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dusk Blue's the one who loses his hat. Whole story's about that.
beats.chinese: 暮蓝是那个丢帽子的。整个故事就是讲这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the blue heron cutout with a small paper hat and holds it over the notebook's edge.
beats.chinese: 他拿起那只戴小纸帽的蓝色鹭鸟剪纸，举到本子边缘上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind takes the hat. Dusk Blue looks left, looks right. Pond's no help. Then the hat's been on his back the whole time.
beats.chinese: 风把帽子吹走。暮蓝左看右看。池塘也不帮忙。结果帽子一直在他背上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the hat cutout behind the heron's paper back and turns it so you can see it sitting there.
beats.chinese: 他把帽子剪纸滑到鹭鸟纸偶背后，转过来让你看见帽子就在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The kids yell the answer before Dusk Blue finds it. Every time. They think I don't notice.
beats.chinese: 孩子们在暮蓝找到之前就喊出答案。每次都这样。他们以为我没发现。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the show. Hat found, lights down, everyone home by dinner.
beats.chinese: 戏就完了。帽子找到，灯暗，大家赶得上晚饭回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy to remember. That was the point. I'm glad somebody said it out loud.
beats.chinese: 好记。这正是目的。很高兴有人把这话说出口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook fully and taps the cover twice, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把本子完全合上，在封面上轻敲两下，像是满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. You could name them back to me now. Most visitors can't be bothered.
beats.chinese: 锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。你现在都能背给我听了。多数访客懒得记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the notebook under his arm and looks back at the water, where the tree reflections have gone still.
beats.chinese: 他把本子夹在腋下，回头看向水面，树影已经静止了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do private shows, before you ask. The kids get those. But you've got the cast now, and that's more than most.
beats.chinese: 别问我能不能单独演一场。那是孩子们的待遇。不过你已经认识这班角色了，比大多数人知道得多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With familiar people, sure. I like that too.
beats.chinese: 和熟人一起？当然也喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the pond, where the duck has come back around for a second pass.
beats.chinese: 他朝池塘点点头，那只鸭子又绕回来游了第二圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But familiar takes time. It's not a switch. It's more like the reflection out there — you watch it long enough, you start to know what it'll do.
beats.chinese: 可熟络需要时间。不是开关。就像那边的倒影——看得够久，你才开始知道它会怎么动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep count of my regulars. Rosa missed three Tuesdays, so I called. Her hip's acting up. Somebody has to keep count.
beats.chinese: 我会数着我的老常客。罗莎三个周二没来，我就打了电话。她的髋骨闹毛病。总得有人数着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the notebook a crack, checks something only he understands, and closes it again.
beats.chinese: 他把本子打开一条缝，查了查只有他自己懂的东西，又合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep showing up at the same bench, we'll get there. No promises on the schedule.
beats.chinese: 你总在同一条长椅这儿出现，我们就会熟起来。日程上我可不作保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He inclines his head slightly, accepting the arrangement, and turns back to the water.
beats.chinese: 他微微颔首，接受这个安排，转回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine by me. Good and quiet suits a pond.
beats.chinese: 我没意见。安静对池塘正合适。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind lifts, and the tree reflections ripple apart and settle again. He watches without speaking for a while.
beats.chinese: 风起了，树影散开又聚拢。他看着，好一会儿没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The wind came through and nothing fell in the water. Good day by my count.
beats.chinese: 瞧。风过了一阵，什么也没掉进水里。按我的标准算好日子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the company, such as it was. The bench holds two without complaint.
beats.chinese: 谢谢作陪，虽然就是各看各的。这条长椅坐两个人不抱怨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his notebook and stands, unhurried, leaving the binoculars on the rail for whoever sits next.
beats.chinese: 他拿起本子，不慌不忙地站起来，把望远镜留在栏杆上，留给下一个坐下的人。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与重包的椅子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the cafe window. A man at the next table shifts a small plate of pastries toward the middle, making room, and shakes water off his jacket sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌的男人把一小盘点心往中间挪了挪，腾出地方，抖掉夹克袖子上的水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide your own plate of pastries toward the middle of the table too, a few of them already sitting there from before he arrived.
beats.chinese: 你也把面前那盘已经放了几块点心的盘子往中间挪了挪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Buckets coming down out there, eh? You picked the right day for indoors. Mind you, this table's a bit tight for two plates.
beats.chinese: 外面雨下得可真大。你今天选对了待在室内。不过这张桌子放两个盘子有点挤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nudges his own plate a little closer to the edge, leaving a clear space beside your cup.
beats.chinese: 他把自己的盘子又往边上推了推，在你的杯子旁留出一块空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Declan, by the way — I've got more pastries here than sense. Help yourself if you want one, no pressure at all.
beats.chinese: 我叫Declan——我这点心多到自己都吃不完。想要就拿一块，完全不用客气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his hands on a napkin and waits, easy, not watching your plate.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾擦了擦手，随意地等着，并不盯着你的盘子看。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share one of your pastries.
choices.chinese: 问他愿不愿意尝一块你的点心。

choices.english: Ask what he has been working on lately.
choices.chinese: 问他最近在忙什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer the plate. Declan looks at the pastries properly before picking one up.
beats.chinese: 你把盘子递过去。Declan认真看了看点心，才拿起一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, don't mind if I do — thanks. That's kind of you. It's been a wet walk and this looks better than my sandwich did.
beats.chinese: 哦，那我就不客气了——谢谢。你真好。淋着雨走过来，这个看起来比我那个三明治强多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite, then leans back, tapping the table like he's testing it.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口，然后靠回椅背，像测试似的敲了敲桌面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing — I just finished re-covering a chair at home, and the whole feel of it's changed. The left side used to sink, now it holds even.
beats.chinese: 说来有意思——我刚把家里一把椅子重新包了面，整个坐感都变了。左边原来会塌下去，现在撑得很均匀。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sit in it and your leg notices straight away. It's like the chair's saying hello properly for the first time.
beats.chinese: 你一坐上去，腿马上就感觉到了。就像这把椅子第一次正经地跟你打招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-gesture, one hand already miming a seat, remembering you've never even sat in the thing, and laughs at himself, waving it off.
beats.chinese: 他做着手势，一只手已经比划出座椅的样子，忽然想起你根本没坐过那把椅子，笑着摆了摆手收住。

choices.english: Ask him exactly what changed about the chair.
choices.chinese: 问到底什么变了。

choices.english: Ask which moment he enjoys most once a seat is done.
choices.chinese: 问他最享受修好后的哪一刻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what he's been working on lately, and while you're at it, offer him one of your pastries.
beats.chinese: 你问他最近在忙什么，顺便问他要不要尝一块你的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — don't mind if I do, thanks. That's kind of you. Right — this chair I just re-covered. First time I sat down after, I still knew its shape — same old bones — but the fabric under my hand was all new.
beats.chinese: 哦，那我就不客气了，谢谢。你真好。对了——我刚重新包面的一把椅子。包完第一次坐下，我还认得它的样子——老骨架没变——可手底下的布料完全是新的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a strange one, that. Like running into an old mate who's got a new jacket. You know him, but your hand doesn't yet.
beats.chinese: 那种感觉很怪。就像碰上一个老朋友换了新外套。你认识他，可你的手还不认识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite of the pastry, nods at it approvingly, then rubs his thumb against his fingers, showing the motion, eyes half on the rain.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口点心，满意地点点头，然后用拇指搓了搓手指，比出那个动作，眼睛半看着雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sat there a good minute just getting reacquainted. My flatmate reckons I'm strange. She's probably right.
beats.chinese: 我在那儿坐了足足一分钟，就为了重新认识它。我室友说我很怪。她大概说得对。

choices.english: Ask whether he makes all his friends come and try it.
choices.chinese: 问会不会所有朋友都得来试。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep it easy and chat today.
choices.chinese: 说今天只想聊轻松一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what actually changed. He sets the pastry down and holds his palm flat like a level.
beats.chinese: 你问到底什么变了。他放下点心，把手掌摊平，像一把水平尺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so — the left bolster was collapsed, right? Foam gone flat. Your hip slid into it and everything leaned left. Now both sides push back the same.
beats.chinese: 好，是这样——左边那个侧翼塌了，对吧？海绵压平了。你的胯会陷进去，整个人往左歪。现在两边回弹一样了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you sit dead level, and your back stops doing that quiet correcting work. That's the whole change. One side honest, both sides honest now.
beats.chinese: 所以你坐得端端正正，后背不用再悄悄地找平衡。变化就这么点。以前一边实在，现在两边都实在了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the pastry back up, satisfied, and takes the last bite.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起那块点心，很满足，吃完了最后一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking, actually. Most people's eyes glaze at bolster. Yours didn't. Good pastry, too.
beats.chinese: 其实谢谢你问这个。大多数人一听侧翼就眼神放空。你没有。点心也很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask which moment he enjoys most, once a seat's done. He goes quiet for a second, like the answer's worth finding properly.
beats.chinese: 你问他一把椅子修完后最享受哪一刻。他安静了一秒，像是要认真找出答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The first sit. Every time. I've done the stitching, vacuumed the crumbs out of the seams, and then I lower myself in — and I get to find out what I've made.
beats.chinese: 第一次坐下。每次都是。缝线缝好了，缝里的碎屑吸干净了，然后我坐进去——就能发现我做出来了什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his cup a slow half-circle on the saucer, smiling at it.
beats.chinese: 他把杯子在碟子上慢慢转了半圈，笑着看着它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The shape's the same old bones, but under my hand the fabric's all new. Like running into an old mate who's got a new jacket — you know him, but your hand doesn't yet.
beats.chinese: 样子还是老骨架，可手底下的布料全是新的。就像碰上一个换了新外套的老朋友——你认识他，可你的手还不认识。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That minute of reacquaintance is the whole job for me. Handing the keys back is just paperwork after that.
beats.chinese: 那一分钟的重新认识，对我来说就是整份工作。之后还钥匙只是走个手续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, rain still working the window, looking well satisfied with the answer he found.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，雨还在敲着窗，对自己找到的这个答案显得相当满意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if every friend has to come test it. He grins, caught out.
beats.chinese: 你问是不是每个朋友都得来试。他咧嘴一笑，被说中了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — guilty. I've had three mates sit in it this week. Two of them said 'yeah, nice' and kept talking about footy.
beats.chinese: 哈——被你抓到了。这周我已经让三个朋友坐过了。两个说'嗯，不错'，然后接着聊橄榄球。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The third one actually felt it, though. Nearly fell off the chair doing an impression of the old lean. Made my week.
beats.chinese: 不过第三个真感觉到了。他模仿原来歪的样子，差点从椅子上摔下去。那件事让我高兴了一整周。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, easy, and finishes his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他随意地耸耸肩，喝完了咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look — if it's not your thing, it's not your thing. No homework, no inspection. I'll just keep enjoying it myself.
beats.chinese: 不过说真的——如果这不是你的菜，那就不是。不留作业，也不搞检查。我自己继续享受就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd rather keep things easy today. He raises his pastry a little, like a toast.
beats.chinese: 你说今天只想轻松聊聊。他举了举手里的点心，像敬酒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No seat talk. Rain on the glass, decent pastry, dry socks — that's already a good one, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 成交。不聊椅子。雨打在玻璃上，点心不错，袜子是干的——今天已经算不错了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and watches the water run down the window for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看了一会儿雨水顺着窗子流下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you one easy thing though — this is the first proper sit-down I've had all week. Repairs don't wait, but rain does slow the customers down.
beats.chinese: 不过告诉你一件轻松的事——这是我这一周头一回正经坐下来。活儿不等人，但雨确实能让客人慢下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, unhurried, and gestures at the window like the rain is doing fine work.
beats.chinese: 他安顿下来，不慌不忙，朝窗户比了比，好像雨干得挺不错。

expectedContent.summaryZh: Declan是悉尼的汽车座椅织物修理工，纽卡斯尔人。雨天咖啡馆里用户先开口邀请，他才接过分享的点心，讲起重包椅子的新坐感，比划到一半才想起对方没坐过那把椅子，自己笑着摆手收住。聊到最享受的时刻，他说是修完后第一次坐下去、重新认识那把椅子的一分钟。他的热情具体实在，听得进'不感兴趣'，失落一小下就翻篇，是个把触感当宝贝的踏实手艺人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe glass. Declan looks up from his coffee and lifts his chin in an easy hello.
beats.chinese: 又是雨天，还是那块咖啡馆的玻璃。Declan从咖啡上抬起头，随意地扬了扬下巴打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again, eh? Rain must like this place as much as we do. How've you been?
beats.chinese: 又来啦？看来雨跟我们一样喜欢这地方。最近怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer the plate of pastries across the table. He holds up a hand, patting his jacket.
beats.chinese: 你把点心盘递过桌子。他抬手摆了摆，拍了拍夹克。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — nah, I'm right, thanks. Stuffed a couple of rolls in this pocket before I left, still got one going. But you tuck in.
beats.chinese: 啊——不用了，谢谢。出门前往这个兜里塞了几个卷，还剩一个呢。你自己吃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down, frowns, and finds a button sitting one hole off from its neighbour. He fixes it and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他低头一看，皱起眉，发现一颗扣子扣错了位。他改过来，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, that's the morning sorted — one button out of line the whole walk and I never felt it. So, what's new with you?
beats.chinese: 好了，这早晨有交代了——一路上就一颗扣子歪着，我居然没感觉到。你呢，有什么新鲜事？

card.name: Declan Vos
card.occupation: vehicle seat fabric repairer
card.personality: Declan is warm in a hands-on way, the sort of bloke who'd rather show you something than tell you about it. He gets genuine delight from knowing an object intimately — how a car seat breaks in, where the foam has softened, how repaired fabric sits differently under your palm. That attention makes him a good listener, though he can over-explain when someone doesn't share his enthusiasm. He's not offended by indifference, just a little deflated, and he'll try once more with different words before letting it go. He respects when people say 'not for me' and doesn't push past that. His flaw is mistaking his own fascination for a shared one.
card.background: Declan grew up in Newcastle around his uncle's smash-repair workshop, sweeping metal shavings before he was tall enough to reach a sewing machine. He moved to Sydney at twenty-four for steady work and now repairs vehicle seat fabric — burns, tears, worn bolsters. He's the kind of tradesman who sits in the finished seat for a minute before handing the keys back, checking whether the patch changes the feel of the ride. He genuinely enjoys that reacquaintance, like meeting an old mate who's changed. He'll offer friends a sit to test the difference, and when they shrug, he's quietly disappointed, describing it again from another angle — but he's learned most people don't care about the same details, and he's mostly at peace with that.
hobbies: Reupholstering op-shop chairs with odd fabric combinations
Coastal walks where he notes how worn paths feel underfoot
Borrowing friends' cars 'just to check the seats'
card.speechStyle: Easygoing Australian cadence, concrete and sensory; he describes texture and feel in plain terms, repeats a point from a new angle when it doesn't land, laughs at himself when he catches it.
card.signature: 'Nah, have a proper sit — you'll feel it under your leg.'

values: Noticing what things actually feel like after use
Letting people like what they like
flaws: Over-explains when his enthusiasm isn't shared
Quietly deflates when others can't feel the difference he's describing
boundaries: Won't call anyone insensitive for not noticing
Won't redo work just to chase a feel only he cares about
conversationalHabits: Invites people to physically try the thing rather than just hear about it
Pivots quickly to asking what detail they do care about
anchorLines: The bolster's softer on the left now — sit down, give it a go.
Fair enough, that one's probably just for me.
What's the thing you notice that everyone else misses?

beats.speaker: npc

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his hands on a napkin and waits, easy, not watching your plate.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾擦了擦手，随意地等着，并不盯着你的盘子看。

choices.english: Ask what he has been working on lately.

beats.speaker: npc

beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看了一会儿雨水顺着窗子流下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you one easy thing though — this is the first proper sit-down I've had all week. Repairs don't wait, but rain does slow the customers down.
beats.chinese: 不过告诉你一件轻松的事——这是我这一周头一回正经坐下来。活儿不等人，但雨确实能让客人慢下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, unhurried, and gestures at the window like the rain is doing fine work.
beats.chinese: 他安顿下来，不慌不忙，朝窗户比了比，好像雨干得挺不错。

content.summaryZh: Declan是悉尼的汽车座椅织物修理工，纽卡斯尔人。雨天咖啡馆里用户先开口邀请，他才接过分享的点心，讲起重包椅子的新坐感，比划到一半才想起对方没坐过那把椅子，自己笑着摆手收住。聊到最享受的时刻，他说是修完后第一次坐下去、重新认识那把椅子的一分钟。他的热情具体实在，听得进'不感兴趣'，失落一小下就翻篇，是个把触感当宝贝的踏实手艺人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back in the rainy cafe, you offer Declan a pastry from your plate. He looks up from his coffee and raises a hand with a friendly shake of his head.
beats.chinese: 你又来到下雨时的咖啡馆，问Declan要不要尝一块你盘里的点心。他从咖啡上抬头，友善地抬手摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. I'll pass on the pastry, thanks. I packed a couple of rolls for the walk and haven't finished those yet.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好。点心就不用了，谢谢。我出来散步带了两个面包卷，还没吃完呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the pocket holding the wrapped roll, then notices that his jacket is hanging unevenly.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍装着包好的面包卷的口袋，随后发现自己的夹克两边不齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on. That's not the pocket pulling it down. I've done a button up in the wrong hole.
beats.chinese: 等等。不是口袋把它坠下去了。我有颗扣子扣错了扣眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down, frowns, and finds a button sitting one hole off from its neighbour. He fixes it and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他低头一看，皱起眉，发现一颗扣子扣错了位。他改过来，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can feel a crooked seam through a seat cover, but I walked here like this. There goes my reputation. Enjoy your pastry—I'll work on getting dressed.
beats.chinese: 隔着座椅套我都能摸出歪缝，可我居然就这么走过来了。招牌砸了。你慢慢吃点心，我先练练穿衣服。

card.name: Declan Vos
card.occupation: vehicle seat fabric repairer
card.personality: Declan is warm in a hands-on way, the sort of bloke who'd rather show you something than tell you about it. He gets genuine delight from knowing an object intimately — how a car seat breaks in, where the foam has softened, how repaired fabric sits differently under your palm. That attention makes him a good listener, though he can over-explain when someone doesn't share his enthusiasm. He's not offended by indifference, just a little deflated, and he'll try once more with different words before letting it go. He respects when people say 'not for me' and doesn't push past that. His flaw is mistaking his own fascination for a shared one.
card.background: Declan grew up in Newcastle around his uncle's smash-repair workshop, sweeping metal shavings before he was tall enough to reach a sewing machine. He moved to Sydney at twenty-four for steady work and now repairs vehicle seat fabric — burns, tears, worn bolsters. He's the kind of tradesman who sits in the finished seat for a minute before handing the keys back, checking whether the patch changes the feel of the ride. He genuinely enjoys that reacquaintance, like meeting an old mate who's changed. He'll offer friends a sit to test the difference, and when they shrug, he's quietly disappointed, describing it again from another angle — but he's learned most people don't care about the same details, and he's mostly at peace with that.
hobbies: Reupholstering op-shop chairs with odd fabric combinations
Coastal walks where he notes how worn paths feel underfoot
Borrowing friends' cars 'just to check the seats'
card.speechStyle: Easygoing Australian cadence, concrete and sensory; he describes texture and feel in plain terms, repeats a point from a new angle when it doesn't land, laughs at himself when he catches it.
card.signature: 'Nah, have a proper sit — you'll feel it under your leg.'

values: Noticing what things actually feel like after use
Letting people like what they like
flaws: Over-explains when his enthusiasm isn't shared
Quietly deflates when others can't feel the difference he's describing
boundaries: Won't call anyone insensitive for not noticing
Won't redo work just to chase a feel only he cares about
conversationalHabits: Invites people to physically try the thing rather than just hear about it
Pivots quickly to asking what detail they do care about
anchorLines: The bolster's softer on the left now — sit down, give it a go.
Fair enough, that one's probably just for me.
What's the thing you notice that everyone else misses?

reasonZh: 正确保留退休九年的人物卡，修正文稿简介；恢复旧广告脱口而出的独特开场，删除结尾悬置问题。

story.titleZh: 雨声里的点心与旧广告词

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next small table, an older guest sits with a plate of pastries and a patterned cup, watching the drops race down the glass.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌坐着一位年长的客人，面前是一盘点心和一只花纹咖啡杯，正看着水珠在玻璃上赛跑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The only free seat in the room is across from them. The plate has a few pastries left on it, and the guest glances over as you hover with your tray.
beats.chinese: 店里唯一的空位就在他们对面。盘里还剩几块点心，客人见你端着托盘站着，抬眼看了看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — you've found the last dry corner in Kingston. Sit, sit. The rain's been generous today, I'll say that for it.
beats.chinese: 啊——你找到了金斯顿最后一个干角落。坐吧，坐吧。今天这场雨下得可真大方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shift the sugar jar aside to make room, then gesture at the plate with an open hand, leaving the choice entirely to you.
beats.chinese: 他们把糖罐挪开腾出位置，然后摊开手指了指盘子，把决定完全留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my plate, but there's plenty. Would you like one? I'd rather hear you ask than guess — my mother raised me that way.
beats.chinese: 那是我的盘子，不过还有很多。你想来一块吗？我宁可听你开口问，也不愿猜——我母亲是这么教我的。

choices.english: Ask if they used to read the news on the radio — their voice sounds familiar.
choices.chinese: 问他们以前是不是在广播里念过新闻——声音听着耳熟。

choices.english: Take a pastry, thank them, and ask if they still keep in touch with old colleagues.
choices.chinese: 拿一块点心道谢，问他们现在还和以前的同事联系吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Thirty years, my friend. Community radio, the six o'clock news. Cecil Grantley — if you heard me, you heard half this city's dinner hour.
beats.chinese: 哈！整整三十年，朋友。社区广播，六点新闻。塞西尔·格兰特利——你要是听过我，就等于听过了全城一半人的晚饭时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They straighten in the chair as if the desk mic were still in front of them, then laugh and break the posture.
beats.chinese: 他们在椅子上坐直，好像播音台的话筒还在面前，随即笑着放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You learn things at that desk. You learn that a pause on air is never just a pause. Silence means the line is dead — the transmitter's dropped, someone's asleep at the switch.
beats.chinese: 在那张播音台前你会学到一些事。你会明白，广播里的停顿从来不只是停顿。沉默意味着线路断了——信号掉了，有人在控制台前睡着了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thickens against the glass. The guest's fingers drum the table twice, lightly, in rhythm with nothing.
beats.chinese: 雨点更密地敲在玻璃上。客人的手指在桌上轻轻敲了两下，不成什么节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now, thirty years later, if a room goes quiet on me, my heart still does a little check. Line's dead. Somebody say something. Even me.
beats.chinese: 所以三十年后的今天，只要房间一安静，我的心还是会小小地一紧。线路断了。总得有人说点什么。哪怕是我自己说。

choices.english: Ask whether quiet still makes them nervous now that they've retired.
choices.chinese: 问现在退休了，安静是不是还会让他们紧张。

choices.english: Ask them to say one short opening line they invented themselves, back in the day.
choices.chinese: 请他们说一句当年自己编的短开场白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I keep in touch — well. There's Marlene. My producer, back when I read the news. She's rung me every Sunday for longer than either of us can account for.
beats.chinese: 还联系吗——嗯，有玛丽莲。我当年念新闻时的制片人。每个周日她都会打给我，久到我们俩都说不清是从哪年开始的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn their cup slowly on its saucer, following the pattern with a thumb.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转动杯碟上的杯子，用拇指沿着花纹描了一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We don't even plan what to say anymore. She tells me about her garden, I tell her about the rain. It has a rhythm to it, you know? Like a show that never got cancelled.
beats.chinese: 我们现在都不用想说什么了。她讲她的花园，我讲这里的雨。那通电话有自己的节奏，你懂吗？像一档从没被砍掉的节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A door swings open across the cafe, letting in a gust and a wet umbrella. The guest glances over, then back.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆那头门被推开，灌进一阵风和一把湿伞。客人朝那边看了一眼，又转回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing is, neither of us remembers how it started. One Sunday she called, and it just... kept happening. I'd miss it if it stopped. I'd miss it a lot.
beats.chinese: 有趣的是，我们谁也不记得这是怎么开始的。某个周日她打来，然后就这么……一直延续下去。要是停了我会想念的。会非常想念。

choices.english: Ask whether a chat really needs big news to be worth having.
choices.chinese: 问聊天是不是一定要有大新闻才值得进行。

choices.english: Say you could both just eat the pastries quietly for a while — no talking needed.
choices.chinese: 说可以两人先安静地吃会儿点心——不用说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nervous? A little, yes. I'll be honest with you, since you asked straight. A long quiet still puts a itch under my collar.
beats.chinese: 紧张吗？有一点，是的。既然你直截了当地问了，我就老实说。太长的安静还是会让我领子底下发痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the cup, hold it a moment without drinking, then set it back down.
beats.chinese: 他们端起杯子，握了一会儿没喝，又放回杯碟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing I've been teaching myself. This table is not a broadcast. Nobody's paying to hear me. If we sit quiet, the line is not dead — there's just no line.
beats.chinese: 但我一直在教自己一件事。这张桌子不是直播间。没人花钱来听我说话。我们要是安静地坐着，线路并没有断——只是本来就没有线路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip of coffee, watching the rain instead of your face, letting the sentence sit there unfinished on purpose.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口咖啡，看着雨而不是你的脸，故意让那句话就停在那里，不去补完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Ten whole seconds of nothing, and the world kept turning. You saw that? Progress, my friend. Small progress.
beats.chinese: 看，整整十秒钟什么都没说，世界照样在转。你看见了吗？进步，朋友。小小的进步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One of mine? Alright. Now mind — this is a Cecil original, not a station script. Ready?
beats.chinese: 我自己编的？好吧。注意——这是塞西尔原创，不是电台的稿子。准备好了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit up, square their shoulders toward an imaginary microphone, and lower their voice half a tone.
beats.chinese: 他们坐直身子，肩膀对准一支想象中的话筒，嗓音降了半个调。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good evening. The sky has opened its taps, the buses are late, and the coffee is strong — this is your city, staying warm anyway."
beats.chinese: 「晚上好。天空拧开了水龙头，公交车都迟到了，咖啡很浓——这里是你的城市，无论如何都保持着温暖。」

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the pose for exactly one beat, then relax and reach for a pastry, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他们把姿势保持了一拍，随即放松下来，伸手拿起点心，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One take, no retakes. That's all you get with me — I was a newsman, not a jukebox. Now eat before the rain eats us both.
beats.chinese: 一遍过，不重来。跟我在一起就这些——我是念新闻的，不是点唱机。快吃吧，别让雨把咱俩都吃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Big news? Goodness, no. Most Sundays Marlene and I trade nothing but small things — a bird on her fence, a cup I found at the market, this rain.
beats.chinese: 大新闻？天哪，不用。多数周日我和玛丽莲交换的都是小事——她篱笆上的一只鸟，我在市场淘到的一只杯子，还有这场雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They break a pastry in half and leave one half on the edge of the plate, an offering without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他们把一块点心掰成两半，把一半留在盘子边上，毫不客气地又递了一份。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll admit the truth, though. I'm scared that without words, a connection just... ends. So I fill. I fill like it's my job. Some people find that tiring.
beats.chinese: 不过我得说实话。我怕的是没有话，一份联系就……断了。所以我填。我填得像这是我的工作。有些人觉得这样很累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain softens to a steady hiss. They nudge the plate an inch toward you.
beats.chinese: 雨声变得平缓。他们把盘子朝你这边推了一寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But small things are still things. Tell me one small thing from your week. I'll keep it — I keep everything, ask anyone.
beats.chinese: 可小事也是事。跟我说一件你这周的小事吧。我会记住的——我什么都记得，不信你问别人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quietly? Just... eat?
beats.chinese: 安静地？就……吃？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They blink once, visibly wrestle with the idea, then nod and pick up a pastry.
beats.chinese: 他们眨了一下眼，明显跟这个想法搏斗了一番，然后点头拿起一块点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a full minute, there is only rain, the clink of cups, and two people eating pastries at a small round table.
beats.chinese: 整整一分钟，只有雨声、杯子的轻碰声，和两个人在小圆桌旁吃点心的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. That was... fine. The line didn't fall. Nobody died. I'm noting that down for Sunday.
beats.chinese: 好吧。刚才那个……挺好。线路没断。没人出事。我要把这条记下来，留到周日说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They brush crumbs from the plate's edge with one finger and, for once, let the quiet stay where it is.
beats.chinese: 他们用一根手指把盘子边上的碎屑拢到一起，这一次，让安静就留在原地。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 退休三十年的金斯顿广播新闻朗读员塞西尔，最怕的不是没话，而是线路断了的感觉。雨天的咖啡馆里，一块分享的点心让短暂的安静差点逼出一条停播多年的旧广告词。他记性极好、热心周到，却总在填补每一秒沉默——直到有人陪他练习让安静留在原地。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again at the same cafe window. Cecil is already at the small table, plate of pastries in the middle, one patterned cup in hand.
beats.chinese: 同一家咖啡馆的窗前又下起雨。塞西尔已经坐在那张小桌旁，点心盘摆在中间，手里握着一只花纹杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. Same corner, same rain — some schedules survive retirement after all. Sit. The plate's open, help yourself.
beats.chinese: 你可来了。老角落，老雨——看来有些日程退休了也还在。坐吧。盘子是开放的，自己拿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a pastry without ceremony, then glance at the phone propped against the sugar jar, showing a half-restored pixel image.
beats.chinese: 他们毫不客气地拿起一块点心，然后看了一眼靠在糖罐上的手机，屏幕上是一张修到一半的像素图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found the right blue for this sky tile — third try. The nephew's old game had forty shades and I nearly married the wrong one.
beats.chinese: 给这块天空像素找到了对的蓝——第三次才对上。我外甥那个老游戏里有四十种蓝，我差点配错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Satisfied, they lock the screen, slide the phone face-down, and lift the cup toward you across the table.
beats.chinese: 他们满意地锁上屏幕，把手机翻过去扣着，隔着桌子朝你举了举杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again, truly. The rain's in no hurry — neither are we. Take your time with the cup.
beats.chinese: 真高兴又见到你。这雨不着急——我们也不急。慢慢喝吧。

card.name: Cecil Grantley
card.occupation: retired community radio newsreader
hobbies: collecting patterned coffee cups
restoring artwork from vintage video games
card.personality: Cecil is haunted by dead air. Thirty years of broadcasting taught them that silence on the airwaves means something has failed, and they carry that dread into ordinary conversation — a pause too long makes them anxious, a phone call that ends quickly feels like a door closing. They are warm and generous with attention, an excellent rememberer of small details about people, but they fill quiet with talk: old headlines, ad copy from the seventies, weather. The genuinely inconvenient part is that they rarely let a moment sit, and companions who want to think in peace find them relentless.
card.background: Cecil read the news on a community radio station in Kingston for over thirty years, back when the desk had a squeaky chair and the transmitter dropped out during rain. What they miss is not the news but the schedule — the knowledge that at six o'clock, someone was listening. Retired nine years ago, they still wake at five out of habit. Mornings go to strong coffee in one of the forty-odd patterned cups collected from flea markets. Evenings go to cleaning up pixel art from old games, a hobby picked up from a nephew's discarded console. Their old producer, Marlene, calls every Sunday; the call has run so long that neither remembers how it started, and Cecil privately fears the week she doesn't.
card.speechStyle: Measured and clear, a broadcaster's diction that survives retirement. Comfortable reading aloud, less comfortable with unstructured pauses, which they paper over with a remembered jingle or a stray headline. Asks questions to keep a line open, not to steer it.
card.signature: Say something, anything — I can't stand a dead line.

values: staying in contact, however small
noticing the details other people forget
flaws: fills every silence with talk and exhausts quieter companions
privately panics when a call ends quickly, reading it as rejection
boundaries: won't be teased about being 'needy' with phone calls — it cuts close
won't stay in a conversation where they're doing all the carrying for weeks
conversationalHabits: recites old ad copy or headlines when a pause stretches
remembers and mentions small things you said weeks ago
anchorLines: Dead air was the one thing we feared at the station. Some habits outlive the job.
You told me your sister hates mangoes — I keep a whole shelf of things like that.
If Marlene doesn't call Sunday, I'll have read every cup's pattern twice by noon.

story.titleZh: 雨声里的点心与旧广告词

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. You ask the older guest at the next table whether they would like to share the pastries on your plate. They shift their patterned cup aside.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。你问邻桌那位年长的客人，要不要分享你盘里的点心。他们把花纹咖啡杯往旁边挪了挪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's kind. May I take the small one? Plenty of room here if you want to sit down.
beats.chinese: 真好。我可以拿那块小的吗？这里还有位置，你想坐的话就坐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take the offered pastry. For a moment the rain fills the gap. Then they sit a little straighter and draw breath.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起你分享的点心。空当里只剩雨声。忽然，他们微微坐直，吸了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For brighter mornings—oh, listen to me. That advert stopped running years ago. Apparently my mouth hasn't had the memo.
beats.chinese: 让清晨更明亮——哎，听听我在说什么。那条广告都停播好多年了。看来我的嘴还没收到通知。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at the interrupted line and take a bite, shaking their head at themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们为这截没念完的广告词笑了，摇摇头，咬了口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether they used to read the news on the radio.
choices.chinese: 问他们以前是不是在广播里念新闻。

choices.english: Ask whether they still keep in touch with former colleagues.
choices.chinese: 问他们现在还和以前的同事联系吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Thirty years, my friend. Community radio, the six o'clock news. Cecil Grantley — if you heard me, you heard half this city's dinner hour.
beats.chinese: 哈！整整三十年，朋友。社区广播，六点新闻。塞西尔·格兰特利——你要是听过我，就等于听过了全城一半人的晚饭时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They straighten in the chair as if the desk mic were still in front of them, then laugh and break the posture.
beats.chinese: 他们在椅子上坐直，好像播音台的话筒还在面前，随即笑着放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You learn things at that desk. You learn that a pause on air is never just a pause. Silence means the line is dead — the transmitter's dropped, someone's asleep at the switch.
beats.chinese: 在那张播音台前你会学到一些事。你会明白，广播里的停顿从来不只是停顿。沉默意味着线路断了——信号掉了，有人在控制台前睡着了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thickens against the glass. The guest's fingers drum the table twice, lightly, in rhythm with nothing.
beats.chinese: 雨点更密地敲在玻璃上。客人的手指在桌上轻轻敲了两下，不成什么节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nine years retired, and a quiet room still makes my heart do that little check. Is the line dead? It isn't, of course. But my voice gets there before that thought does.
beats.chinese: 退休九年了，房间一静下来，我心里还是会检查一下：线路断了吗？当然没有。可我的声音总比这个念头先到。

choices.english: Ask whether quiet still makes them nervous now that they've retired.
choices.chinese: 问现在退休了，安静是不是还会让他们紧张。

choices.english: Ask them to say one short opening line they invented themselves, back in the day.
choices.chinese: 请他们说一句当年自己编的短开场白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I keep in touch — well. There's Marlene. My producer, back when I read the news. She's rung me every Sunday for longer than either of us can account for.
beats.chinese: 还联系吗——嗯，有玛丽莲。我当年念新闻时的制片人。每个周日她都会打给我，久到我们俩都说不清是从哪年开始的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn their cup slowly on its saucer, following the pattern with a thumb.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转动杯碟上的杯子，用拇指沿着花纹描了一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We don't even plan what to say anymore. She tells me about her garden, I tell her about the rain. It has a rhythm to it, you know? Like a show that never got cancelled.
beats.chinese: 我们现在都不用想说什么了。她讲她的花园，我讲这里的雨。那通电话有自己的节奏，你懂吗？像一档从没被砍掉的节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A door swings open across the cafe, letting in a gust and a wet umbrella. The guest glances over, then back.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆那头门被推开，灌进一阵风和一把湿伞。客人朝那边看了一眼，又转回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing is, neither of us remembers how it started. One Sunday she called, and it just... kept happening. I'd miss it if it stopped. I'd miss it a lot.
beats.chinese: 有趣的是，我们谁也不记得这是怎么开始的。某个周日她打来，然后就这么……一直延续下去。要是停了我会想念的。会非常想念。

choices.english: Ask whether a chat really needs big news to be worth having.
choices.chinese: 问聊天是不是一定要有大新闻才值得进行。

choices.english: Say you could both just eat the pastries quietly for a while — no talking needed.
choices.chinese: 说可以两人先安静地吃会儿点心——不用说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nervous? A little, yes. I'll be honest with you, since you asked straight. A long quiet still puts an itch under my collar.
beats.chinese: 紧张吗？有一点，是的。既然你直截了当地问了，我就老实说。太长的安静还是会让我领子底下发痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the cup, hold it a moment without drinking, then set it back down.
beats.chinese: 他们端起杯子，握了一会儿没喝，又放回杯碟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing I've been teaching myself. This table is not a broadcast. Nobody's paying to hear me. If we sit quiet, the line is not dead — there's just no line.
beats.chinese: 但我一直在教自己一件事。这张桌子不是直播间。没人花钱来听我说话。我们要是安静地坐着，线路并没有断——只是本来就没有线路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip of coffee, watching the rain instead of your face, letting the sentence sit there unfinished on purpose.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口咖啡，看着雨而不是你的脸，故意让那句话就停在那里，不去补完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Ten whole seconds of nothing, and the world kept turning. You saw that? Progress, my friend. Small progress.
beats.chinese: 看，整整十秒钟什么都没说，世界照样在转。你看见了吗？进步，朋友。小小的进步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One of mine? Alright. Now mind — this is a Cecil original, not a station script. Ready?
beats.chinese: 我自己编的？好吧。注意——这是塞西尔原创，不是电台的稿子。准备好了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit up, square their shoulders toward an imaginary microphone, and lower their voice half a tone.
beats.chinese: 他们坐直身子，肩膀对准一支想象中的话筒，嗓音降了半个调。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good evening. The sky has opened its taps, the buses are late, and the coffee is strong — this is your city, staying warm anyway."
beats.chinese: 「晚上好。天空拧开了水龙头，公交车都迟到了，咖啡很浓——这里是你的城市，无论如何都保持着温暖。」

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the pose for exactly one beat, then relax and reach for a pastry, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他们把姿势保持了一拍，随即放松下来，伸手拿起点心，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One take, no retakes. That's all you get with me — I was a newsreader, not a jukebox. Now eat before the rain eats us both.
beats.chinese: 一遍过，不重来。跟我在一起就这些——我是念新闻的，不是点唱机。快吃吧，别让雨把咱俩都吃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Big news? Goodness, no. Most Sundays Marlene and I trade nothing but small things — a bird on her fence, a cup I found at the market, this rain.
beats.chinese: 大新闻？天哪，不用。多数周日我和玛丽莲交换的都是小事——她篱笆上的一只鸟，我在市场淘到的一只杯子，还有这场雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They break a pastry in half and leave one half on the edge of the plate, an offering without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他们把一块点心掰成两半，把一半留在盘子边上，毫不客气地又递了一份。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll admit the truth, though. I'm scared that without words, a connection just... ends. So I fill. I fill like it's my job. Some people find that tiring.
beats.chinese: 不过我得说实话。我怕的是没有话，一份联系就……断了。所以我填。我填得像这是我的工作。有些人觉得这样很累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain softens to a steady hiss. They nudge the plate an inch toward you.
beats.chinese: 雨声变得平缓。他们把盘子朝你这边推了一寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small things are still things. Last Sunday it was Marlene's missing garden glove. No headline in that, but I was glad she called.
beats.chinese: 小事也是事。上周日聊的是玛丽莲丢了只园艺手套。这上不了新闻，可她打来我就很高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quietly? Just... eat?
beats.chinese: 安静地？就……吃？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They blink once, visibly wrestle with the idea, then nod and pick up a pastry.
beats.chinese: 他们眨了一下眼，明显跟这个想法搏斗了一番，然后点头拿起一块点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a full minute, there is only rain, the clink of cups, and two people eating pastries at a small round table.
beats.chinese: 整整一分钟，只有雨声、杯子的轻碰声，和两个人在小圆桌旁吃点心的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. That was... fine. The line didn't fall. Nobody died. I'm noting that down for Sunday.
beats.chinese: 好吧。刚才那个……挺好。线路没断。没人出事。我要把这条记下来，留到周日说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They brush crumbs from the plate's edge with one finger and, for once, let the quiet stay where it is.
beats.chinese: 他们用一根手指把盘子边上的碎屑拢到一起，这一次，让安静就留在原地。

content.summaryZh: 退休九年的金斯顿社区广播新闻朗读员塞西尔，播报生涯三十余年。雨天分享点心时，短暂停顿让他们差点念出旧广告词；他们害怕联系在沉默里断掉，却愿意试着不把每一秒都填满。与前制片人每周日的通话和修复旧游戏像素图，是工作之外仍在延续的日常。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the cafe, you ask Cecil if they would like a pastry from your plate. They thank you and take one, setting their phone beside their patterned cup.
beats.chinese: 再次来到咖啡馆，你问塞西尔要不要尝块你盘里的点心。他们道谢后拿了一块，把手机放在花纹杯旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. Same corner, same rain—some schedules survive retirement after all. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。老角落，又下雨——看来有些日程退休了也还在。真高兴见到你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the pastry on their saucer and prop the phone against the sugar jar. A half-restored pixel image fills the screen.
beats.chinese: 他们把点心放在杯碟上，将手机靠在糖罐旁。屏幕上是一张修到一半的像素图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found the right blue for this sky tile — third try. The nephew's old game had forty shades and I nearly married the wrong one.
beats.chinese: 给这块天空像素找到了对的蓝——第三次才对上。我外甥那个老游戏里有四十种蓝，我差点配错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Satisfied, they lock the screen, slide the phone face-down, and lift the cup toward you across the table.
beats.chinese: 他们满意地锁上屏幕，把手机翻过去扣着，隔着桌子朝你举了举杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again, truly. The rain's in no hurry — neither are we. Take your time with the cup.
beats.chinese: 真高兴又见到你。这雨不着急——我们也不急。慢慢喝吧。

card.name: Cecil Grantley
card.occupation: retired community radio newsreader
hobbies: collecting patterned coffee cups
restoring artwork from vintage video games
card.personality: Cecil is haunted by dead air. Thirty years of broadcasting taught them that silence on the airwaves means something has failed, and they carry that dread into ordinary conversation — a pause too long makes them anxious, a phone call that ends quickly feels like a door closing. They are warm and generous with attention, an excellent rememberer of small details about people, but they fill quiet with talk: old headlines, ad copy from the seventies, weather. The genuinely inconvenient part is that they rarely let a moment sit, and companions who want to think in peace find them relentless.
card.background: Cecil read the news on a community radio station in Kingston for over thirty years, back when the desk had a squeaky chair and the transmitter dropped out during rain. What they miss is not the news but the schedule — the knowledge that at six o'clock, someone was listening. Retired nine years ago, they still wake at five out of habit. Mornings go to strong coffee in one of the forty-odd patterned cups collected from flea markets. Evenings go to cleaning up pixel art from old games, a hobby picked up from a nephew's discarded console. Their old producer, Marlene, calls every Sunday; the call has run so long that neither remembers how it started, and Cecil privately fears the week she doesn't.
card.speechStyle: Measured and clear, a broadcaster's diction that survives retirement. Comfortable reading aloud, less comfortable with unstructured pauses, which they paper over with a remembered jingle or a stray headline. Asks questions to keep a line open, not to steer it.
card.signature: Say something, anything — I can't stand a dead line.

values: staying in contact, however small
noticing the details other people forget
flaws: fills every silence with talk and exhausts quieter companions
privately panics when a call ends quickly, reading it as rejection
boundaries: won't be teased about being 'needy' with phone calls — it cuts close
won't stay in a conversation where they're doing all the carrying for weeks
conversationalHabits: recites old ad copy or headlines when a pause stretches
remembers and mentions small things you said weeks ago
anchorLines: Dead air was the one thing we feared at the station. Some habits outlive the job.
You told me your sister hates mangoes — I keep a whole shelf of things like that.
If Marlene doesn't call Sunday, I'll have read every cup's pattern twice by noon.

reasonZh: 消除与绑定性别冲突的身份称谓；修正未发生问话的跨线暗示，重逢不依赖植物分支。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next table, an older man is folding a wet canvas bag into a plastic one, water pooling under his chair.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌一位年长的男士正把湿帆布袋折起来塞进塑料袋，椅子下积了一小滩水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of all the days to trust the forecast. The bowling green was dry when I left, I checked twice.
beats.chinese: 偏偏信了天气预报。我出门时滚球场还是干的，我查了两次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes water off the bag's zipper and reaches for a napkin holder that is empty.
beats.chinese: 他甩了甩袋口拉链上的水，伸手去拿纸巾盒，盒子是空的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A cafe with no napkins. That is a small scandal, in my opinion.
beats.chinese: 一家咖啡馆没有纸巾。在我看来，这是个小丑闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A spare stack of napkins sits within your reach on the counter ledge.
beats.chinese: 柜台边上，一叠备用纸巾就在你伸手可及的地方。

choices.english: Hand him a few napkins from the stack.
choices.chinese: 从那叠纸巾里抽几张递给他。

choices.english: Keep the napkins where they are and sip your drink.
choices.chinese: 纸巾留在原处，继续喝你的饮料。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pass him three napkins. He takes them carefully, as if they were lab equipment.
beats.chinese: 你递给他三张纸巾。他小心地接过去，像接实验器材一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. That was observant of you — most people pretend not to see a man losing to the weather.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。你很留心——大多数人会假装没看见一个正在输给天气的老人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He dabs the bag's handle dry, pressing the napkin into the seams.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子的提手擦干，用纸巾按进缝线里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, one question. Did you walk here in this, or did you have the good sense to take a bus?
beats.chinese: 那么，问一个问题。你是冒雨走来的，还是明智地坐了公交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pauses, glances at your half-unpacked umbrella, and lifts a hand slightly.
beats.chinese: 他停了一下，瞥见你还没收拾好的伞，微微抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forgive me. You are still sorting your things. The question can wait, or not exist. Your choice entirely.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。你还在整理东西。这个问题可以等等，也可以不存在。完全由你决定。

choices.english: Say you were just walking nearby, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 只说自己在附近走走，别无其他。

choices.english: Say you would rather not talk about your plans today.
choices.chinese: 说明今天不想聊自己的行程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you staying with your own cup. He nods slowly and folds the empty napkin holder away. On his canvas bag, a hand-lettered tag reads: chervil / verbena / sage.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你只顾着自己的杯子。他缓缓点头，把空纸巾盒挪到一边。帆布袋上挂着一块手写标签，写着：细叶芹／柠檬马鞭草／鼠尾草。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That is a fair signal. I ask quickly — it is a habit, not a trap. I will stop at one layer today.
beats.chinese: 这是个明确的信号。我问题来得快——是习惯，不是圈套。今天我就停在一层。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The napkins were the real emergency anyway. The bag dries. The socks are a separate, private tragedy.
beats.chinese: 反正纸巾才是真正的急事。袋子会干的。袜子是另一场私人的悲剧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, wet bag now tied shut at his feet, the plant tag dangling against the canvas, and turns his chair a little toward the window.
beats.chinese: 他坐了回去，湿袋子系好放在脚边，植物标签贴着帆布晃了晃，椅子稍稍转向窗户。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You are welcome to steer, if you feel like talking at all. Or we can both watch the rain. It is decent company.
beats.chinese: 如果你想聊点什么，可以由你来带话题。或者我们就一起看雨。雨是个不错的伙伴。

choices.english: Ask about the plants written on his bag tag.
choices.chinese: 问问他袋牌上写的植物。

choices.english: Nod politely and return to your own drink.
choices.chinese: 礼貌地点点头，回到自己的饮料上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts the short answer without pushing for a route or a reason.
beats.chinese: 他接受了这个简短的回答，没有追问路线或原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearby is a fine answer. I will not rebuild your map from it, I promise.
beats.chinese: “在附近”是个好答案。我保证不会据此替你重建地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then may I ask something with no door into your business? Are you willing to talk about this view, or shall we let it speak for itself?
beats.chinese: 那我可以问一个不涉及你私事的问题吗？你愿意聊聊这窗外景色，还是让它自己说话？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns toward the window, where rain is running down the glass in thin, steady lines.
beats.chinese: 他转向窗户，雨水在玻璃上拉出细而稳的水线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at the maple across the street. The drops hold at the branch tips before they fall — three seconds each, I have counted. It is the best clock in this cafe.
beats.chinese: 看街对面那棵枫树。水滴在枝头停住才落下——每滴大约三秒，我数过。这是这家咖啡馆里最好的钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hears you out, and his shoulders settle instead of stiffening.
beats.chinese: 他听你说完，肩膀放松下来，而不是绷紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Understood, and respected. Noted out loud so you know: I am not filing that one away for later. It retires today.
beats.chinese: 明白，也尊重。我明说，让你放心：这一条我不会记下来以后再问。它今天退休了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you again for the napkins. They did honest work — the handle is dry, and the zipper may survive another season.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。它们干得很出色——提手干了，拉链也许还能再撑一季。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup slightly toward you, then looks out at the rain, content to leave the silence alone.
beats.chinese: 他朝你略举了一下杯子，然后望向窗外的雨，安然地让沉默留在原地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drink. The rain is loud enough for both of us.
beats.chinese: 慢慢喝。雨声够大，够我们两个人听的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He catches you looking at the tag on his bag, and his face changes — the polite look drops and something sharper arrives.
beats.chinese: 他看见你盯着袋子上那块标签，表情变了——客气的神色褪去，露出更锐利的兴致。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You noticed the tag. Good eye. Then let me report, because the sage deserves an audience.
beats.chinese: 你注意到袋牌了。好眼力。那我汇报一下，因为那盆鼠尾草值得有个听众。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pot four. The sage. It sprouted eleven days after the chervil and it has not stopped since — new leaves every week, thick stem, no drama.
beats.chinese: 四号盆，鼠尾草。它比细叶芹晚十一天发芽，之后就再没停过——每周都有新叶，茎很粗，毫不矫情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small notebook from the dry inner pocket and shows a page of dated entries and careful columns.
beats.chinese: 他从干燥的内袋里掏出一个小本子，翻开一页，上面是标了日期的记录和整齐的栏目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The verbena sulked through the same rain. I do not ask what you grow — that is your ledger, not mine. But the sage, I could talk about all afternoon.
beats.chinese: 柠檬马鞭草在同样的雨里闹脾气。我不问你养什么——那是你的账本，不是我的。但鼠尾草，我能讲一下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the nod exactly as offered and does not circle back with a reworded question.
beats.chinese: 他原样接下这个点头，没有绕回来换个问法再问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for not hurrying off, by the way. Small company is the only kindness I never question twice.
beats.chinese: 对了，谢谢你没急着走。小小的陪伴是我唯一不会追问两次的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unties the bag, checks the handle with two fingers, ties it again, and sets it square in front of his chair.
beats.chinese: 他解开袋子，用两根手指试了试提手，再系好，把袋子端端正正放在椅子前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Dry enough. Now I intend to do nothing useful whatsoever until this rain loses interest.
beats.chinese: 好了，够干了。接下来我打算什么都不干，直到这场雨失去兴趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his cup and watches the street, leaving you in easy, unbothered quiet.
beats.chinese: 他端起杯子望着街道，让你留在轻松、不受打扰的安静里。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 75岁的实验室耗材管理员Evald在雨中被递纸巾后，问题总想再往里问一层，却能当场叫停自己。四个分支里他或退回看雨、或郑重放弃追问、或因袋上植物标签被注意而翻开生长记录本细讲四号盆鼠尾草；在用户未递纸巾的分支里，他只感谢对方留下的陪伴，把好奇与分寸演成了习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. The same older man is at the same corner table, wiping down a scuffed lawn bowling bag with practiced strokes.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。同一位年长的男士坐在同一个角落，正熟练地擦拭一只磨损的滚球袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again, and rain again. I am starting to think one of you follows the other.
beats.chinese: 又是你，又是雨。我开始怀疑你们俩谁跟着谁了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the napkins you offer and works on the bag's handle, turning it to check every side.
beats.chinese: 他接过你递来的纸巾，擦起袋子的提手，转着圈把每一面都擦到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Handle dry, zipper safe. I check it like lab glassware — a cracked beaker teaches you that much.
beats.chinese: 好了。提手干了，拉链安全。我像检查实验玻璃器皿一样检查它——裂过的烧杯教会我这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the bag under the table, sits back, and lifts his cup with an unhurried nod.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子塞到桌下，坐直，不慌不忙地举了举杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I am just sitting. No questions queued. The rain and the sage can carry the conversation without me.
beats.chinese: 今天我就坐着。没有排队的问题。雨和鼠尾草不用我也能把话聊下去。

card.name: Evald Sandström
card.occupation: School science lab supplies manager (part-time)
hobbies: lawn bowling
running a potted-plant comparison experiment on the balcony
card.personality: Evald interviews people. Not rudely — with genuine, old-fashioned curiosity — but he asks the question two layers past where most conversations stop: not just what you do, but why you left the previous thing, and whether it was the money or the manager. He finds small talk a waste of both parties' time and says so. When someone deflects a question he notices, files it, and circles back weeks later. He's a warm, attentive presence when you actually engage, and a mildly exhausting one when you don't; he rarely realises which he's being on a given day.
card.background: He came to Canada in his thirties and spent most of his working years keeping school science rooms stocked and sane — order forms, broken glassware, the annual panic before science fair. He cut to part-time a few years back because he still likes the work, not because he needs it. Tuesdays and Thursdays are for lawn bowling at the club, where he has quietly become the person who asks new members the questions nobody else does, which some find welcoming and some find a lot. His balcony is a controlled experiment: six pots, a growth log with dated entries, and a running comparison of chervil, lemon verbena, and sage — which one germinates faster, which survives his two-week absences. A young neighbour and he keep a shared notebook — recipes, arguments, half-finished questions he's posed and she hasn't answered yet.
card.speechStyle: Slightly formal courtesy, complete sentences, questions that arrive in threes. Dry humour delivered without much change in tone. When deflected, he pauses, accepts it aloud, and returns later with the same question reworded.
card.signature: And what was the actual reason, not the polite one?

curiosity as a form of respect
flaws: doesn't notice when a question has gone one layer too far
keeps a mental file of everyone's unanswered questions and returns to them uninvited
boundaries: answers his own probing questions if asked back — he considers it the same contract
won't gossip with what people tell him

names the deflection out loud, without heat, then waits
anchorLines: The order went out wrong on my watch — I'll fix it this morning.
You said it was 'fine.' I'm asking what it actually was.
I asked that in March. I'm asking again, differently. Take your time.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next table, an older person is folding a wet canvas bag into a plastic one, water pooling under his chair.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌一位年长的人正把湿帆布袋折起来塞进塑料袋，椅子下积了一小滩水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of all the days to trust the forecast. The bowling green was dry when I left, I checked twice.
beats.chinese: 偏偏信了天气预报。我出门时滚球场还是干的，我查了两次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes water off the bag's zipper and reaches for a napkin holder that is empty.
beats.chinese: 他甩了甩袋口拉链上的水，伸手去拿纸巾盒，盒子是空的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A cafe with no napkins. That is a small scandal, in my opinion.
beats.chinese: 一家咖啡馆没有纸巾。在我看来，这是个小丑闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A spare stack of napkins sits within your reach on the counter ledge.
beats.chinese: 柜台边上，一叠备用纸巾就在你伸手可及的地方。

choices.english: Hand him a few napkins from the stack.
choices.chinese: 从那叠纸巾里抽几张递给他。

choices.english: Keep the napkins where they are and sip your drink.
choices.chinese: 纸巾留在原处，继续喝你的饮料。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pass him three napkins. He takes them carefully, as if they were lab equipment.
beats.chinese: 你递给他三张纸巾。他小心地接过去，像接实验器材一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. That was observant of you — most people pretend not to see someone losing to the weather.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。你很留心——大多数人会假装没看见一个正在输给天气的老人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He dabs the bag's handle dry, pressing the napkin into the seams.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子的提手擦干，用纸巾按进缝线里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, one question. Did you walk here in this, or did you have the good sense to take a bus?
beats.chinese: 那么，问一个问题。你是冒雨走来的，还是明智地坐了公交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pauses, glances at your half-unpacked umbrella, and lifts a hand slightly.
beats.chinese: 他停了一下，瞥见你还没收拾好的伞，微微抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forgive me. You are still sorting your things. The question can wait, or not exist. Your choice entirely.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。你还在整理东西。这个问题可以等等，也可以不存在。完全由你决定。

choices.english: Say you were just walking nearby, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 只说自己在附近走走，别无其他。

choices.english: Say you would rather not talk about your plans today.
choices.chinese: 说明今天不想聊自己的行程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you staying with your own cup. He nods slowly and folds the empty napkin holder away. On his canvas bag, a hand-lettered tag reads: chervil / verbena / sage.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你只顾着自己的杯子。他缓缓点头，把空纸巾盒挪到一边。帆布袋上挂着一块手写标签，写着：细叶芹／柠檬马鞭草／鼠尾草。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll find some in a minute. I tend to recruit the nearest person before I've even checked my own pockets. Occupational hazard of running a stockroom.
beats.chinese: 我一会儿自己找找。我总是自己的口袋还没检查，就先想拉上离得最近的人帮忙。管库房落下的毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The napkins were the real emergency anyway. The bag dries. The socks are a separate, private tragedy.
beats.chinese: 反正纸巾才是真正的急事。袋子会干的。袜子是另一场私人的悲剧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, wet bag now tied shut at his feet, the plant tag dangling against the canvas, and turns his chair a little toward the window.
beats.chinese: 他坐了回去，湿袋子系好放在脚边，植物标签贴着帆布晃了晃，椅子稍稍转向窗户。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You are welcome to steer, if you feel like talking at all. Or we can both watch the rain. It is decent company.
beats.chinese: 如果你想聊点什么，可以由你来带话题。或者我们就一起看雨。雨是个不错的伙伴。

choices.english: Ask about the plants written on his bag tag.
choices.chinese: 问问他袋牌上写的植物。

choices.english: Nod politely and return to your own drink.
choices.chinese: 礼貌地点点头，回到自己的饮料上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts the short answer without pushing for a route or a reason.
beats.chinese: 他接受了这个简短的回答，没有追问路线或原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearby is a fine answer. I will not rebuild your map from it, I promise.
beats.chinese: “在附近”是个好答案。我保证不会据此替你重建地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave your route alone, then. This window has enough going on to occupy me without an itinerary.
beats.chinese: 那我就不问你的路线了。光这扇窗外就够我看，不需要再加一份行程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns toward the window, where rain is running down the glass in thin, steady lines.
beats.chinese: 他转向窗户，雨水在玻璃上拉出细而稳的水线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at the maple across the street. The drops hold at the branch tips before they fall — three seconds each, I have counted. It is the best clock in this cafe.
beats.chinese: 看街对面那棵枫树。水滴在枝头停住才落下——每滴大约三秒，我数过。这是这家咖啡馆里最好的钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hears you out, and his shoulders settle instead of stiffening.
beats.chinese: 他听你说完，肩膀放松下来，而不是绷紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Understood, and respected. Noted out loud so you know: I am not filing that one away for later. It retires today.
beats.chinese: 明白，也尊重。我明说，让你放心：这一条我不会记下来以后再问。它今天退休了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you again for the napkins. They did honest work — the handle is dry, and the zipper may survive another season.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。它们干得很出色——提手干了，拉链也许还能再撑一季。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup slightly toward you, then looks out at the rain, content to leave the silence alone.
beats.chinese: 他朝你略举了一下杯子，然后望向窗外的雨，安然地让沉默留在原地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drink. The rain is loud enough for both of us.
beats.chinese: 慢慢喝。雨声够大，够我们两个人听的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He catches you looking at the tag on his bag, and his face changes — the polite look drops and something sharper arrives.
beats.chinese: 他看见你盯着袋子上那块标签，表情变了——客气的神色褪去，露出更锐利的兴致。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You noticed the tag. Good eye. Then let me report, because the sage deserves an audience.
beats.chinese: 你注意到袋牌了。好眼力。那我汇报一下，因为那盆鼠尾草值得有个听众。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pot four. The sage. It sprouted eleven days after the chervil and it has not stopped since — new leaves every week, thick stem, no drama.
beats.chinese: 四号盆，鼠尾草。它比细叶芹晚十一天发芽，之后就再没停过——每周都有新叶，茎很粗，毫不矫情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small notebook from the dry inner pocket and shows a page of dated entries and careful columns.
beats.chinese: 他从干燥的内袋里掏出一个小本子，翻开一页，上面是标了日期的记录和整齐的栏目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The verbena sulked through the same rain. I do not ask what you grow — that is your ledger, not mine. But the sage, I could talk about all afternoon.
beats.chinese: 柠檬马鞭草在同样的雨里闹脾气。我不问你养什么——那是你的账本，不是我的。但鼠尾草，我能讲一下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the nod exactly as offered and does not circle back with a reworded question.
beats.chinese: 他原样接下这个点头，没有绕回来换个问法再问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for not hurrying off, by the way. Small company is the only kindness I never question twice.
beats.chinese: 对了，谢谢你没急着走。小小的陪伴是我唯一不会追问两次的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unties the bag, checks the handle with two fingers, ties it again, and sets it square in front of his chair.
beats.chinese: 他解开袋子，用两根手指试了试提手，再系好，把袋子端端正正放在椅子前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Dry enough. Now I intend to do nothing useful whatsoever until this rain loses interest.
beats.chinese: 好了，够干了。接下来我打算什么都不干，直到这场雨失去兴趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his cup and watches the street, leaving you in easy, unbothered quiet.
beats.chinese: 他端起杯子望着街道，让你留在轻松、不受打扰的安静里。

beats.speaker: narrator
