reasonZh: 恢复已规划的宠物拜访故事和两层选择；移除读用户笔记、说教、跨分支知识及固定星期，重逢不再重复狗的场面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In the park, you sit on a bench and open your notebook, writing down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 在公园里，你坐在长椅上打开笔记本，把周围的见闻记下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older person on the next bench leans over slightly, reading your page upside down with obvious curiosity.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上一位长者微微凑过来，倒着看你写的页面，显然很好奇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Making notes, eh? Good habit. Most people just stare at their phones out here.
beats.chinese: 在做记录啊？好习惯。大多数人在外面只会盯着手机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man with a scruffy brown dog passes by. Wren raises a hand and calls out politely.
beats.chinese: 一个遛着棕色杂毛狗的男人经过。温伦抬手礼貌地打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oi, Tom — is he friendly today? Mind if I say hello to Biscuit for a minute?
beats.chinese: 嘿，汤姆——他今天乖吗？我能跟饼干打个招呼吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that? You always ask first. Rule number one with other people's dogs.
beats.chinese: 看到了吗？一定要先问。碰别人的狗，这是第一条规矩。

choices.english: Watch how he greets the dog
choices.chinese: 看他怎么跟狗打招呼

choices.english: Ask about the notebook habit
choices.chinese: 问他记笔记的习惯

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner nods. Wren crouches and scratches the dog behind the ears, gentle and unhurried.
beats.chinese: 主人点头。温伦蹲下来轻轻挠狗的耳后，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good boy, eh. Bit of a limp on the left front, Tom. Getting any better?
beats.chinese: 真乖。左前腿有点瘸啊，汤姆。好点了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner says a few words, then tugs the lead. The dog trots off. Wren's hand drops at once and he stands, brushing off his knees.
beats.chinese: 主人说了几句，然后拉了拉狗绳。狗小跑着离开。温伦立刻收手，站起来拍拍膝盖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. Two minutes of Biscuit, and now he's gone. Perfect system.
beats.chinese: 好了。和饼干（Biscuit，狗的名字）待了两分钟，然后它就走了。完美的安排。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits back down on the bench, completely relaxed, and glances at your notebook again.
beats.chinese: 他坐回长椅，完全放松，又瞥了一眼你的笔记本。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't keep a dog of his own
choices.chinese: 问他为什么不自己养一只狗

choices.english: Ask if the owner ever urges him to adopt one
choices.chinese: 问主人会不会劝他领养

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask about the notebook. He taps the bench between you like it's obvious.
beats.chinese: 你问他记笔记的事。他敲了敲你们之间的长椅，好像答案很明显。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Write down what you actually saw, not what you think you saw. Same as my job. I fix smart door locks — half the job is writing down what the customer forgot to mention.
beats.chinese: 记下你真正看到的，不是你以为看到的。跟我的工作一样。我修智能门锁——一半的活儿是记下客户忘了说的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The dog and its owner circle back along the path. Wren watches them come, waiting until the owner slows down.
beats.chinese: 狗和主人沿小路绕回来。温伦看着他们走近，等主人放慢脚步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tom! Round again already? He walking you today, or are you walking him?
beats.chinese: 汤姆！又绕回来了？今天是他遛你，还是你遛他？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner laughs and lets the dog sniff toward the bench. Wren holds out two fingers for it to sniff.
beats.chinese: 主人笑了，让狗朝长椅这边嗅。温伦伸出两根手指让它闻。

choices.english: Ask if he knows that dog well
choices.chinese: 问他是不是认识那只狗

choices.english: Say you'd rather not touch the dog yourself
choices.chinese: 说自己不想摸狗

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask why he doesn't keep a dog of his own. His eyebrows go up, and his voice gets a notch shorter.
beats.chinese: 你问他为什么不自己养一只狗。他眉毛一挑，语气硬了一分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because caring for one is an every-day thing. Every day, rain or not, five in the morning or not. I like the visits. That's the whole arrangement.
beats.chinese: 因为养它就是每天的事。每天都要，下雨也要，早上五点也要。我喜欢的是这种拜访。安排就是这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't make it sad. It's not sad, it's Tuesday. I've got a quiet flat I'm fond of and a full night's sleep.
beats.chinese: 别把这弄得很伤感。不伤感，今天就是星期二。我有喜欢的安静公寓，还有整晚的好觉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods, mostly to himself, and watches Tom and Biscuit disappear around the hedge. He doesn't call after them.
beats.chinese: 他点点头，多半是对自己点的，看着汤姆和饼干消失在树篱后面。他没有喊他们。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing that down too, I bet. Go on then. 'Old fella refuses free dog.'
beats.chinese: 我猜你也要把这句记下来。写吧。'老头拒绝白送的狗。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether the owner ever urges him to take a dog home. He snorts, one short syllable of a laugh.
beats.chinese: 你问主人会不会劝他领养一只狗回家。他哼了一声，短促地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then someone does. Tom's sly about it — 'Biscuit's litter, you know.' I tell them straight: I like the visits, not the vet bills and the five a.m. walks.
beats.chinese: 偶尔有人劝。汤姆还会拐弯抹角——'饼干那一窝，你知道吧。'我就直说：我喜欢的是拜访，不是兽医账单和早上五点的遛狗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, easy, no edge in it. The bench is warm in the sun and he settles back like a man with nothing to defend.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，很轻松，没有火气。长椅被太阳晒得暖烘烘的，他往后一靠，像个没什么需要辩解的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They take the hint eventually. I'm not angry at them for asking — but I'm not carrying what they're offering either. That's the whole arrangement.
beats.chinese: 他们最后都能听懂。他们劝我不代表我生气——但他们塞过来的担子我也不接。安排就是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps your notebook once with a finger, meaning: write that down if you want.
beats.chinese: 他用手指点了点你的笔记本，意思是：愿意就记下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if he knows the dog well. He scratches the dog's ears while the owner stands chatting.
beats.chinese: 你问他是不是很认识那只狗。他一边挠狗耳朵，主人在旁边聊天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course I do. Biscuit's a regular. This whole park's full of my regulars — none of them pay me a cent.
beats.chinese: 当然认识。饼干是常客。整个公园都是我的常客——没一个付我钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner tugs the lead and they move off down the path. Wren stands, gives a small wave, and sits back down.
beats.chinese: 主人拉了拉狗绳，他们沿小路走远。温伦站起来，挥了挥手，又坐回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You were going to ask if I get sad when they walk off. Nah. A short hello done properly beats a long one done badly.
beats.chinese: 你刚才是不是想问他们走了我难不难过。不难受。好好打的短招呼，胜过打得糟糕的长招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks his pocket, pats it once, and pushes himself up from the bench.
beats.chinese: 他摸了摸口袋，拍了一下，从长椅上撑起身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off round the block. Enjoy your notes — and if you see a grey cat with a crooked ear, that's Margaret. Write that down.
beats.chinese: 好了，我要去绕街区了。好好写你的笔记——要是看到一只耳朵有缺口灰猫，那叫玛格丽特。把这个记下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd rather not touch the dog yourself. Wren shrugs like you've said something perfectly sensible.
beats.chinese: 你说你自己不想摸狗。温伦耸耸肩，好像你说得特别在理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good on you. Half the people out here grab at dogs like they're vending machines. He's not a snack dispenser, eh, Biscuit?
beats.chinese: 很好。外面一半的人抓狗就像抓自动售货机。他不是零食机，对吧，饼干？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't call the dog closer or hold it toward you. The dog sniffs the grass, unbothered, while the owner chats on.
beats.chinese: 他没有把狗叫近，也没有把它往你那边递。狗在草地上嗅来嗅去，毫不在意，主人在旁边继续聊天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Watching's a proper way to enjoy them too. Better, sometimes. You notice the limp, the ears, whether the owner looks wrecked.
beats.chinese: 看着也是一种正经的喜欢方式。有时候还更好。你能注意到瘸腿、耳朵，还有主人是不是累坏了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner says goodbye and leads the dog on. Wren lifts two fingers in a small salute and turns back to you.
beats.chinese: 主人道了别，牵着狗走了。温伦竖起两根手指小小致意，转回来看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. You've got your notes, I've got my walk. Good system, both of us.
beats.chinese: 好了。你有你的笔记，我有我的散步。咱俩的安排都挺好。

expectedContent.summaryZh: 七十一岁的温伦是奥克兰西区的智能门锁售后技师，独居却自在。他熟悉街坊每只猫狗，先问主人、摸两分钟就收手，坚决不养——喜欢短暂相处不等于想承担全天照料。有人劝他'带一只回家'时，他会干脆说明自己喜欢的是拜访不是饲养，语气轻松但不接对方塞来的担子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same bench. You open your notebook and start writing down what you see, and Wren is beside you, turning a small worn brass box over in his hands, clicking its latch open and shut.
beats.chinese: 你回到同一条长椅，打开笔记本开始记录周围的见闻。温伦就坐在旁边，手里转着一个磨旧的黄铜小盒，咔哒咔哒地开合搭扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Latch was sticking. Fixed it on the spot — no house call needed today, which suits me fine.
beats.chinese: 搭扣卡住了。当场就修好了——今天不用上门，正合我意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He snaps the box shut, drops it into his coat pocket, and gives you a short nod instead of a handshake.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子咔哒扣好，收进外套口袋，朝你短短点了下头，没有握手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back for more notes? Good. Biscuit came past earlier — I gave him the two fingers, said my line, kept my hands to myself. System held.
beats.chinese: 又来做记录了？好。饼干早些时候路过——我伸了两根手指，打了句招呼，手没乱碰。规矩守住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before the queue of dogs gets longer. Write something good, eh.
beats.chinese: 好了，趁狗的队伍还没变长我先走了。好好写点什么啊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off around the path at an easy pace, pocket clicking faintly with every step.
beats.chinese: 他迈着轻松的步子沿小路走去，口袋里的盒子随着脚步轻轻作响。

card.name: Wren Tualagi-Fahey
card.occupation: part-time after-sales technician for smart door locks
card.personality: Wren is a warm, brisk seventy-one-year-old who knows every dog and cat on the block by name and most of their quirks. He'll happily crouch down for a scratch and a chat with the owner, then stand up and go home to a quiet flat he genuinely enjoys. He's sociable without being needy, practical, a bit blunt when people project loneliness onto him. He likes short, uncomplicated contact — with animals, with neighbours, with most things. He can be impatient with sentimentality and with anyone treating his preferences as a puzzle to fix.
card.background: Wren grew up in West Auckland in a big, noisy family, and after decades of full houses — flatmates, kids, a partner, various animals that came with all of them — he lives alone now and finds it restful rather than empty. He works part-time fixing smart door locks, which suits him: turn up, sort the problem, chat briefly, leave. The neighbourhood dogs know him because he stops, every time, and their owners know him as the man who asks the right questions about a limp or a fussy appetite. When someone suggests he take one home for company, he gets short: he likes the visits, not the vet bills, the 5 a.m. walks, the whole weight of it. He's firm that this isn't sadness. It's just what he wants, and he's had enough decades to know the difference.
hobbies: Neighbourhood pet visits (with owners' permission)
Fixing and tinkering with small mechanisms
Short evening walks around the block
card.speechStyle: Short, dry, warm underneath; asks practical questions, cuts through fuss, laughs in single syllables.
card.signature: 'Nah, I'm right — but he's a good boy, eh.'

values: Honest affection without obligation
Respecting other people's animals and rules
flaws: Impatient when people psychoanalyse him
Can shut a conversation down too abruptly
boundaries: Won't take a pet home, full stop
Won't play with an animal without the owner's okay
conversationalHabits: Opens with the animal, not the person
Deflects concern with dry humour
anchorLines: Nah, I'm right — but he's a good boy, eh.
I like the visits. That's the whole arrangement.
Don't make it sad. It's not sad, it's Tuesday.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on a park bench. Nearby, an older person raises a hand to a passer-by with a scruffy brown dog.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上打开笔记本。附近一位长者朝牵着棕色杂毛狗的路人抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello, Tom. Is Biscuit in the mood for a scratch today?
beats.chinese: 你好，汤姆。饼干今天愿意让人挠挠吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner nods and pauses. Wren crouches, lets the dog approach and gently scratches behind its ears. When Tom moves on, Wren drops his hand straight away.
beats.chinese: 主人点头停下。温伦蹲下来，等狗靠近后，轻轻挠了挠它耳后。汤姆继续走时，温伦立刻收回手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two minutes of Biscuit. Lovely. People see me doing that and think I must want a dog. I don't, actually.
beats.chinese: 和饼干待两分钟，真不错。人家看我这样，就以为我一定想养只狗。其实我不想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Wren sits at the other end of the bench, leaving your notebook plenty of room. The dog and its owner continue down the path.
beats.chinese: 温伦在长椅另一端坐下，给你的笔记本留出足够的地方。狗和主人继续沿小路往前走。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't want a dog of his own.
choices.chinese: 问为什么不自己养一只狗。

choices.english: Ask whether he knows that dog.
choices.chinese: 问是不是认识那只狗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because looking after one is every day. The walks, the company, the vet. I enjoy saying hello. That isn't the same offer.
beats.chinese: 因为照顾它是每天的事。遛狗、陪伴、看兽医。我喜欢打个招呼。这跟愿意养它不是一回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His answer comes out a little sharper than before. He rubs a loose thread on his coat cuff, then looks back at you.
beats.chinese: 这句回答比刚才硬了一点。他捻了捻袖口的一根线头，又看向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing against people who do it. Tom loves the whole business. I like going home to my quiet flat and leaving things exactly where I put them.
beats.chinese: 我没觉得养狗的人有什么不好。汤姆就喜欢这一整套。我喜欢回到自己安静的公寓，东西都还待在我放下的位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances along the path. Biscuit stops to investigate a tuft of grass, and Tom waits.
beats.chinese: 他朝小路上看去。饼干停下来研究一丛草，汤姆在旁边等着。

choices.english: Say enjoying dogs and keeping one are different things.
choices.chinese: 表示喜欢狗和养狗是两回事。

choices.english: Ask whether anyone tries to persuade him to adopt.
choices.chinese: 问有没有人劝他领养。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Biscuit, yes. I see those two around here. Tom used to stop while I was on my way to a lock repair, and Biscuit inspected the tool bag.
beats.chinese: 认识饼干。经常在这儿看到他们俩。以前我出门修锁时，汤姆会停下来聊两句，饼干就检查我的工具包。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the coat pocket where a small brass puzzle box makes a faint click.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍外套口袋，里面一个黄铜小机关盒轻轻响了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still ask each time. Sometimes Tom's in a hurry, sometimes the dog's not interested. Being familiar doesn't reserve me a turn.
beats.chinese: 不过每次还是会问。有时汤姆赶时间，有时狗没兴趣。认识不代表就给我留着摸它的份儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pair are farther down the path now. Wren stays seated rather than calling them back.
beats.chinese: 一人一狗已经沿小路走远。温伦仍坐着，没有把他喊回来。

choices.english: Ask whether he misses the dog when it leaves.
choices.chinese: 问狗走了会不会舍不得。

choices.english: Say you would rather not touch a dog yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己不想摸狗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At that distinction, his shoulders loosen. He nods once, looking pleased not to have another case to argue.
beats.chinese: 听到这个区别，他肩膀放松下来，点了点头，很高兴不用再争辩一场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. I like watching the cricket, too. Nobody hands me a bat and says the team is my responsibility now.
beats.chinese: 就是。我也喜欢看板球，可没人因此塞给我一根球棒，说现在这支队归我负责。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Tom and Biscuit disappear around the hedge. Wren follows them with his eyes, then settles back.
beats.chinese: 汤姆和饼干消失在树篱后。温伦目送他，随后靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was a good little visit. I'm quite happy for it to have been little.
beats.chinese: 刚才那一小会儿挺好。就只有一小会儿，我也很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then. Someone offered to introduce me to a rescue dog last month. A very nice offer, but I said no before they arranged anything.
beats.chinese: 偶尔。上个月有人想带我认识一只待领养的狗。好意是好意，但我在他们安排之前就说不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens the loose cuff thread with a thumbnail and gives a small shrug.
beats.chinese: 他用指甲把袖口线头压平，轻轻耸了耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said I enjoyed their dog's company and wasn't looking for my own. They looked disappointed. I can live with that; I couldn't promise a dog a different life.
beats.chinese: 我说我喜欢跟他们的狗待着，可没在找自己的狗。他们有点失望。这我能接受，但我不能给一只狗许下另一种生活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His voice eases again. He watches a cyclist pass, giving the subject a moment to settle.
beats.chinese: 他语气又松下来，看着一辆自行车经过，让话题慢慢落定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They're still talking to me, by the way. We managed that much.
beats.chinese: 对了，他们现在还跟我说话呢。至少这点我们处理好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not sad, no. I enjoyed the hello. I don't need to stretch it until one of us gets fed up.
beats.chinese: 不难过。刚才打招呼我已经挺高兴。不必非延长到谁先不耐烦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the brass box from his pocket, checks that its little sliding panel is closed and puts it away again.
beats.chinese: 他从口袋里掏出黄铜盒，确认小滑板关好了，又收回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Besides, I've got a walk to finish. Biscuit isn't the only one who needs to get round the park.
beats.chinese: 而且我自己的散步还没走完呢。又不是只有饼干需要绕公园走一圈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Wren rises, checks the bench for anything left behind and gives you a brief wave before setting off along the path.
beats.chinese: 温伦站起来，检查长椅上有没有落下东西，朝你简短挥了挥手，沿小路走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. I'll remember that if we see him again. You don't owe Biscuit a greeting either.
beats.chinese: 那很正常。下次碰到它我会记着的。你也不欠饼干一个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't call the dog back or suggest that you might change your mind. His hand rests on his own coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 他没有把狗叫回来，也没暗示你可能会改变主意，手安稳地放在自己的外套口袋上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People do love turning a preference into a project. I spend enough time getting stubborn locks to cooperate. People can make their own arrangements.
beats.chinese: 人们真爱把别人的喜好当成一项改造工程。我对付不听话的门锁就花够时间了。人还是自己安排自己吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A leaf lands near the notebook. Wren shifts his shoe out of the way, leaving it where you can see it.
beats.chinese: 一片叶子落在笔记本附近。温伦把鞋挪开，让它留在你看得见的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've got your notes; I've got my walk. That works nicely.
beats.chinese: 你有你的笔记，我有我的散步。这样挺好。

beats.chinese: 他迈着轻松的步子沿小路走去，口袋里的盒子随着脚步轻轻作响。

card.name: Wren Tualagi-Fahey
card.occupation: part-time after-sales technician for smart door locks
card.personality: Wren is a warm, brisk seventy-one-year-old who knows every dog and cat on the block by name and most of their quirks. He'll happily crouch down for a scratch and a chat with the owner, then stand up and go home to a quiet flat he genuinely enjoys. He's sociable without being needy, practical, a bit blunt when people project loneliness onto him. He likes short, uncomplicated contact — with animals, with neighbours, with most things. He can be impatient with sentimentality and with anyone treating his preferences as a puzzle to fix.
card.background: Wren grew up in West Auckland in a big, noisy family, and after decades of full houses — flatmates, kids, a partner, various animals that came with all of them — he lives alone now and finds it restful rather than empty. He works part-time fixing smart door locks, which suits him: turn up, sort the problem, chat briefly, leave. The neighbourhood dogs know him because he stops, every time, and their owners know him as the man who asks the right questions about a limp or a fussy appetite. When someone suggests he take one home for company, he gets short: he likes the visits, not the vet bills, the 5 a.m. walks, the whole weight of it. He's firm that this isn't sadness. It's just what he wants, and he's had enough decades to know the difference.
hobbies: Neighbourhood pet visits (with owners' permission)
Fixing and tinkering with small mechanisms
Short evening walks around the block
card.speechStyle: Short, dry, warm underneath; asks practical questions, cuts through fuss, laughs in single syllables.
card.signature: 'Nah, I'm right — but he's a good boy, eh.'
